title: Berlin: Rigaer94 verteidigen gegen Räumung 15.12.
content:
Wie wir letztes Jahr berichtet haben, sind die zwischen den alten Mietvertragsinhaber*innen und den selbsternannten Anwälten Bernau und Aretin des angeblichen Eigentümers (Leonid Medved) zwar nicht formell, aber faktisch, Räumungstitel. Diese kommen zu den zwei bereits aus den letzten Jahren existierenden Räumungstiteln hinzu, was bedeutet das es jetzt insgesamt acht Räumungstitel im Haus gibt. In den letzten Monaten haben unsere Gegner einige Räumungsklagen zurückgezogen, die für sie aussichtslos wirkten. Obwohl dadurch einige Individuen aus den Räumungsklagen raus sind, sind das für uns keine guten Neuigkeiten – vielmehr macht es ein Räumungsszenario wahrscheinlicher, da es bald keine offenen Klagen, sondern nur noch Räumungstitel geben wird.


Es ist mal wieder ernst. Noch diesen Sommer haben wir davon berichtet, dass einige Räumungstitel gegen Wohnungen in unserem Haus bestehen: (

here

)


Letzte Woche Mittwoch, am 11. November, gab es wieder einen Verhandlungstermin zu diesen Räumungsklagen. In der Verhandlung machte der Richter erneut deutlich, dass er keineswegs plant, die Lafone Investments Limited als rechtsfähig anzuerkennen. Noch während der Verhandlung zogen die Anwälte des vermeintlichen Eigentümers dann auch die letzten aussichtslosen Klagen gegen diejenigen Individuen zurück, die nicht in Verbindung mit Mietverträgen stehen. Das scheint ihre aktuelle Strategie zu sein: Den Weg für eine Teilräumung zu ebnen. Und heute sehen wir auch, was genau das bedeutet:


Innerhalb der letzten Tage haben wir vier Räumungsankündigungen erhalten. Drei davon resultieren aus den Deals der alten Mietvertragsinhaber*innen mit den selbsternannten Anwälten. Eine der Räumungsankündigungen basiert auf einem bereits länger existierenden Räumungstitel. Bisher wissen wir also sicher, dass es vier Wohnungen betrifft. Wir müssen aber davon ausgehen, dass zu den vier weiteren Wohnungen auch noch Räumungsankündigungen eintreffen werden.


Die Obergerichtsvollzieherin Frau Knop (Segelfliegerdamm 89 12487 Berlin, Tel.03091693556) hat sich für den 15.12.26 um 06:00 Uhr morgens

 angekündigt, um die ehemaligen Mietvertragsinhaber*innen aus den Wohnungen zu räumen und die vermeintlichen Eigentümer*innen in diese “einzuweisen”.


Was treiben die Behörden da?


Wir fragen uns, ob die Ankündigung der Gerichtsvollzieherin eine rein bürokratische Angelegenheit ist, oder ob Bullen und Politik von Anfang an ihre Finger mit im Spiel haben. Es könnte ja sein, dass Frau Knop mal einen Brief losgeschickt hat, weil es einfach der übliche Verwaltungsweg ist.- ohne sich der Konsequenzen bewusst zu sein. Oder saß sie bereits mit Bernau, Aretin, einem „Eigentümer“, den Bullen und dem Innensenat an einem Tisch? Wissen dann die Hundertschaften schon Bescheid, dass sie sich auf Überstunden und Kürzungen von Urlaubstagen kurz vor Weihnachten und Silvester einstellen müssen? Oder machen die das gerne ehrenamtlich?


Falls es so ist, dass Politiker:innen bereits Bescheid wissen: Kurz vorm Sommer schien es wahrscheinlicher (

All out for the defence of Rigaer94

), dass ein Angriff gegen unser Haus dem CDU-geführten Senat im Berliner Wahlkampf attraktiv erschien. Die CDU hätte ihr Wahlversprechen einhalten können und sich zusammen mit Innensenatorin Iris Spranger (SPD) als Hardliner gegen links verkaufen können. Ist es jetzt der letzte Versuch einer abgewählten Regierung dem neuen Senat zu schaden bzw. ihn zu zwingen, eine Räumung zu Ende zu führen, die allen Wahlversprechen der LINKEn entgegen steht? Oder ist es der konfrontative Kurs im Kampf gegen eine Bewegung von unten, der mehr und mehr auf der Tagesordnung steht und auf den sich alle Parteien einigen können? (

Andreas Geisel

, ehemaliger Innensenator,

Juni 2021

). Auf rechtlicher Ebene hat sich seitdem nicht viel verändert.


Diese Fragen sind dringend. Sie zu beantworten überlassen wir anderen.


Für uns ist auf dieser Ebene aber klar, dass ein nicht legitimierter „Eigentümer“


 aufgrund eines daher unrechtmäßigen Deals mit Leuten,

 die eigentlich keinen Deal abschließen dürfen, weil sie

 weder im Besitz der Wohnungen sind,

 noch die Miete zahlen, die monatlich anfällt


kein Recht besitzt, eine Gerichtsvollzieherin zu beauftragen, die tatsächlichen Bewohner:innen dieser Wohnungen rauszuschmeißen.


Es ist eine bitterkalte Zeit…


Der Rausschmiss aus dem eigenem Zuhause ist die Realität vieler Menschen. Auch mitten im Winter. Weil die Miete unbezahlbar ist, weil es für Arbeit nur Brotkrumen …

content:
Arts et politiques de la désertion, de la Première Guerre mondiale à nos jours

, c'est le dernier livre publié par les éditions lundimatin et c'est un travail aussi magistral que d'actualité. Rencontre et discussion avec son auteur Luca Salza. Comment déserter, avec armes et bagages.


La fin de la guerre froide promettait une ère de paix mais revoilà la guerre. Les États se renforcent et se réarment, les fronts se répandent, le droit international part en miettes et les vies, par milliers, sont pulvérisées. Dans l'instant du danger,

Arts et politiques de la désertion

 explore les luttes et les innovations politiques comme artistiques qui n'ont pas seulement contesté pacifiquement la guerre mais l'ont attaquée de front.


On y croise André Breton et Franz Kafka, Rosa Luxemburg et Virginia Woolf, Victor Serge et Simone Weil, Arthur Cravan, Charlie Chaplin et bien d'autres.


On y découvre l'internationalisme ouvrier qui décide de retourner les armes, les artistes et les poètes qui rompent les rangs, le féminisme de la différence qui

préfère ne pas

. Dans les rues de Petrograd insurgées comme dans les tavernes zurichoises, chuchoté sous les bombardements ou dispersé sur les champs de bataille, le mot d'ordre « Guerre à la guerre ! » synthétise les énergies explosives et occultes qui ont refusé de laisser la guerre en paix.


Une étude littéraire, historique et contemporaine de la désertion comme une contre-histoire du monde et de la guerre.


Luca Salza

 est Professeur des Universités. Ses recherches portent sur la fin du monde et ses bifurcations possibles.

author: anonerror
title: LOS AMIGOS DE DURRUTI (1937-1939)  Historia, revolución y crítica del colaboracionismo libertario. Presentación de Guillamón en Atenas — 28 de noviembre de 2026.
content:
LOS AMIGOS DE DURRUTI (1937-1939)


Historia, revolución y crítica del colaboracionismo libertario.

Presentación en Atenas — 28 de noviembre de 2026.


Compañeros: Quiero comenzar agradeciendo la publicación de la traducción griega de mi libro sobre Los Amigos de Durruti y la posibilidad de presentarlo en Atenas. La traducción de una obra histórica no consiste únicamente en trasladar unas palabras de una lengua a otra. También permite poner en circulación experiencias, debates y problemas políticos que pertenecen a una historia común del movimiento obrero internacional.


El libro que presentamos hoy trata de una organización relativamente pequeña, que desarrolló su actividad durante un período muy breve, entre 1937 y 1939. Sin embargo, su importancia histórica no guarda proporción con su dimensión organizativa ni con la duración de su existencia.


Los Amigos de Durruti plantearon algunos de los problemas fundamentales de cualquier proceso revolucionario: la relación entre revolución y guerra, entre organización y autonomía obrera, entre los principios y la práctica política, entre la destrucción del Estado y la construcción de nuevas instituciones sociales.


Por eso este libro no pretende ser solamente una investigación sobre un episodio de la Guerra Civil española. Su propósito es también contribuir a la teoría revolucionaria mediante el estudio de una experiencia histórica concreta.


Hay una convicción que recorre todo el trabajo:

sin la teorización de las experiencias históricas del proletariado revolucionario no puede existir una teoría revolucionaria.

Y sin teoría revolucionaria, la acción colectiva corre el riesgo de quedar subordinada a las circunstancias inmediatas, a las necesidades de la guerra o a las decisiones de quienes terminan administrando las organizaciones obreras.


La historia de Los Amigos de Durruti permite examinar precisamente ese problema.


1. Julio de 1936: una revolución que no destruyó el Estado


Para comprender el nacimiento de Los Amigos de Durruti debemos regresar al 19 de julio de 1936. El levantamiento militar y fascista contra la República fue derrotado en Barcelona gracias, fundamentalmente, a la resistencia armada de los trabajadores. Las fuerzas obreras, y muy especialmente los COMITÉS DE DEFENSA DE LA CNT, protagonizaron la insurrección que impidió el triunfo de los militares en Cataluña.


Pero lo que ocurrió entonces fue mucho más que una victoria militar.


Los trabajadores expropiaron sistemáticamente fábricas, talleres y empresas. Se incautaron de edificios y medios de transporte. Organizaron colectividades, comités revolucionarios de barrio (o locales), comités de abastos y organismos de control obrero. En numerosos pueblos y ciudades catalanes, los comités revolucionarios asumieron funciones que anteriormente ejercía el Estado.


Los trabajadores, gracias a setenta años de pedagogía libertaria, se organizaron desde abajo y resolvieron problemas concretos de producción, distribución, abastecimiento, transporte y defensa.


La revolución era una realidad que se desarrollaba cotidianamente en las calles, las fábricas y los pueblos, impulsada por los comités revolucionarios.


Y aquí aparece la primera gran contradicción de la revolución española.


La cúpula de la organización que había encabezado la insurrección obrera, la CNT, renunció a destruir el aparato estatal republicano y optó por colaborar en su reconstrucción.


El 21 de julio de 1936 se constituyó el Comité Central de Milicias Antifascistas (CCMA). En él participaron representantes de la CNT, la FAI, el POUM, la UGT, el PSUC, los partidos republicanos y el gobierno de la Generalidad de Cataluña.


Entre los líderes de la CNT se impuso la ideología de unidad antifascista como único medio de ganar la guerra al fascismo.


Pero esa unidad tenía un precio muy elevado: la renuncia a los propios principios.


La Agrupación de los Amigos de Durruti definiría posteriormente el CCMA como un

organismo de colaboración de clases.

 No lo consideraba un órgano de poder revolucionario, sino una estructura que permitía a la burguesía republicana conservar y fortalecer el Estado.


Esta interpretación es fundamental para comprender el libro.


El problema no consistía simplemente en que los anarquistas hubieran entrado en una institución gubernamental. El problema era mucho más profundo:

la colaboración antifascista había sustituido al programa revolucionario

.


La lucha contra el fascismo justificó la renuncia a …

author: Freedom Editor
title: Court halts sanctions against Autistici/Inventati
content:
Italian tech collective was de-banked following “terrorism” designation by the Trump regime

An important ruling against financial overreach: United States anti-terrorism lists do not have automatic legal effect in Italy. The judge has ordered the immediate unblocking of an account, reaffirming the limits on the power of banks.

This significant decision extends well beyond the specific case of Autistici/Inventati, establishing a concrete limit on the United States’ attempt to extend its own sanctions globally. In an order dated 20 November, the Court of Pisa granted an urgent appeal filed by the association Autistici/Inventati (AI ODV) against Banca Popolare Etica, ordering the immediate restoration of full access to the association’s current account and the funds held within it. The bank was also ordered to pay the legal costs.

The ruling, signed by Judge Teresa Guerrieri, addresses a situation that began on August 26, when the U.S. Department of the Treasury—through the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC)—placed Autistici/Inventati on a list of entities subject to anti-terrorism sanctions. A few days later, on 1 September, Banca Etica informed the association of a “temporary limitation on account operations,” effectively rendering the funds in the account inaccessible. The bank justified this action by citing the need to assess the client’s updated risk profile and the potential implications of the American sanctions.

The Court of Pisa rejected this position, establishing a fundamental principle: inclusion on an OFAC list does not automatically trigger an obligation to freeze funds under the Italian legal system. Any asset-freezing measures must be grounded in national or European Union law, rather than merely in the decision of a foreign administrative authority. An American designation may be a factor to consider in risk assessment and anti-money laundering (AML) due diligence obligations; however, it does not authorise a bank to render a client’s entire account inaccessible—on a general basis and for an indefinite period.

This point is particularly significant because the judge draws a clear distinction between the monitoring obligations of financial intermediaries and the power to impose actual restrictive measures. While AML regulations allow for enhanced due diligence and, in certain circumstances, the refusal to execute specific transactions, they do not grant banks an independent, broad-reaching power to freeze assets. In the case of A/I, Banca Etica failed to identify any binding Italian or European legal instrument—or any contractual provision—that could justify a total block on the client’s funds.

Even more relevant is the reasoning regarding so-called “secondary sanctions,” through which Washington exerts pressure on non-U.S. economic entities. The court acknowledges that U.S. sanctions can have tangible economic consequences for European intermediaries, but clarifies that this risk does not equate to an automatic recognition of their legal validity within the Italian legal system. Citing the case law of the Court of Justice of the European Union, the judge underscores the necessity of distinguishing between the economic impact of extraterritorial measures and their legal legitimacy in Europe.

This is precisely the political crux of the matter that we have highlighted since the beginning of this case. The power of US sanctions lies not merely in the measures adopted in Washington, but in their capacity to influence the decisions of banks, platforms, and service providers in other countries. The fear of economic repercussions drives these intermediaries to act as enforcers of foreign decisions, even in the absence of any domestic legal obligation requiring them to do so. The result is a form of economic repression in which exclusion from essential services can precede any judicial determination.

The Court of Pisa addresses this very mechanism, asserting that banking prudence cannot devolve into an arbitrary power to suspend contractual rights. The ruling further acknowledges the disproportionate nature of the freeze: rendering the association’s only account inaccessible effectively prevented it from fulfilling its obligations and carrying out its normal activities—all without any specific justification being provided for opting for a blanket restriction rather than scrutinising individual transactions.

Naturally, this court order does not overturn the OFAC designation, nor does it constitute …

author: Unknown
title: IHD releases report on violence and suspicious deaths
content:
The Women's Commission of the Amed (Diyarbakır) Branch of the Human Rights Association (IHD) released its report on violence and suspicious deaths in Kurdistan between 25 November 2025 and 25 November 2026 to mark the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. Commission members Berfin Elçi and Eylem Kaya attended the press statement held at the association's premises.


Berfin Elçi said that the records compiled since 25 November 2025 showed that women faced severe violence in their homes, on the streets and in public life. Elçi said that 44 women lost their lives as a result of violence within families and intimate relationships, while nine women lost their lives as a result of violence in the social sphere during this period. She added that 63 suspicious deaths had also been recorded. Berfin Elçi said that the total number of deaths documented in the detailed records was 116 and added: "Effective investigations must establish the circumstances surrounding suspicious deaths and determine whether anyone bears responsibility."


Berfin Elçi listed their demands as follows:


- Law No. 6284 must be effectively implemented, women's applications for protection must be processed without delay, and the implementation of protection orders must be regularly monitored.


- Turkey must rejoin the Istanbul Convention, and the safeguards provided by the Convention for combating violence must be effectively implemented.


- Comprehensive and effective investigations must be conducted into women's deaths and allegations of sexual violence, the responsibility of public officials must be investigated, and impunity must be ended.


- Women's access to safe accommodation, legal assistance, healthcare services and economic support must be ensured. Opportunities to submit applications in their mother tongue and access interpretation services must be provided and expanded.


- The activities of women's organizations and journalistic work that exposes violence must not be obstructed, and women's right to organize must be protected.


- Women's effective participation in building peace and determining policies to combat violence must be ensured.


Elçi said: "On the occasion of 25 November, we call on all institutions to fulfill their obligations and on society to stand in solidarity with women's struggle for equality and freedom."

author: Corey Larocque
title: Mounties took too long to get their man, judge says
content:
Two sex charges against an Iqaluit man will not proceed because the RCMP took more than four years after the charges were laid to arrest their suspect.


A 14-year-old girl had reported to police in August 2020 that Isaac Strickland has sexually assaulted her multiple times over a period of one year.


She was 13 and he was 19 the first time she was allegedly sexually assaulted, said Justice Mark Mossey in a decision handed down Wednesday. A court-ordered ban prevents the identification of the girl.


Strickland was charged Dec. 7, 2020, with one count of sexual assault and and one count of sexual interference, and RCMP obtained a warrant for his arrest.


But Strickland wasn’t arrested until Jan. 8, 2025, more than four years later, after the complainant told police where to find him.


Mossey called it a “troubling case” in a decision he gave Wednesday in response to an application from Strickland’s lawyer to have the charges stayed.


“The RCMP’s failure to act with reasonable diligence, or to act at all for almost 50 months … will necessarily result in serious allegations of sexual abuse against a child being unable to be tested at trial,” Mossey wrote in his decision.


“Mr. Strickland would not have been difficult to find, had the RCMP taken any steps, at all, to locate him.”


Strickland has a Charter-protected right to be tried within a reasonable amount of time from when charges are laid, said Mossey in his decision. The Supreme Court has established that amount of time should be 30 months.


Curtis Mesher, Strickland’s lawyer, declined to comment on the case, saying his client had not given him instructions about talking to the media.


In the summer of 2020 Strickland was living in Iqaluit with his parents.


That September, RCMP looked for him at the Frobisher Inn, where he was a security guard. But a manager told police Strickland had moved to Ottawa.


That led police to Algonquin College, where they were told he was a student. It turned out he was not at the college but was enrolled at Nunavut Sivuniksavut instead.


Police looked for him at an address they were given not far from Nunavut Sivuniksavut. But they had the wrong address. He was actually living in an apartment next door.


In April 2021, Strickland took a job at Inuuqatigiit Centre for Inuit Children, Youth and Families in Ottawa that required him to get a criminal record check. As part of this process, Strickland gave his address to police, said Mossey.


“The [criminal record check] came back clean, and at no point was Mr. Strickland told by police that he had outstanding criminal charges,” said Mossey in his decision.


In October 2023, Strickland moved to Pangnirtung for a job with Innguaq Association, and in 2024 took a job with the hamlet.


By November 2024, Strickland was back in Iqaluit working at Atiigo Media and staying in staff housing. He was arrested on Jan. 8, 2025, after the complainant led police to him.


In the four years his arrest warrant was active, Strickland filed tax returns and got a Nunavut driver’s licence among other government-issued identification, Mossey said, referring to an affidavit Strickland filed as part of his application to have the charges stayed.


Strickland’s mother is a retired assistant deputy minister of Public Safety in Nunavut, he said in his affidavit, and was “regularly in contact with RCMP and other Justice stakeholders throughout her employment.”


In August 2020, around the time the complaint was made, Strickland was living with the son of an RCMP officer for a two-week period before going to Nunavut Sinuviksavut.


He was also highly visible on various social media platforms.


“On many of the platforms, where he posted under his own name, Mr. Strickland’s location was listed during livestreams,” Mossey said.


Crown lawyer Jennifer Althot-Savoie argued the delay was “an exceptional circumstance” that should have stopped the 30-month clock from ticking.


But the judge said exceptional circumstances are outside the Crown’s control because they are unforeseen and cannot be remedied.


“Mr. Strickland’s case is not such an instance,” Mossey wrote, adding none of the delays in arresting him were attributable to Strickland.


The Public Prosecution Service of Canada does not comment on judicial decisions, a spokesperson said by email on Thursday, but noted the service has a 30-day window to file an appeal in Nunavut.


The spokesperson for the Nunavut RCMP could not be reached for comment …

author: Daniel Avalos
title: 25N: Las familias, las ausencias y una lucha que sigue en las calles
content:
Foto: Dani Avalos, para ANRed.


Desde Tribunales hasta Plaza Congreso, organizaciones feministas, sociales, gremiales, sectores de izquierda y familiares de víctimas de femicidio marcharon en el Día Internacional de la Eliminación de la Violencia contra las Mujeres. Justicia, memoria, reclamos económicos y una pregunta que sigue sin respuesta: «¿Dónde está Tehuel?».

 Texto y fotos: Dani Avalos, para ANRed.


La marcha avanzó desde Tribunales hasta Plaza Congreso. Entre banderas, carteles y cantos, distintas organizaciones volvieron a encontrarse en las calles para poner en común sus reclamos frente a las violencias que atraviesan la vida de las mujeres.


Foto: Dani Avalos, para ANRed.


La dimensión del problema también aparece en las estadísticas. Según el Observatorio de las Violencias de Género Ahora Que Sí Nos Ven, entre el 1 de enero y el 20 de noviembre de 2026 se registraron 273 víctimas letales de violencia de género en Argentina. El relevamiento incluye 222 femicidios directos, 32 femicidios vinculados, nueve travesticidios y transfemicidios y diez instigaciones al suicidio. Son vidas que faltan y familias que deben enfrentar las consecuencias de una violencia que no deja de repetirse.


Participaron el colectivo Ni Una Menos, organizaciones sociales, gremios y agrupaciones feministas y de izquierda, entre ellas Pan y Rosas y Las Rojas. También estuvieron familiares de víctimas de femicidio. Y fueron ellos quienes dejaron algunas de las imágenes más fuertes de la jornada.


Madres, padres, hermanas, niños y niñas acompañaban las fotografías de las mujeres asesinadas. Rostros que se hacían presentes en medio de la movilización, junto a familias que siguen reclamando justicia. La entereza con la que sostenían esos reclamos fue una de las cosas que más llamó la atención. No estaban solos: alrededor había otras familias, organizaciones y personas que acompañaban sus demandas.


Foto: Dani Avalos, para ANRed.


Las caras de los femicidas se vieron en folletos y carteles. Una manera de ponerles rostro a quienes cometieron los crímenes y de insistir en que detrás de cada femicidio hay una historia que no puede quedar reducida a una estadística.


Las consignas fueron dando cuenta de la amplitud de los reclamos. «Justicia por los femicidios» volvió a escucharse a lo largo de la marcha. «Endeudarse también es violencia» incorporó la dimensión económica a una discusión que no puede limitarse a las agresiones físicas. La precariedad y las dificultades para sostener la vida también forman parte de las desigualdades que atraviesan a las mujeres.


Y una pregunta volvió a recorrer la movilización: «¿Dónde está Tehuel?». Una consigna que mantiene vigente el reclamo por su aparición.


La marcha tuvo distintos protagonistas y reclamos, pero también un punto de encuentro: la decisión de seguir organizándose. Los familiares de las víctimas, las organizaciones feministas, los gremios y los movimientos sociales compartieron la calle en una jornada donde el acompañamiento y la unidad tuvieron una presencia concreta.


«Ahora que sí nos ven», cantaban.


Foto: Dani Avalos, para ANRed.
sourceTags: Día Internacional de la Eliminación de la Violencia contra las Mujeres

author: Harriet Williamson
title: Met Police Still Racist, Misogynistic, Homophobic, Investigation Finds
content:
The Metropolitan police is still institutionally racist, misogynistic and homophobic, a new investigation has found three years after the damning Casey review.


The

new 389-page report

by Dr Gillian Fairfield, commissioned by London mayor Sadiq Khan and published on Wednesday, states: “The Casey review found the Met was institutionally racist, misogynistic and homophobic. 


“Our role has been to assess the Met’s progress in addressing this; we judge these fundamental, systemic issues remain.”


Out of the 14 recommendations made by Baroness Lousie Casey

in 2023

 after a serving Met officer kidnapped, raped and murdered Sarah Everard, Farfield’s investigation found that the force had not made good progress on any of them. 


The new report raises serious concerns about the treatment of bereaved families when the Met carries out investigations into murders and deaths, and about “predatory behaviour” from some senior officers towards younger women.


The fact survivors have reported domestic abuse by police officers is evidence of “an organisation perpetuating additional harm, not preventing it”, it added.


Fairfield said the Met “struggles to acknowledge racism” and “if it can’t name it, it can’t face it. If it can’t face it, it can’t sort it out.”


The report highlights bereaved families who accuse the force of gaslighting, victim-blaming and lying to them about important aspects of investigations into the deaths of their loved ones.


Khan said he was “appalled by the treatment of some of the victims highlighted in this review”. 


The mayor has also called on Met commissioner Mark Rowley to “reset his relationship with those of us tasked with holding the Met to account” and “provide Londoners with the police service they deserve” in response to Fairfield’s findings. 


Rowley said he accepted the review’s findings. 


The Green party’s London policing lead Benali Hamdache called for the Met to be broken up and replaced with smaller, local forces that are “more democratic and accountable to the communities they serve”.


Hamdache said: “The Met does not operate in a vacuum, and politicians must take responsibility. Rather than challenging police brutality and the disproportionate policing of marginalised communities, too many have politicised these issues and undermined efforts to hold the Met to account.”

Ενός συστήματος εξουσίας όπου οι γυναικοκτονίες, οι βιασμοί, οι παιδοβιασμοί και τα κυκλώματα τράφικινγκ προωθούνται και συγκαλύπτονται από τους κρατικούς θεσμούς και την αστυνομία. Του ίδιου συστήματος εξουσίας, όπου

προσφύγισσες και μετανάστριες εξευτελίζονται και κακοποιούνται στα σύνορα και στα στρατόπεδα συγκέντρωσης και δολοφονούνται στα κέντρα των πόλεων, όπου οι διακρίσεις και οι επιθέσεις σε άτομα της ΛΟΑΤΚΙ+ κοινότητας διαρκώς πληθαίνουν, όπου οι φτωχές και οι εργάτριες βρίσκονται αντιμέτωπες με παρενοχλήσεις, απολύονται λόγω εγκυμοσύνης, δολοφονούνται στα κάτεργα της μισθωτής σκλαβιάς, όπως αυτό της “Βιολάντα” στα Τρίκαλα, ενώ ταυτόχρονα οι αντικοινωνικές αναδιαρθρώσεις σε κάθε πεδίο της καθημερινότητας οξύνουν τις συνθήκες εκμετάλλευσης και καταπίεσης. Ταυτόχρονα η έμφυλη βία σε συνθήκες πολέμου και γενοκτονίας αποτελεί όπλο καθυπόταξης, όπως επίσης μέσο τρομοκράτησης και καταστολής των αγωνιζόμενων και εξεγερμένων από τα σώματα ασφαλείας. Οι θεσμικές επέτειοι και οι υποκριτικές διακηρύξεις δεν είναι παρά το προσωπείο αυτού ακριβώς του συστήματος, το οποίο γεννά, θρέφει και συγκαλύπτει την έμφυλη βία.


Η χειραφέτηση δεν θα έρθει από τους καταπιεστικούς θεσμούς των κυρίαρχων, που στόχο έχουν την υποταγή, την εκμετάλλευση και τον κατακερματισμό των καταπιεσμένων. Θα κατακτηθεί στους δρόμους, στους χώρους δουλειάς και στις γειτονιές, μέσα από την αυτοοργάνωση, την αλληλεγγύη και τον αγώνα. Στεκόμαστε στο πλευρό των εξεγερμένων γυναικών σε κάθε γωνιά του πλανήτη: στην Παλαιστίνη, στο Σουδάν, στο Ιράν, στο Μεξικό και παντού όπου οι καταπιεσμένες αγωνίζονται για ζωή, γη και ελευθερία. Στεκόμαστε δίπλα στις εργάτριες, στις μετανάστριες και προσφύγισσες, στα ΛΟΑΤΚΙ+ άτομα, στις έγκλειστες στις φυλακές και στα στρατόπεδα συγκέντρωσης του ελληνικού κράτους. Με όπλο μας τη συλλογικοποίηση και την οργάνωση των αντιστάσεών μας, να αγωνιστούμε για έναν κόσμο ελευθερίας, ισότητας και αλληλεγγύης για όλες και όλους.

author: CMI Argentina
title: En Argentina se registraron 266 femicidios en lo que va de 2026
content:
Según el último informe del Observatorio Nacional MuMaLá, entre el 1 de enero y el 20 de noviembre de 2026 se registraron 266 femicidios y 788 intentos en nuestro país. Es decir 1 femicidio cada 29 horas. Se trata del mayor aumento en la frecuencia de crímenes hacia mujeres, lesbianas, travestis y trans desde 2020. El dato surge a pocos días de las movilizaciones convocadas para el 25N, Día Internacional de la Eliminación de la Violencia contra las Mujeres.


El desglose de los 266 femicidios relevados por el Observatorio MuMaLá, señala que 194 fueron femicidios directos, 32 femicidios vinculados (21 de niños/varones y 11 de niñas/mujeres), 21 feminicidios en contexto de narcotráfico y crimen organizado, 10 suicidios feminicidas, 9 trans/travesticidios, 1 crimen de odio y 9 muertes violentas asociadas al género (en ocasión de robos u otros delitos).


Como consecuencia, 207 niños, niñas y adolescentes quedaron sin sus madres.


El informe también indica que solo el 11% de las mujeres asesinadas había realizado denuncias previas contra su agresor; y dentro de ese grupo que denunció, el 66% contaba con una orden de restricción o perimetral y el 14% tenía botón antipánico. Además, el 11% de los femicidas poseía antecedentes penales por violencia de género y el 5% pertenecía a alguna fuerza de seguridad.


En tanto, el 61% de los crímenes ocurrió en la vivienda de la víctima o en la vivienda compartida, y el 62% fue cometido por parejas, exparejas o familiares.


Aunque la edad promedio es de 37 años, fueron asesinadas 30 niñas y adolescentes (0 a 18 años) y 21 adultas mayores (60 años o más).


La tasa nacional de femicidios se ubica en 1 cada 100.000 mujeres, las jurisdicciones con mayores índices son Santa Fe (2,4), Santiago del Estero (2,3), San Luis (1,8), Misiones y Salta (1,5).


“Frente a un escenario que ya perforó los peores registros de los últimos cinco años, cuando todavía resta más de un mes para cerrar 2026, desde MuMaLá exigimos la inmediata Declaración de Emergencia Nacional en Violencias de Género”, afirman desde la organización.

author: cnt.es
title: Un 25N para todas, contra las violencias machistas y por la vida
content:
Leer en

Castellano

Català

Euskera

Galego

Asturianu


Castellano

Un 25N para todas, contra las violencias machistas y por la vida


En enero de este año, una abuela y sus nietas, ambas hijas de una mujer asesinada por su exmarido en 2023, fueron desahuciadas en Villaverde, barrio de Madrid, sin que las administraciones que debían protegerlas como víctimas de violencia machista hicieran nada para impedirlo. A Carmen y a su hija de 11 años no las desahució un fondo buitre sino su exmarido. Fue en Arrigorriaga, Bizkaia, el pasado octubre. Las suyas son historias de violencia machista económica que las feministas tan bien conocemos. Sabemos que a nosotras no solo nos expolian el banco, la patronal o los rentistas, sino también nuestros maltratadores. Y que las violencias machistas se ceban especialmente con las mujeres y las infancias.


Por eso, el pasado 11 de noviembre hicimos una huelga como una casa por una vivienda asequible y por salarios suficientes, pero no solo. Salimos a las calles porque necesitamos un sistema público fuerte que atienda a las mujeres y criaturas en situación de violencia, que ofrezca recursos y casas de acogida y atención integral para las sobrevivientes de violencias machistas. Un sistema que gaste menos en armas e invierta más en cuidados.


El 11N tomamos las calles en defensa de la vida. Y este 25 de noviembre, día internacional contra las violencias machistas, volvemos a hacerlo.


No caminamos solas. Nos preceden siglos de lucha y años de experiencias más recientes: desde los movimientos de denuncia como el Ni una menos argentino a las huelgas feministas del Estado español en 2018 y 2019, el Me Too, el Yo también y todas las historias de denuncia que miles de mujeres anónimas llevamos años compartiendo para crear un relato común. Nuestro relato. Ese que muestra que las violencias machistas son estructurales. Que tienen un patrón, aunque no son solo cuestión de clase.


Sabemos también que no nos afectan igual a todas. Que no puede denunciar o pedir ayuda igual la que vive en su país que la que ha migrado. Que, para las compañeras en situación irregular o de reagrupación familiar, la dependencia de su maltratador es mayor. Que las cadenas económicas que sufrimos quienes cuidamos nos atan aún más a situaciones de violencia de las que no es imposible salir: si cuidar nos empobrece, ¿cómo dejar una relación de maltrato si los precios de la vivienda son inasequibles? ¿Cómo romper con un padre maltratador si el sistema juzga primero a madres y a criaturas que denuncian abuso y violencia machista? ¿Cómo defendernos ante administraciones y juzgados que ponen en el punto de mira en las madres y nos arrancan a nuestras criaturas?


Por todo eso, también, saldremos este 25N. Lo hacemos desde el anarcosindicalismo porque la organización es la forma de lucha de quienes no tienen armas. La huelga es una herramienta de lucha y la solidaridad y sororidad son el camino.


Más frente a una ultraderecha negacionista de las violencias machistas, frente a la reacción contra los feminismos. En defensa del consentimiento, de la igualdad radical y del derecho al aborto; contra la gestación subrogada, la precarización de nuestras vidas y la de nuestras criaturas y contra este sistema que nos violenta mientras ampara a nuestros maltratadores. Porque nadie será libre hasta que todas lo seamos.


Este 25N tomamos las calles para seguir luchando por el fin de las violencias machistas. Tomamos las calles, de nuevo, por la vida.


Català

Un 25N per a totes, contra les violències masclistes i per la vida


Al gener d’enguany, una àvia i les seves netes, totes dues filles d’una dona assassinada pel seu exmarit al 2023, van ser desnonades a Villaverde, barri de Madrid, sense que les administracions que havien de protegir-les com a víctimes de violència masclista fessin res per a impedir-ho. A la Carmen i a la seva filla d’11 anys no les va desnonar un fons voltor sinó el seu exmarit. Va ser a Arrigorriaga, a Bizkaia, el passat octubre. Les seves són històries de violència masclista econòmica que les feministes tan bé coneixem. Sabem que a nosaltres no sols ens espolien el banc, la patronal o els rendistes, sinó també els nostres maltractadors. I que les violències masclistes les percebem especialment les dones i les infàncies.

author: Unknown
title: ^ and in addition to being a kind of ‘what-about-ism’, the 'everyone does it’ narrative ignores the…
content:
how-to-radicalize-a-tme

:

:

I think people need to understand that

everyone

 has to unlearn misogynistic behaviors and thinking patterns. Cis women and trans women and cis men and trans men and anyone who doesn’t fall under those categories are all completely capable of being misogynistic and actively hurtful to women. Trans men are included in this, obviously, but when you

only

 call for trans men to unlearn this mindset, you are no longer being progressive and fair. You are singling out a minority.

I’d like to challenge the last part of this post because I think it is ignoring the context of those calls to trans men. You’re totally correct in saying that anyone can perpetuate misogyny. However, particularly on online spaces like Tumblr, there has been a rise in TME and Trans masc individuals perpetuating misogyny and especially transmisogyny. So much that there is a 100% serious “pro transmisogyny” tag on tumblr!

It is not unfair to call this out. There are a lot of trans mascs on this site espousing transmisogny, and increasingly radical beliefs.

Any group of people has some amount of bad actors, so I am not going to deny that trans mascs have never faced vitriol unfairly, but we still cannot ignore the larger pattern of who is populating the #pro transmisogyny  tags, and how they react to being called out on it.


^ and in addition to being a kind of ‘what-about-ism’, the 'everyone does it’ narrative ignores the

specifics

of who is motivated to perform which misogynistic behaviors and what the result of that is.

Cis men are encouraged by the patriarchy to affirm their own gender - and hold at bay insecurities about their own gender - by publicly performing misogyny, and to blame women for any way in which they feel insufficiently masculine.

“It’s not the patriarchy that makes you feel this way! It’s those damn bitches who don’t see that i’m the good guy!”.

This dynamic makes cis men vulnerable to recruitment by groups such as incels and MRA’s, who both in different ways strengthen this narrative that it’s all women’s fault and that the way to be more of a man is to be more misogynist.

Trans men often experience intense invalidation of their gender by society, and deep trauma-induced insecurity about their own masculinity. Some trans men respond to this be staying/becoming feminists and challenging what masculinity means. These trans men tend to stand in solidarity with trans women and to recognize the unique ways in which transmisogyny harms trans women.

But some trans men turn to the performance of misogyny as a way to affirm their own gender, and blame trans women (= the only group of women that they can safely shout at under the patriarchy) for any way in which they feel insufficiently masculine.

“It’s not transphobia that makes you feel this way! It’s those damn trans bitches that criticize your gender-affirming performances of misogyny”

. This dynamic makes those particular men vulnerable to recruitment by an online subculture of “pro transmisogyny” which strengthens this narrative that it’s all trans women’s fault and that the way to be more of a man is to be more misogynist to trans women.

That dynamic and its results are specific and need to be discussed specifically. 'everyone does misogyny’ doesn’t help us with this shit.

author: Unknown
title: There this understanding of Transmasc/Transfem that is not an identity per say but the way you transition from your asab and more importantly how you are seen by society not your personal identity. So. A feminine enby who uses they/them is transmasc bc they are transition away from femininity and “femaleness” ; vice versa for a butch transfem with they/them pronouns. This is why many nonbinary ppl who were CAMAB see themselves as transfem regardless if they see themselves as women/or fem-aligned bc the world sees themselves as trans women and thus affected by transmisogyny. Idk how to think of it bc I do understand  where they are coming from. I
content:
Oh yeah, that's a very common misconception outside of the nonbinary community about the use of transition labels! I'm happy to explain.

First off, the transmasc/transfem labels have evolved over time. They started gaining traction in the early 2000s — although they had existed since at least the '90s — and were used as a catch-all term for anyone who was trans, without having to necessarily identify as transsexual or binary transgender. Like many historical labels, they have existed for most of their history as nebulous terms with no set definition, just a general vibe.

To start, I want to note that some of the earlier attempts at defining those labels did try to describe them in terms of what one is transitioning away from, instead of what one's actual gender identity is.

For example,

advocate S. Leigh Thompson (who is a trans man) proposed this definition in 2006

:

Transmasculine: Any person who was assigned female at birth but feels that is an incomplete or incorrect description of their gender.

That being said, those sorts of definitions never really became the predominant ones inside of nonbinary communities. And as of right now, they are actively disliked by most. For one, they don't take into account intersex people, who might have a complex history with gender and might use "contradictory" labels like AFAB transfem or AMAB transmasc. Furthermore, those definitions just.. don't make sense from a nonbinary perspective. Which is a big problem, since the labels transfem/transmasc are supposed to be used to include (some of) us.

Those definitions stem from the exorsexist idea that there is only one possible direction of transition: away from your "biological sex" and towards the "opposite sex". But gender is more complex than a line that goes from "man" to "woman" in which getting away from "man" necessarily pushes you towards "woman" and vice versa. For example, a medically-transitioning transneutral person might wish to remove their gendered characteristics (breasts, facial hair, etc.), but not wish to gain the ones associated with the opposite sex, like a binary-aligned trans person typically would. Even though they are transitioning away from typical presentations of their assigned sex-gender, their transition is also atypical for transfems/transmascs norms, and categorizing them as either of those just based on their AGAB would be reductive. Not to mention that social transition (being recognized as one's actual gender by society) is an integral part of transitioning, too. Categorizing a trans person as transmasc or transfem when they don't consider their gender identity masculine nor feminine is basically misgendering. At the end of the day, you (general you) are still telling someone who sees themselves as neutral, or androgynous, or fluid, or anything else they might identity as, that they need to be categorized based on the gender binary.

This framework also leads to the false idea that nonbinary people will always have more in common with binary trans people of the same "biological sex" than a nonbinary person of the "opposite" one with a similar gender identity. This is simply not the case, and in nonbinary spaces we rarely divide ourselves based on AGAB. A transmasculine or transfeminine enban might feel understood and included in trans man/woman spaces, but that's because they are transitioning towards masculinity/femininity just like them, not because AGAB inherently creates a connection between trans people. I, for one, feel a lot more understood amongst other neutral/unaligned people than I do around more binary-aligned people with my same AGAB.

Now, there are people who, despite being told all of this, will still argue in favor of using the labels in the way you (asker) have observed from others. Often under the guise of "society at large is transphobic and doesn't recognize nonbinary genders, so your oppression can only be described accurately if the labels indicate what you're transitioning away from". And my question to them is: if society is transphobic and doesn't recognize me as my actual gender, shouldn't a trans advocacy movement strive to change that, instead of telling trans people their identity doesn't exist? Furthermore: why does transness always need to be defined in terms of suffering? Why should an identity label be assigned to me based on how society (mis)treats me, instead of giving me the agency to choose the words to describe my own experience?

And, if you allow me …

author: Shayna Medley
title: This Supreme Court Case Could Open the Floodgates to Anti-Trans Lawsuits
content:
The case illustrates just how deeply trans health care and reproductive rights are intertwined.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

The Supreme Court has taken up another case that could impact transgender and reproductive rights.

The case, International Partners for Ethical Care v. Ferguson, was brought by parents who oppose the availability of abortion and trans health care in Washington State. Specifically, they sued the state over three laws that they allege would allow runaway youth to access gender-affirming or reproductive health care in licensed shelters without parental consent.

Oral arguments will take place on Dec. 7, 2026.

I am a litigator and law professor who studies the intersection between trans and reproductive rights. This case illustrates just how deeply trans health care and reproductive rights are intertwined. And if the plaintiffs are successful, the case could open the door to more legal challenges by parents attempting to undermine bodily autonomy rights that they don’t believe young people should have.

The plaintiffs’ arguments in IPEC v. Ferguson rest on attenuated and far-fetched claims of harm.

The parents in the case do not have children living in homeless youth shelters. Yet, they allege that they have changed their parenting styles in response to these statutes out of fear that prohibiting their children from socially transitioning in any way will cause them to flee home and seek medical care without their consent.

Notably, the Washington laws at issue in this case do not regulate parents’ conduct or speech. So the harms the plaintiffs are alleging are self-imposed choices — not the result of Washington’s laws.

And, according to the state of Washington, the only kind of gender-affirming care youth can access without parental consent in any case is a referral to outpatient mental health services.

So, the question before the Court is a narrow one: Do these parents have standing to sue over Washington’s runaway youth laws?

Standing is a legal concept derived from Article III of the U.S. Constitution, which requires that anyone bringing a lawsuit in federal court demonstrate an “injury in fact.” That means they must show that they have been harmed or face an imminent threat of future harm by the laws they’re challenging.

Standing is an important constitutional principle. Civil rights attorneys generally advocate for it to be interpreted broadly, because it is essential that people who’ve been harmed by the government be able to enforce their constitutional rights in court.

However, opponents of trans and reproductive rights are increasingly contorting the meaning of “harm” to undermine bodily autonomy.

Because the Court is currently only considering whether the plaintiffs in Ferguson have met the legal requirements of standing to move forward with their case — not deciding whether their arguments challenging Washington’s laws are winning ones — the question before the Court is a procedural one.

But the Court’s ruling could nonetheless have a ripple effect on trans and reproductive rights.

As the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals concluded when it decided this case in 2025, the plaintiffs’ theory of harm rests on a string of hypothetical allegations that: “(1) one of the Individual Plaintiffs’ minor children (2) runs away (3) to a licensed shelter (4) while actively seeking or receiving gender-affirming care, resulting in (5) the shelter taking in the child (6) despite knowing that the minor is there without parental permission.”

The court found the parents’ concerns to be “amorphous and insufficiently explained.” Concluding there was insufficient evidence of harm, the court dismissed the case for lack of standing. A district court previously dismissed the parents’ arguments on similar grounds in 2024.

Despite two lower courts finding that the parents lacked standing to sue the state, the Supreme Court granted the parents’ appeal.

Usually, when two lower courts make the same ruling based on a straightforward application of the law, there’s little reason for the Supreme Court to take up a case. The law is clear. As Washington State argued in its Oct. 21, 2026, brief to the Court, the parents’ theory of standing is “‘startlingly broad’” and “invites absurd results.”

But given the track record of the Roberts Court in creating a national pathway for tenuous …

author: TGEU
title: Joint LGBTI+ NGO letter to the Turkish Embassy in Berlin, Germany
content:
On 25 November, TGEU – Trans Europe and Central Asia,

OII Europe

 and

OII Germany

 have sent a joint letter to the German foreign ministries to express serious concerns about the situation in Türkiye and the recent targeting of the LGBTI+ organisations and human rights defenders.


Since 12 September, several police raids have been conducted in Türkiye, targeting LGBTI+ human rights defenders and organisations, as part of the so-called “My Family is Safe” operations. During these raids, police seized digital equipment of the activists and organisations. Websites and social media accounts of LGBTI+ activists and organisations were blocked. 78 people have been in detention for 2 months. On 23 October, in a new wave of arrests, 45 people across 7 provinces were taken into custody and more than 20 of them, including 10 trans women, were imprisoned. Again, on 3 November, 22 people were detained and questioned, several of whom are trans women, in relation to “forming an organisation for the purpose of committing a crime”. Relying on obscenity clauses and provisions on prostitution, Turkish authorities have targeted trans people and sex workers in all waves of the arrests. 


Already, in January 2026, Ankara Public Prosecutor’s Office filed a lawsuit against head of the

17 Mayıs Association

 Defne Güzel with alleged charges of violating public morality by publishing the Turkish translation of

OII Europe’s publication #MyIntersexStory

, a collection of testimonies of intersex people, and an exhibition catalogue. The lawsuit followed an expert report from 2025 which concluded that the activities of the 17 Mayıs Association are entirely consistent with the objectives set out in its statutes and that there are no irregularities whatsoever. Güzel was later acquitted of all charges in the first hearing in May.  


Human rights at stake


These operations mark a significant escalation in the criminalisation of LGBTI+ human rights activism in Türkiye, and a direct attack on freedom of expression, association, and the defence of human rights. The October operations criminalise non-normative identities and bodies, including trans and intersex people and organisations, based only on social media posts declared by the Ankara Chief Public Prosecutor’s Office as “contrary to public morality, targeting families, children and young people, detrimental to their development, encouraging gender neutrality and disruptive to public order”.


LGBTI+ organisations in Türkiye are targeted for their legitimate activities. The domestic and international funding they receive is lawful, and they operate as registered associations under Turkish law. With these actions, the Turkish government continues to undermine the right of legally registered organisations to participate in democratic processes.


The ongoing imprisonment of 78 individuals since September, the inhumane prison conditions and the torture perpetrated against them breach international human rights law, as well as the Constitution of Türkiye and the Turkish Penal Code. The European Court of Human Rights and the UN Human Rights Committee have made clear that public morality cannot justify infringing fundamental rights. These operations also institutionalise discrimination and arbitrary detention, fuel a climate of hatred, threaten the right to life of LGBTI+ people, and increase state-sanctioned hate speech.


Germany’s role


It is clear that the rights of LGBTI+ people in Türkiye and civic freedoms enjoyed by all Turkish citizens are at stake. As a longstanding strategic partner of Türkiye and a vocal critic of Türkiye’s backsliding on rule of law, it is imperative that Germany speaks up and reminds Türkiye of its obligations as a member of the Council of Europe and a candidate country of the EU, to respect fundamental human rights standards that apply to all, no matter a person’s sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or sex characteristics.


As the home to the largest Turkish diaspora, Germany hosts several LGBTI+ human rights defenders, whose work and ability to return to Turkey safely also depends on the end to the targeting of LGBTI+ human rights defenders. As one of the strongest supporters of Türkiye’s accession, Germany should actively support the freedom of association and LGBTI+ human rights in Türkiye.


Our demands


Therefore, the undersigned organisations operating in Germany urge the German foreign ministries to:


Call for the immediate release …

title: «Avisame cuando llegues»
content:
Foto: corresponsal popular, para ANRed


En el marco del 25 N, Día Internacional de Lucha Contra las Violencias Machistas, se convocó desde la Asamblea Comarcal Transfeminista a una jornada cultural y de lucha en la localidad de El Hoyo (Chubut). Hubo lectura de poesía, canción, música y danza, con el fin de acompañarse, recordar y organizarse. “Nos parece muy importante seguir tejiendo la Comarca, el feminismo y el transfeminismo, más allá de donde vivamos. Entender que este territorio extenso necesita de esa red”, expresaron desde la Asamblea.

Por Corresponsal popular para ANRed.


“Nos parece muy importante constituirnos comarcalmente, porque

las cosas que pasan no nos separan por cuestiones jurisdiccionales y por los límites que ponen otres

.

Los problemas son comunes, las redes son comunes, nos juntamos para nosotros, para nosotres

, entonces hay que seguir tejiendo la Comarca, el feminismo y el transfeminismo de la Comarca, más allá de donde vivamos. Esto nos parece muy importante hoy. Este año intentamos que el 8M fuera fuerte en Bolsón, el 3J en Puelo y apostamos fuertemente al 25N acá. Queremos sostenerlo, sostener el trabajo del feminismo comarcal. Asi que bueno, los invito a eso, a que estemos atentas, atentes, y fortalezcamos las redes más allá del lugarcito donde vivamos. Entender que este territorio extenso necesita de esa red extendida”, expresaron desde la

Asamblea Comarcal Transfeminista

, al término de las distintas intervenciones culturales y previo a la marcha por la localidad.


Foto: corresponsal popular, para ANRed


Y agregaron: “contarles también que

mensualmente nos venimos juntando en una cosa que se llama RONDAS, rondas feministas, rondas transfeministas

, y ahí vamos también armando algunas herramientas y respuestas que vamos necesitando a problemas puntuales. La otra vez nos juntamos a jugar, porque eso también nos parecía importante. Dedicarnos un rato a otra cosa. Pero también nos juntamos a hacer fanzines para decirnos cosas, contarnos cómo nos acompañamos, qué cosa hace cada red.

Sabemos que en Puelo es muy fuerte y muy constante y muy sostenedor que les jubilades sostengan ya no me acuerdo cuantas marchas, pero bueno esa reunión de jubilades tiene también esa impronta comarcal y apostamos a eso, a sostenerlo

”.


Foto: corresponsal popular, para ANRed


Foto: corresponsal popular, para ANRed


“He visto a las mujeres


Más bellas del mundo.


Convertirse en diminutas sombras


Satisfaciendo los deseos de sus seres queridos.


He visto a las mujeres


Mas inteligentes de la vida


Haciendo añicos sus argumentos


Frente al protagonismo de sus amantes.


He visto mujeres con alas


Sacando lustre a los barrotes


De las jaulas que les compran sus maridos.


Las he visto bajarse de la luna


Para vivir en la cueva del sapo


De su amado. 


Las he visto superar el hambre, 


Las guerras, la muerte

author: CNT Santander
title: No hay Revolución Social sin Revolución Feminista
content:
25N, DÍA INTERNACIONAL DE LA ELIMINACIÓN DE LA VIOLENCIA EJERCIDA SOBRE LA MUJER


 


Este 25 N, volvemos a salir a las calles

 para denunciar todas las formas de violencia que el patriarcado ejerce sobre nuestros cuerpos, nuestras vidas y nuestras libertades. Una violencia que no puede entenderse como un problema individual, porque es una violencia estructural. Está profundamente arraigada en un sistema que pretende controlar nuestros cuerpos, condicionar nuestras decisiones, limitar nuestra autonomía y mantenernos en una posición de subordinación.


El patriarcado nunca ha actuado solo. Lo sostiene el sistema capitalista en el que vivimos, y se reproduce a través del capacitismo, el edadismo, el racismo, la explotación laboral, el colonialismo, la homofobia, la transfobia, y todas aquellas estructuras de poder que no aceptan las disidencias y las diversidades, esas estructuras que generan desigualdades y convierten nuestras vidas en territorios de dominación.


La violencia machista tiene muchas caras, las mujeres lo sabemos bien; feminicidios, agresiones sexuales, acoso, maltrato psicológico, violencia sexual digital, abuso infantil, amenazas, control económico, humillación…


Y no debemos olvidar que se alimenta de la precariedad a la que nos condena, la explotación de las trabajadoras del hogar y quienes se encargan de los cuidados, la discriminación laboral, el racismo institucional, la violencia obstétrica, la negación de derechos y la falta de recursos y protección para quienes necesitan escapar de situaciones de violencia.


No todas las mujeres vivimos la violencia de la misma manera, pero somos capaces de entender el sufrimiento de nuestras iguales. Y queremos dejar claro que cuando hablamos de nuestras iguales, cuando utilizamos este femenino, no lo hacemos de una manera neutra. Nuestro plural femenino es, y será siempre, inclusivo con todas las disidencias, interseccional, transfeminista,

 

antirracista y sin jerarquías. Porque ha de ser una herramienta de emancipación colectiva.


Estamos con las mujeres migrantes y las racializadas, porque nos queremos sin fronteras. Estamos con las mujeres discas y las neurodivergentes, porque no nos queremos por nuestra capacidad de producir más y más. Estamos con las mayores, ancianas o viejas*, porque hay mucha vida y mucha lucha en la que nos necesitamos de todas las edades. Estamos con las mujeres encarceladas y las niñas que pasan su infancia y adolescencia en centros de menores, porque nos queremos libres. Estamos con las infancias abusadas. Estamos con las bolleras, las bi, las personas trans y no binarias, y todas las disidencias, porque nadie nos tiene que decir quiénes somos.


Sabemos que quienes viven en situaciones de exclusión social, por una parte de la sociedad enferma de odio, encuentran obstáculos añadidos para defenderse, denunciar y acceder a una vida digna y libre. Sus hermanas y hermanes no lo olvidamos.


Nuestros cuerpos no tienen dueño y nuestros corazones no necesitan pedir permiso para ser. Cada una tenemos derecho a vivir nuestra identidad, nuestra sexualidad y nuestra vida con dignidad, autonomía y total libertad.


La solución a esta violencia machista que nos mata y nos ahoga, es y siempre será la respuesta colectiva. Desde

CNT Santander

, denunciamos la indiferencia institucional, la falta de recursos públicos, la precarización de los servicios de atención y una justicia que muchas veces ni escucha ni protege a nuestras hermanas y hermanes, la precariedad laboral que impide a muchas mujeres tener su independencia económica y autonomía.


Por ello, la respuesta debe ser colectiva, sin fisuras, todas a una, hasta destruir todas las relaciones de poder que permiten que unas personas sometan a otras.


¡Frente a sus violencias, organización y autodefensa!


Como anarcosindicalistas, apostamos por el apoyo mutuo, la solidaridad combativa, la organización desde abajo y la construcción de redes comunitarias capaces de acompañar, escuchar, proteger y sostener a todas las mujeres. Reivindicamos la autodefensa feminista como una herramienta colectiva para recuperar nuestra autonomía, acabar con las agresiones machistas y romper el aislamiento que tantas veces impone esa maldita violencia.


Queremos espacios de trabajo libres de acoso y explotación, sindicatos comprometidos con la igualdad real y efectiva, barrios seguros para todas las personas y relaciones construidas desde el respeto, el consentimiento y la libertad.


Lucharemos para …

author: By Camilla Conzelli, Contributor
title: Trans Teacher Fired, Then Held in Men’s Cell, as Turkey Escalates Crackdown on LGBTQIA+ People
content:
Istanbul, Turkey — Months after being fired, trans teacher Zoe Lila was detained at a Sept. 15 protest against the “My Family Is Safe” operation, Turkey’s crackdown on LGBTQIA+ people, and she was held in a men’s cell.


“I was a queer kid, I’ve been discriminated against since childhood, and I never felt included in the school system,” Zoe Lila said. “That’s why teaching isn’t just a job for me: it means being there as an educator, making sure no human being experiences any kind of discrimination.”


Lila is a young Turkish trans woman who has worked in education for 10 years. In 2021, she started teaching English at a private school, Açı Middle School in Istanbul. “It’s an international school that welcomes many minorities and bases its approach on human rights,” she explained. “So I felt like I had finally found my place.”


Zoe Lila


In 2024, when she began hormone replacement therapy, Lila told the school’s administration about her transition. “Their first reaction was, ‘It’s your right, we’ll support you,’” she recalled. Encouraged by that support, she decided to stay in Turkey, despite a long and complex process.


Reyda Ergün, an academic working on LGBTQIA+ rights, said the country is one of the worst examples of a medicalized model for gender affirmation.


Under the

current legal framework

, vaginoplasty or phalloplasty is a binding prerequisite for legal recognition. The surgery can only be authorized by a court, and the person must have a diagnosis of “transsexualism” certifying that surgery is necessary for their mental health. After the operation, a second court proceeding begins in which a judge has the discretion to decide whether the procedure was “sufficient and appropriate” to change the person’s biological characteristics.


Since 2018, Ergün has co-authored an annual report published by

Kaos GL

, an organization that monitors the employment conditions of LGBTQIA+ people in Turkey’s

public

 and

private

 sectors.


Over the years, the data has revealed that

concealing one’s identity

 is the primary means of self-defense workers adopt for fear of retaliation or dismissal.


In this context, trans people are especially vulnerable. “The long and complex nature of the affirmation and legal recognition process can expose people to further discrimination and job insecurity,” Ergün said. “When changes in official records and physical appearance become visible before legal recognition has been obtained, concealment strategies are no longer viable, and the risks that had been averted until then materialize.”


Zoe Lila’s story is a textbook example. In the summer of 2026, she completed the process leading to her gender-affirming surgery. In mid-June, she first came out to her colleagues and then, during a dedicated session led by a psychologist, to her 120 students. The reaction at school was initially warm and welcoming, but a few days later, everything fell apart.


A parent sent Lila’s photo and personal information to pro-government media, setting off a virulent hate campaign. Newspapers published her image with a cross over her face, revealing all of her personal data and the details of the school where she worked.


“It was horrible. It was the most unfair, unethical and unlawful article I’ve ever read in my life. And the person it was talking about was me,” Lila said. Soon she began receiving death threats and insults, including from her own family. Feeling unsafe, she left her apartment and moved in with a friend.


Meanwhile, Turkey’s Ministry of National Education intervened directly at the school. Under threat of sanctions and mass layoffs, school administrators caved to the political pressure. On June 24, 2026, just 10 hours before her long-scheduled vaginoplasty, the school told Lila it would not renew her contract.


“I was fired 10 hours before the surgery, and it was devastating,” she said. The operation went ahead as planned, but Lila suddenly found herself without a job, without income and at the center of a violent attack. She immediately turned to a lawyer to take legal action, but ran up against Turkish labor law: private school teachers are typically hired on renewable one-year contracts, which rules out a lawsuit for reinstatement.


Still, the fight continues through complaints filed with the relevant authorities and the creation of a

solidarity network

. “We don’t want financial compensation,” Lila said. “We want this to be an act of defense for trans and LGBTQ+ …

content:
Wir haben uns heute als Frauen und alle die als solche unterdrückt werden, kämpferisch die Straße und die Nacht genommen!


Jede von uns kennt die Angst davor alleine im Dunkeln nach Hause zu laufen, die Angst davor verfolgt und belästigt zu werden. Jede von uns kennt patriarchale Gewalt. Doch wir haben von klein auf gelernt zu akzeptieren, was uns angetan wird. Gelernt darüber zu schweigen und die Schuld bei uns selbst zu suchen. Aber diese Gewalt ist Teil des patriarchalen und kapitalistischen Systems und sie ist dafür da uns einzuschüchtern und unten zu halten.


Wir sagen: Es reicht!


Um diesem System den Kampf anzusagen, müssen wir uns zusammenschließen, lernen gemeinsam zu kämpfen und uns auferlegte Rollenbilder zu durchbrechen. So wird Angst in Stärke und Mut verwandelt und wir verstehen, dass wir uns diese zu nutzen machen können.


Auch müssen gerade wir als Frauen eine militante Haltung und daraus hervorgehend, eine militante Praxis entwickeln. Denn unsere Befreiung wird nicht mit Worten erkämpft werden. Dabei können wir lernen, von den Kämpferinnen der YPG, von der feministischen Bewegung Lateinamerikas und so vielen weiteren Genossinnen aus der ganzen Welt. Denn wir werden uns nur selbst schützen. Und nur wir können dem Ursprung der patriarchalen Gewalt, diesem kapitalistischen und patriarchalem System etwas entgegensetzen. Kämpfen wir also gemeinsam für den revolutionären Bruch und den Aufbau des Kommunismus!


Für die Feministische Revolution!


Heraus zum Tag gegen Gewalt an Frauen!


Anmerkung des Moderationskollektiv von barrikade.info: «Unsere Sprache spiegelt gesellschaftliche Machtverhältninsse und Unterdrückungsformen wieder. Dazu gehören Sexismus und die erzwungene Geschlechterbinarität. Dies äussert sich u.a. in der Nutzung einer binären Sprache. Dies bedeutet, dass nur in den Kategorien «Frau» und «Mann» gedacht und geschrieben wird. Als Kollektiv einer emanzipatorischen, anti-autoritären Medien-Plattform erwarten wir eine diskrimiierungsfreie Haltung. Die Geschlechtsbinarität stellt eine Unterdrückung dar und die Verwendung binärer Sprache in Momenten, in denen die Schreibenden die Geschlechtsidentität der Menschen nicht kennen und/oder Identitäten, welche nicht in dieser Binarität Platz haben, unsichtbar gemacht werden, ist diskriminierend.


Anstelle von binären Begriffen kann in solchen Momenten genderneutrale Sprache verwendet werden (z.B. Demonstrierende). Auch kann versucht werden, durch andere Begriffe die gewünschte Menschengruppe zu beschreiben (z.B. TINFA*), sowie kann auf die Nutzung von Genderzeichen, wie dem Genderstern, zurückgegriffen werden. Oder durch die Nennung, wer nicht gemeint ist, lassen sich ebenfalls inklusive Menschengruppen schaffen (z.B. alle, welche nicht Teil der hegemonialen Männlichkeit sind).


Natürlich gibt es noch weitere Möglichkeiten, welche genutzt werden können.

author: Andrea DiP
title: ‘Para onde eu vou?’ Brasil é julgado na Corte Interamericana por direito de mulher trans
content:
“Eu sei que, para muitas pessoas aqui, deve soar estranho uma pessoa que não se identifica com o sexo de nascimento. E eu tentei por muitos anos viver da forma que eu havia nascido, mudando o meu foco para o trabalho, para aprender coisas. E quando não deu mais, eu tentei viver de uma certa forma, só que percebi que não era possível.”


É assim que a cabeleireira Luiza Melinho iniciou o seu depoimento à Corte Interamericana de Direitos Humanos (IDH), no dia 19 de novembro, na audiência de mérito do Caso 13.021, Luiza Melinho vs. Brasil, que aconteceu durante dois dias na sede do tribunal, em San José, na Costa Rica.


O julgamento é inédito em dois sentidos:

É a primeira vez que a Corte examina especificamente o direito à saúde de pessoas trans em um caso que envolve procedimentos de afirmação de gênero, e é a primeira vez que o Brasil responde ao tribunal por violações de direitos de uma pessoa LGBTQIAPN+

. A sentença, que ainda não tem data para sair, pode criar parâmetros internacionais para todo o continente. Em caso de condenação, o tribunal poderá determinar medidas de reparação à vítima, como indenizações e ações de reabilitação, além de impor ao Estado providências destinadas a evitar a repetição das violações constatadas.


Se o Brasil for condenado, terá de cumprir a decisão, porque as sentenças da Corte são vinculantes para os países que reconhecem sua jurisdição.


A coluna teve acesso exclusivo aos pareceres de dois peritos que representaram o Estado brasileiro. Os nomes dos peritos, assim como trechos exatos dos documentos serão preservados.


Em 1997, aos 26 anos, Luiza deu entrada no Hospital das Clínicas da Unicamp depois de uma tentativa de suicídio. No atendimento psiquiátrico, a equipe médica identificou que ela precisava de um tratamento de afirmação de gênero, com procedimentos cirúrgicos.

 Por anos, Luiza fez tudo o que o protocolo da época exigia: passou por avaliações em psiquiatria, psicologia, endocrinologia, genética e otorrinolaringologia, e a indicação cirúrgica foi respaldada por pareceres médicos.


Em março de 2001, ela estava internada para uma condroplastia, a redução do pomo de Adão, no pescoço, quando a cirurgia foi cancelada. O motivo, segundo os autos citados em um dos pareceres periciais, foi o “horário de almoço do anestesista da sala”. Pouco depois, a direção da clínica avisou que o hospital não daria continuidade aos procedimentos.


“Quando eu fui chamada na sala da diretora da clínica, ela estava com cópias do meu prontuário e simplesmente me entregou e disse: ‘Olha, nós não vamos fazer a cirurgia, então eu te oriento a buscar um outro lugar’. Eu olhei para ela e disse: ‘Mas para onde eu vou?’” lembrou Luiza em seu depoimento à Corte.


Não havia para onde ir. Conforme ofício judicial de 2004, o serviço do HC-USP declarou que suas triagens estavam fechadas por excesso de demanda e por reforma física

; e “não aproveitamos avaliações feitas por outras instituições ou profissionais […] Quem se candidata ao tratamento deve ter em mente que inicia do marco zero e esperará, no mínimo, por dois anos para a indicação cirúrgica, se é que ela vai acontecer”.


A própria psiquiatra que acompanhava Luiza na Unicamp escreveu à diretoria, em 2002, que as pacientes estavam “se sentindo traídas e abandonadas por nós”.


No mesmo ano, Luiza se automutilou. “Eu senti que os meus sonhos tinham saído e eu já vinha tendo os sintomas ruins da castração química, então eu me mutilei. Naquele momento, eu pensava assim: ‘Eu tiro isso de mim nem que eu morra, mas eu tiro isso de mim, porque eu não quero mais, eu não sei como continuar isso tudo’ conta em seu depoimento.


Em 2005, angustiada, Luiza se endividou e fez a cirurgia na rede privada, em uma clínica, sem a estrutura hospitalar necessária, paga com um empréstimo da empregadora. “Eu fui pagando esse financiamento ao longo dos anos para que eu pudesse pelo menos ter um mínimo de dignidade”. Perante a Corte, ela relata que após o procedimento, não recebeu do médico qualquer orientação de cuidados pós-operatórios.


Quando voltou ao SUS para buscar atendimento devido aos efeitos dessa operação, ouviu de novo uma recusa: “A cirurgia não foi feita aqui, não é responsabilidade nossa”.


Em agosto deste ano, aos 58 anos, ela precisou passar por uma nova cirurgia para tratar as consequências daquele procedimento.

 “[A cirurgia] era a única forma que eu tive de poder ter um pouco de paz comigo mesma, de fazer com que o meu corpo fosse o meu …
