author: Nick Manley
title: Pengantar Singkat Teori Ekonomi Laissez-Faire Sayap Kiri: Bagian Pertama
content:
Oleh:

Nick Manley

. Teks aslinya berjudul “

Brief Introduction To Left-Wing Laissez Faire Economic Theory: Part One

”. Diterjemahkan ke dalam Bahasa Indonesia oleh Taratsa


Dalam dua tulisan

blog

 saya sebelumnya, saya menanggapi artikel Lynn Stuart Parramore berjudul

How Piketty’s Bombshell Book Blew Up Libertarian Fantasies

. Pada akhir tulisan

kedua

, saya berjanji akan menjelaskan teori ekonomi yang saya gunakan untuk mengkritik artikel tersebut. Tulisan ini akan menjadi pengantar singkat mengenai teori ekonomi itu. Mari kita mulai.


Teori ini dikenal sebagai anarkisme pasar kiri (

left-wing market anarchism

) atau sosialisme laissez-faire (

laissez-faire socialism

). Gagasan dasarnya adalah bahwa pasar yang benar-benar bebas belum pernah ada, dan kapitalisme sesungguhnya merupakan sistem yang bertumpu pada negara (

statist system

). Teori ini juga berangkat dari keyakinan bahwa pasar yang benar-benar bebas akan menghasilkan tingkat kesetaraan relatif yang lebih tinggi serta kondisi kerja yang lebih berpihak kepada pekerja.


Hal pertama yang perlu dibahas adalah empat monopoli besar yang diidentifikasi oleh mendiang

anarkis individualis

,

Benjamin Tucker

. Keempatnya dijelaskan dalam esainya yang terkenal,

State Socialism and Anarchism: How Far They Agree, And Wherein They Differ

. Keempat monopoli tersebut adalah monopoli uang, monopoli tanah, monopoli tarif, serta monopoli paten atau kekayaan intelektual. Mari kita bahas satu per satu.


1. Monopoli Uang (

Money Monopoly

)


Monopoli uang berkaitan dengan pemberian privilese oleh pemerintah atau negara kepada individu-individu tertentu maupun orang-orang yang memiliki jenis properti tertentu. Privilese ini berupa hak eksklusif untuk menerbitkan uang. Dampaknya adalah tingkat suku bunga tetap tinggi atau setidaknya dipertahankan pada tingkat yang lebih tinggi secara artifisial.


Dalam masyarakat anarkis pasar libertarian kiri, siapa pun akan bebas menerbitkan mata uang sendiri. Persaingan akan mendorong biaya pinjaman uang turun hingga mendekati biaya tenaga kerja yang dibutuhkan untuk menjalankan kegiatan perbankan. Efek positif lain yang diidentifikasi Tucker adalah hilangnya kendali sebagaimana disebutkan berikut:


Konon, para pemegang privilese ini mengendalikan tingkat suku bunga, tarif sewa rumah dan bangunan, serta harga barang-barang—yang pertama secara langsung, sedangkan dua lainnya secara tidak langsung.


Kevin Carson

 mengutip Alexander

Cairncross

yang menyatakan bahwa:


Pekerja Amerika memiliki persediaan modal yang lebih besar di rumah mereka sendiri daripada di pabrik tempat mereka bekerja….


Modal atau properti tersebut dapat digunakan sebagai jaminan atau agunan. Hal ini akan memperkuat posisi tawar pekerja dalam hubungannya dengan modal, karena mereka dapat membangun sistem kredit bersama untuk menjalankan usaha secara mandiri, terpisah dari para kapitalis. Sebagaimana

dicatat

Gary Elkin:


Penting untuk dicatat bahwa, melalui usul Tucker untuk memperkuat posisi tawar pekerja dengan memberikan akses terhadap kredit mutual, apa yang disebut sebagai anarkisme individualis bukan hanya sejalan dengan kendali pekerja, tetapi justru akan mendorong terwujudnya kendali tersebut. Sebab, jika akses terhadap kredit mutual dapat meningkatkan posisi tawar pekerja sebagaimana diklaim Tucker, mereka akan mampu (1) menuntut dan memperoleh demokrasi di tempat kerja, serta (2) menggabungkan akses kredit mereka untuk membeli dan memiliki perusahaan secara kolektif.


2. Monopoli Tanah (

Land Monopoly

)


Monopoli tanah terjadi ketika pemerintah atau negara memberikan maupun melindungi hak kepemilikan tanah yang tidak didasarkan pada prinsip penguasaan dan penggunaan (occupation and use). Kritik ini ditujukan kepada praktik kepemilikan tanah oleh tuan tanah yang tidak menggarap atau menggunakan tanahnya sendiri (absentee landlordism), beserta praktik penarikan uang sewa yang menyertainya.


Praktik tersebut menghalangi pekerjaan berbasis tanah untuk menjadi faktor yang dapat bersaing dengan sektor industri. Selain itu, monopoli ini juga menghancurkan kemandirian yang seharusnya dapat diperoleh seseorang melalui penguasaan tanah atau pemanfaatan tanah bersama yang bebas dari negara.


3. Monopoli Tarif (Tariff Monopoly)


Monopoli tarif berkaitan dengan perlindungan keuntungan industri kapitalis domestik dari persaingan asing. Kebijakan ini menaikkan harga barang sehingga semakin banyak hasil kerja yang harus diserahkan oleh …

author: ROAPE
title: When ‘the people’ become a problem
content:
The return of political economy to the centre of debates on minerals, sovereignty, and wealth also politicises a more concealed but fundamental category of politics: the people. The people as the foundational logic of politics is obscured either by reducing agency to voting and institutionally mediated participation or through the introduction of ‘meta’ categories for understanding people and their behaviour, such as those found in modern economics. While both tendencies draw legitimacy from the people, neither represents the ultimate contour of popular participation.


In fact, the liberal framework itself often produces a greater degree of depoliticisation of popular will, contradicting its claims to popular legitimacy. Within the neoliberal ‘free trade’ world, this depoliticisation is further amplified by reducing state capacity in favour of private enterprise and ownership.


As I argued in my

earlier piece

, the recent political trajectory of Burkina Faso is significant precisely because questions of ownership, extraction, production, and economic sovereignty have returned to the sphere of popular political contestation. Reduced state capacity does not simply diminish sovereign power; it transforms the role of the state into an arbitrator of bourgeois interests over popular representation, privileging profit over people while representing the category of the people through differentiated and graded notions of ‘development’.


The question of state agency in Africa against neoliberal and neo-imperial interventions has long been a subject of scholarly and theoretical debate. Reduced state capacity facilitates neoliberal extraction of resources, the INGO raj, environmental destruction, and the undermining of mechanisms of popular representation. When popular will is asserted, a subtler yet visible distinction between the liberal and the illiberal is often mobilised to critique the economics and politics of such movements.


In popular discourse, this binary is largely treated as a neutral descriptive category, almost self-evident in its meaning. Yet an inquiry into its history reveals it as a political technology: a method of political discourse through which popular movements – particularly in the Third World – have been classified, disciplined, and, when necessary, delegitimised by pitching one side against the other.


The liberal/illiberal binary has, of course, acquired considerable complexity, and recent scholarly interventions have captured its variability, particularly in Africa and Latin America. But its political uses remain consequential.


From the hypocrisy of the West to the selective deployment of human rights, justice, and other ‘moral’ equivalents – while ongoing crises in Gaza, Sudan, and elsewhere in the Global South are largely ignored by the mainstream – to the concealment of economic dependency and the relationship of the ‘First’ World to the ‘Third’, depoliticisation has become a norm rather than an exception.


As Eyob Balcha Gebremariam has

recently argued

 writing for roape.net, Eurocentrism and the selective application of the so-called ‘rules-based world order’ continue to shape international narratives in ways that privilege Western interests while presenting them as universal norms. Liberal-democratic states, whether the United States, France, or India, have themselves mobilised brutal armed power to crush popular agitations by farmers, students, and workers.


The fissures in the liberal/illiberal binary, therefore, reveal not only its poverty as an account of political life, but also the hollowness of ‘by the people, for the people’ sloganeering when confronted with people acting beyond the institutional boundaries prescribed for them. The question, then, is what can some of the political-economic changes in today’s Africa teach us about the people and their political agency?


One of the first and most important lessons from Burkina Faso and the political transitions there comes from de-concealing the concealed: the people. The Volunteers for the Defence of the Homeland (VDPs) have been

a particular focus of discussion

 on Burkina Faso. Established in 2020, the VDPs are

locally and voluntarily recruited civilian auxiliaries

, provided with arms and military training, who support the national armed forces in defending communities against jihadist insurgent groups. Their

mobilisation was substantially expanded

 under Ibrahim Traoré after 2022.

author: Monthly Review Press
title: Chris dePloeg in conversation with Jason Hickel about “The Exterminating Empire”
content:
Pakuis de Zwijger

, Monday, November 23rd: :ive with Jason Hickel,

Ghassan Abu-Sittah

,

Harriët Bergman

,

Chihiro Geuzebroek

,

Max de Ploeg

 and the author!


In collaboration with In collaboration with Pijke ter Laak, join

Pakuis de Zwijger

 for a conversation with author Chris de Ploeg about his new book, a radical and urgent indictment of the global capitalist system and the imperial violence it unleashes upon people and planet alike. At its core, the book argues that genocide and ecocide are not tragic byproducts of capitalism – they are its fundamental features.


Together with renowned climate author Jason Hickel (in person), frontline Palestinian surgeon Ghassan Abu-Sittah (joining online) and our moderator, climate justice activist and researcher Harriët Bergman, we will dive deeper into the interconnections of the great challenges of our time–and more importantly, how to fight back. There will also be cultural performances from Chihiro Geuzebroek and brothers Chris and Max de Ploeg, tying their ancestral struggles in Bolivia and Armenia to the global struggle for liberation.

REGISTER HERE!


REVIEWS:


Morning Star

:

 “How did such a horror come to pass?” by Alex Hall


“

The Exterminating Empire

 began life as a Master’s thesis, nurtured into book form by Jason Hickel — the degrowth economist and author of The Divide, who contributes the foreword. The mentorship was well placed and De Ploeg has produced an impressively searing panorama of our global predicament…”


Counterpunch

, “

Resisting Annihilation: Reviewing “The Exterminating Empire”

, by Seth Sandronsky


“…de Ploeg, who does far more than compile lists of atrocities, draws parallels between the American holocaust of the native inhabitants’ relations with buffaloes and Israel’s genocide against Palestinians and their farming of olive trees. Land theft and separating those living on the land from it are nothing new. The author has skin in the game, given his family survived the Armenian genocide and Nazi holocaust…”


Counterpunch

, “

Capitalism is Waging War on Palestine While Creating a Burning Planet

” by Daniel Falcone:


Daniel Falcone:

What is the central argument of

The Exterminating Empire

 and how is the book structured? It looks as though the book serves as an intervention as well as an addition to current scholarship.  


Chris Kaspar de Ploeg:

 I open the book with some jarring facts that seem paradoxical at first sight. We need about 30 percent of our productive capacity to

give everyone on the planet a good life

. Not just the basics like housing, clothing and healthcare, but also modern appliances like refrigerators, laptops, access to the internet and more. At the same time, that standard of living is denied to about

80 percent of the world population

. Green energy has been cheaper than fossil fuels for years, yet climate breakdown is only accelerating. We could

solve world hunger

 with about 0.03 percent of global GDP, but hunger is only increasing.


That looks like an extraordinarily wasteful system, and it is. The point, however, is that under capitalism, these are not paradoxes at all. In fact, they are signs of capital’s success. Under our current economic system, the primary goal, ruthlessly pursued, is

profit maximization

. That profit maximization is reached through pushing down costs–and we are those costs, our labour, our environments, our lives–and by conquering markets, often through a mix of military and economic warfare. That essentially puts

capitalism on a warpath against life

. The system is working exactly as it is supposed to.


We see, for example, that profit rates are higher in the fossil fuel industry because it essentially

functions through monopolies

, despite the higher costs. We see that the military-industrial complex is growing exponentially, targeting any vestiges of resistance against

US-led global hegemony

, which globalized harsh budget cuts in social welfare, healthcare and education. These very conditions of

structural impoverishment

 then create the conditions of desperation necessary for people and countries to accept their status as sources for cheap labour, resources and land for global corporations, mostly centered in the Global North.


In the book I write about a dialectic between slavery and genocide, and between structural genocide and active genocide. A good way to understand that relationship is by going back to the

We Charge Genocide petition …

author: Unknown
title: Passer de la théorie à l'action : comment lutter contre le capitalisme énergétique vert ?
content:
Le capitalisme vert incarné par les énergies dites «

 

renouvelables

 

» est un impensé de la lutte pour la protection de l'environnement. Il repose sur une colonisation des consciences où la «

 

transition énergétique

 

» tient lieu de cheval de Troie pour faire accepter l'inacceptable : la destruction effective de l'environnement. Il est nécessaire de questionner ce mécanisme symbolique et de revenir à une lutte radicale et concrète contre l'exploitation humaine et des écosystèmes sous toutes ses formes.


Vantée sans relâche par les élites comme

LA

 solution au changement climatique, la transition énergétique est surtout

LA

 solution pour continuer à faire du «

 

business as usual

 

». Il est toujours question de faire du pognon en poursuivant la même logique d'extraction maximaliste des ressources naturelles. Malgré les beaux discours, la société thermo-industrielle se maintient en se «

 

greenwashant

 

». Plus pervers que le pétrole et le nucléaire, le photovoltaïque et l'éolien s'imposent par la colonisation des consciences avant celle des terres.


Penser les conséquences des énergies «

 

renouvelables

 

»


Face au bulldozer de la doxa de la transition énergétique, le chercheur Vincent Mignerot donne les bases d'une autodéfense intellectuelle. Assez rare pour être noté, Vincent Mignerot est

un chercheur autodidacte

 dont les thèses ont obtenu une forme de reconnaissance officielle par l'intelligentsia académique. Cette double caractéristique lui a donné la liberté nécessaire pour développer une pensée non-polluée par le préformatage universitaire et suffisamment étayée scientifiquement pour ne pas pouvoir être écartée d'un revers de la main par les mandarins des facs, les premiers chiens de garde du système dominant.


Vincent Mignerot est un penseur important, car il remet en cause le présupposé fondamental sur lequel repose la fiction de la transition énergétique :

les énergies «

 

renouvelables

 

» ne remplacent pas les énergies fossiles

. Au contraire, elles s'y ajoutent et ne font que faciliter l'exploitation des puits de pétrole jusqu'à la dernière goutte. On dilue le pétrole et le nucléaire avec les énergies «

 

renouvelables

 

» pour toujours plus de gabegies énergétiques :

SUV

 électriques,

IA

, cryptomonnaies… Plus de dope pour plus de junkies

 

!


Pour le dire de manière moins imagée : 30 ans de fable marketing sur les énergies «

 

renouvelables

 

» ne tiennent pas face à la

réalité mesurable

. La consommation d'énergie par habitant ne fait qu'augmenter et le bilan carbone fait de même. Pourtant, les énergies «

 

renouvelables

 

» se sont développées… pour le plus grand bénéfice de Total et compagnie (devenu TotalEnergies par volonté d'y associer la nouvelle poule aux œufs d'or «

 

renouvelables

 

»)

 

!


L'autre apport important de Vincent Mignerot est de considérer notre société capitaliste comme une société «

 

thermo-industrielle

 

», qui en conséquence répond aux lois de la thermodynamique, dont celle de l'entropie.


Quand

les thuriféraires de la transition énergétique

 évoquent des énergies «

 

renouvelables

 

», ils induisent dans la conscience collective l'idée d'un système fermé qui s'autoentretient et donc serait vertueux. Or, un panneau photovoltaïque ou une pale d'éolienne, ça s'use… «

 

Pas d'inquiétude

 

», vous répondront les transitionnistes, «

 

grâce au recyclage et à l'énergie produite par les autres éoliennes, on peut faire du neuf avec du vieux sans produire de

CO2

 

». Si le propos est volontairement caricatural par souci d'explicitation, il s'agit bien de l'idée qui se diffuse dans tous les cercles de la société capitaliste (

les partis politiques classés à gauche n'y échappant pas

), et sans remise en question.


C'est là que l'application par Vincent Mignerot des lois de la thermodynamique à notre société capitaliste permet de souligner une fausse impression. Dans le quotidien, le système capitaliste (occidental) apparaît très stable : il n'y a pas de manque d'énergie ou de ressources. Les prix peuvent être très élevés (par exemple celui de l'essence à cause de la guerre contre l'Iran déclenchée par Trump et Netanyahou), mais il n'y a pas de pénurie à l'échelle de la société (notre propos n'est pas ici d'aborder la question sous l'angle social et de la répartition des richesses au sein de la société, enjeu essentiel qui mérite une analyse à part entière).


En réalité, tout est dans la …

author: anarchist*innen
title: Deutschland-Griechenland: Reiseverbot und repressive Maßnahmen gegen Anarchist*innen
content:
Information bezüglich einer Ausreiseverweigerung, die am 22.11.26 durch die Bundespolizei gegen eine Person entschieden und durchgesetzt wurde.


Am Sonntag, den 22. November, wurde einer Person, die für die Demonstration in Gedenken an Kyriakos Xymitiris am 31.10.2025 in Athen angeklagt ist, die Ausreise aus Deutschland verweigert. Sein Reisepass wurde abgenommen und eine Meldeauflage für den 24. November in einer Berliner Polizeistation erlassen. Dadurch war ihm die Teilnahme an seinem eigenen Prozess im Gericht Evelpidon in Athen am 24. November nicht möglich. Eine andere Person, Halterin eines griechischen Passes, welche mit ihm hätte fliegen sollen, wurde ebenso von der Bundespolizei an der Ausreise gehindert.


Die Geschehnisse trugen sich am Frankfurter Flughafen zu, wo zunächst die andere Person nach der Passkontrolle dazu aufgefordert wurde, mit zur Polizeistation des Flughafens zu kommen. Zusammen kamen die zwei Gefährt*innen zur Station, wo sie getrennt wurden und alle Sachen durchsucht wurden. Der Person, die angeblich nicht Ziel der Polizeimaßnahme war, wurde gesagt, dass die Polizei die Absicht hätte, eine Nackt- und auch Rektaluntersuchung durchzuführen. Die Verweigerung der Kooperation und die Forderung eines Gerichtsbeschlusses für dieses Vorgehen führte dazu, dass der leitende Beamte von der Entscheidung absah, nur um als Grund anzugeben, dass er dies tue, da er eine Kooperation der Person für das noch anstehende Verfahren erwarte.


Dann wurden beide Personen getrennt voneinander zum Verhör gebracht, welches der Entscheidung darüber dienen sollte, ob sie das Recht zur Ausreise hätten.


Der Person, die ursprünglich Ziel der polizeilichen Aktion war, wurde kurz ein Schrieb in griechischer Sprache mit dem übersetzten Titel „Belehrung von Personen bei präventiven freiheitsentziehenden/-beschränkenden Maßnahmen“ gezeigt. Darin war als Grund angekreuzt: „Identitätsfeststellung oder Überprüfung der Berechtigung zum Grenzübertritt“. Die Polizei fragte nach dem Grund der Reise nach Athen. Die Person machte keine Angaben außer dem Zeigen ihres griechischen Passes. Die Polizei entschied dann offenbar, die Ausreise nicht offiziell zu verbieten und lies sie gehen ohne eine rechtliche Erklärung zu machen oder eine offizielle Entscheidung zu verkünden. Dies geschah zu einem Zeitpunkt als das Gate zum Flugzeug nach Athen schon geschossen und das Boarding nicht mehr möglich war.


Der anderen Person übergab die Polizei einen Schrieb auf Deutsch mit dem selben Titel wie oben genannt und zusätzlich ein vierseitiges Dokument, welches die Absicht der Polizei erklärte, ihm die Ausreise in jedes andere Land bis zum 24. November um 24:00 zu untersagen. Weiter wurde darin die Absicht genannt, ihm eine Meldeauflage für den 24. November in einer Polizeistation in Berlin Friedrichshain aufzuerlegen. Im Falle einer Nicht-Einhaltung sollte eine Strafe von 100 Euro anfallen.


Der wesentliche Teil der vier Seiten Text beschrieb die Begründung der Polizei für ihre Absichten. Hier eine Zusammenfassung der Formulierungen aus der Feder der Polizei:


-nach polizeilicher Information gibt es eine Ankündigung einer “Solidaritätsversammlung für inhaftierte, flüchtige und verfolgte Aktivistinnen und Aktivisten”1 für den 24.11., bei welcher es sich um eine Versammlung des gewaltorientierten, griechischen Anarchistmus handelt


-diese Veranstaltung is öffentlich auf athens.indymedia.org angekündigt


-Veranstaltungen, die in der Vergangenheit auf athens.indymedia.org angekündigt wurden, führten meistens zu Ausschreitungen gegenüber Einsatzkräften und zu einer lokalen, nationalen und internationalen Berichterstattung


-als Beispiel wird die Gedenkveranstaltung für Kyriakos Xymitiris am 31.10.2026 genannt, wo es in den letzten Jahren zu verschiedensten Straftaten (eine längere Aufzählung folgt) kam


-polizeiliche Informationen über den Gefährten, insbesondere eine lange Liste an verschiedensten Straftatbeständen (für die er niemals verurteilt oder auch nur offiziell beschuldigt wurde)


-polizeiliche Informationen über einige politische Veranstaltungen, auf denen er gesehen wurde


-Annahmen darüber, dass er Teil einer in Berlin agierenden Struktur ist, die sich einerseits auf die Ereignisse des 31. Oktober 2024, Kyriakos Xymitiris und die Anarchist*innen Marianna Manoura und Dimitra Zarafeta bezieht, andererseits mit der Rigaer94 in Verbindung steht

title: T'es exploité·e ? Arrête. / Une émission de Minuit Décousu
content:
Cette semaine, on en découd avec l'exploitation et le travail. On cause travail gratuit, travail bénévole, travail du sexe et anarchisme avec le

projet Évasions

 et plein d'autres choses !


"

Le travailleureuse vend sa force de travail à un patron, en échange d'un salaire, qu'il ou elle est contraint de faire, parce qu'on ne possède pas les moyens de production, genre les outils, l'usine pour produire des trucs, les terres pour cultiver, un parc immobilier à louer... Bref, quand le seul truc qu'on possède c'est sa force de travail, bah on l'échange contre un salaire, qui nous permet de bouffer, de se loger, de se payer un peu de fun en vacances ou au bar, et d'élever ses enfants qui pourrint à leur tour vendre leur force de travail et perpétuer le capitalisme.

"


150 ans après les premières définitions marxistes, le concept d'exploitation pur jus a un peu bougé. La théorie de la valeur travail a été contestée, on a aussi dit que l'exploitation ne pouvait pas se réduire au travail de production, ou que le tout donnait une vision trop simplifiée du monde du travail. C'est pourquoi cette semaine, Minuit Décousu a choisi d'en découdre avec l'exploitation et le travail pour voir que ces définitions ont pu être retravaillées à plein d'endroits, élargies et approfondies. Dans cette émission, tu pourras entendre :


 Il était une fois... le Capital

 Dépasser le misérabilisme et l'empowerment, l'anarchisme et le travail du sexe (entretien avec le Projet Évasions*)

 Le travail du sexe, une fuite du salariat vers les interstices ? (*)

 Le travail gratuit est-il toujours de l'exploitation ?

 S'affranchir des injonctions sur la sexualité et le genre (*)

 Bien cordialement


L'émission s'écoute sur notre

audioblog

,


, et un peu partout en podcast. Bonne écoute !


Un gros big up au

projet Évasions

 pour leur entretien et pour les travaux ! La brochure Illégale Élégance, parue cette année, est dispo sur

leur site internet

.


Minuit Décousu, c'est un fanzine radiophonique nocturne sur

Radio Canut

 (Lyon et alentours),

Radio Vassivière

 (Limousin) et

Cause Commune

 (Paris/IDF). Semaine après semaine pendant une heure, on en découd avec la nuit et on tire les fils de sons, de textes, d'archives et de voix qui s'entremêlent.

author: Unknown
title: Секретными свидетелями в деле анархиста Бориса Дубкова стали двое его знакомых, которые предложили ему поджечь военкомат
content:
Анархист Борис Дубков перед задержанием обсуждал поджог военкомата с двумя знакомыми, которые позже стали секретными свидетелями под псевдонимами «Екатерина Морозова» и «Жак Фреско». В деле есть стенограммы их разговоров, узнала «Медиазона».

23-летний студент медицинского колледжа из Москвы Борис Дубков обвиняется в покушении на теракт, обороте взрывчатки, изготовлении взрывных устройств и обучении террористической деятельности. Ему вменяют попытку поджога районного военкомата в Аксае Ростовской области в июне 2025 года. Дело рассматривает Южный окружной военный суд.

Дубков приехал из Москвы в Ростов-на-Дону 11 июня 2025 года, по его словам, чтобы увидеться с новыми знакомыми, которых он знал как Екатерину Морозову и Жака Фреско. Согласно показаниям Дубкова в суде, именно они уговорили его принять участие в поджоге Аксайского районного военкомата. «12 июня мы окончательно пришли к выводу, что совершим акцию: я, Катя и Жак», — говорил молодой человек.

Разговоры Дубкова с «Морозовой» и «Жаком Фреско» записывались на диктофон, следует из справок о результатах ОРМ «Наблюдение», которые огласили в суде 25 ноября.

Согласно стенограммам этих записей, Дубков накануне поджога «провел разведку местности», купил петарды «Пулеметная лента» в ростовском магазине пиротехники «Веселая затея» и приготовил пять коктейлей Молотова. Какую роль в подготовке акции сыграли два секретных свидетеля, в справках не говорится; в суде «Морозову» и «Жака Фреско» пока не допрашивали.

Сам Дубков объяснял, что «решение бросать бутылки с бензином — даже не коктейли Молотова — было принято спонтанно, заранее никак не обдумывалось, не обговаривалось. Я пытался их отговорить — у меня это не получилось. В ходе нашего разговора я только сильнее убедился, что тоже хочу совершить акцию».

Дубкова задержали в Аксае ночью 16 июня 2025 года. В рюкзаке у анархиста нашли дымный порох «массой не менее 29,41 грамма» в банке, несколько камней и стеклянные осколки со следами бензина — вероятно, от бутылок, разбившихся при задержании. Кроме того, перед несостоявшейся акцией молодой человек спрятал в тайнике четыре ленты петард, один коктейль Молотова и телефон.

Дубков признал вину в обороте взрывчатки и изготовлении зажигательных устройств, а также покушении на теракт, но без «умысла на лишение жизни охранника». «Нашей задачей была дестабилизация военкомата и устрашение правящих органов», — уточнил он.

«Сожалею о том, что это ловушка оказалась», — сказал Дубков.

В апреле Южный окружной военный суд вынес приговор по другому делу о подготовке к поджогу военкомата в Ростове-на-Дону, ключевую роль в котором сыграли показания засекреченной свидетельницы «Вероники Беловой». «Медиазона» выяснила, что завербованная ФСБ девушка присутствовала при планировании поджога, покупала бензин для коктейлей Молотова и сопровождала будущих обвиняемых вплоть до задержания. В итоге ростовчане Иван Благодатских и Илья Кудинов получили 9 и 10 лет, а приехавший из Москвы Ахмед Рамалданов — 8 лет строгого режима.

344082, Ростовская область, Ростов-на-Дону, ул. Большая Садовая, д. 31

title: Neuigkeiten von der Antimilitaristischen Versammlung Wedding (AMAW)
content:
[english below]


Als „Antimilitaristische Versammlung Wedding“ treffen wir uns nun schon seit einiger Zeit im anarchistischen Raum Radau. Wir versuchen, unsere offene Versammlung  auf horizontale und antiautoritäre Weise zu gestalten.


Einen Kilometer von hier entfernt hat Rheinmetall mit der Produktion von Komponenten für Panzermunition, Artilleriesysteme, gepanzerte Fahrzeuge und – wie kürzlich bekannt wurde – Teilen für Kamikaze-Drohnen für Israel begonnen. Teile, klein, aber tödlich, einer größeren Maschine: des andauernden kolonialen und völkermörderischen Projekts, das Krieg nutzt, um Gewinne zu erzielen.


Für diejenigen, die sich dem Kampf gegen Kriege, Besatzung und Militarisierung sowie gegen die erschreckende Normalisierung des seit drei Jahren live übertragenen Völkermords an den Palästinenser*innen anschließen, ist Repression keine Frage des „Ob“, sondern des „Wann“. Während die Technologien der Repression immer ausgefeilter werden, sind ihre Taktiken altbekannt: Einschüchterung, Überwachung, Misshandlung und Inhaftierung. Die Darstellung von Gefährt*innen als „Extremist*innen“ und Gefahr für die Gesellschaft. Dieselbe Gesellschaft, die jetzt aufgefordert wird und später gezwungen sein wird, ihre Kinder in den Krieg zu schicken. Die alte Geschichte von „bösen Militanten“ gegen die „guten Bürger*innen“ bröckelt.


Seit der Razzia im März schleichen Zivilpolizist*innen bei fast jeder öffentlichen Versammlung von AMAW vor der Tür der Bibliothek „Radau“ herum. Insbesondere die PMS-Beamten haben unsere Räume und öffentlichen Veranstaltungen wiederholt mit ihrer widerwärtigen Präsenz belästigt. Eine Präsenz, die Teil einer umfassenderen Praxis der Überwachung, Einschüchterung und des ständigen Versuchs ist, diejenigen zu kontrollieren und Terror unter denen zu verbreiten, die Widerstand leisten.


Wer ist schuldig am Tod Tausender Menschen weltweit durch Krieg, Enteignung und von Menschen verursachte Katastrophen?


Wir lehnen das Konzept der Schuld angesichts globaler Kriege und Verwüstungen ab. Wir sind nicht schuldig, aber wir sind alle Kompliz*innen im Kampf gegen Unterdrückung!


Die Polizei geht in der ganzen Stadt gegen antimilitaristische Aktivitäten vor – erst kürzlich hat sie Schüler*innen und Studierende vor ihren Schulen und Universitäten zusammengeschlagen und festgenommen, weil sie sich gegen ihr eigenes Gemetzel gewehrt haben. Der Terror der Repression hat sich verschärft und richtet sich als Teil einer Aufstandsbekämpfungsstrategie gegen immer mehr Gefährt*innen und politische Räume. Dies ist weder eine Angelegenheit, die nur ein bestimmtes politisches Milieu betrifft, noch ist es einfach nur eine weitere „Episode“ in der alltäglichen Konfrontation zwischen Anarchist*innen und dem Staat. Auch wenn die repressiven Mechanismen des Staates ihren erklärten Feind vielleicht mit größerer Intensität und Offenheit ins Visier nehmen, betrifft diese repressive Politik doch alle, die kämpfen und Widerstand leisten.


Der Staat und die Polizei werden Solidarität, Selbstorganisation und Kollektivität gegen sich vorfinden. Sie werden uns gemeinsam finden, wie wir uns der Repression widersetzen und ihr Gewaltmonopol praktisch in Frage stellen.


Wir werden unsere öffentlichen Aktionen und unseren Kampf gegen eine Welt voller Spitzel und Ungerechtigkeit nicht einstellen. Wir widersetzen uns der täglichen Gewalt von Staaten und Herren, Grenzen und Gefängnissen, Razzien und Einschüchterungen – wir begrüßen die Gewalt der Unterdrückten!


—


News from the Anti-Militarist Assembly Wedding


As the Anti-Militarist Assembly Wedding we have been meeting in the infoladen for some time now. Our open assembly attempts to be a horizontal, and anti-authoritarian procedure.


One kilometer from here, Rheinmetall produces components for tank ammunitions, artillery systems, armored vehicles and – as recently revealed – parts of kamikaze drones for Israel. Parts, small but deadly, of a bigger machine: the ongoing colonial and genocidal project that uses war to turn in profits.


For those who join the struggle against wars, occupation and militarization, and against the normalization of three years of live-streamed genocide against the Palestinians, repression is not a matter of if but when. While the technologies of repression become more sophisticated, its tactics are old: intimidation, surveillance, abuse and incarceration. Portraying comrades as „extremists“ and a danger to society. author: Thunderbird
title: Will anarchist book fairs remain safe spaces for anarchists?
content:
The context of the incident at the anarchist book fair in Brno (so-called Czech Republic).


Author


pocketedition.nublogs.org


    Submitted by

Thunderbird

 on November 23, 2026


On October 3, 2026, at the Anarchist Book Fair in Brno

1


, a person collaborating with Pocket Edition

2


 was subjected to aggressive behavior by a member of the Brno-based AFA group and several other individuals. It was clear from the aggressors’ statements that their intention was to physically assault the person in question, intimidate them, and force them to leave the book fair. Similar incidents have also occurred in the past at a concert at Club 007

3


 and at the Book Fair in Prague

4


. In our view, therefore, this is not an isolated incident, but a deeper and long-standing problem that cannot be dismissed as a trivial dispute.


We cannot expect the responsibility for resolving this problem to fall solely on the direct participants in these dramatic situations or on the groups that organize the events where such incidents occurred. Although the prompt and empathetic response of the Brno Book Fair’s organizing team helped mitigate the effects of the aggression this time and ensure that the victim had a safe haven from the aggressors, we believe that a comprehensive solution to this problem must also include, in the future, the active participation of the public attending book fairs and the entire anarchist movement, which presents such events as a significant part of its own safety infrastructure. Therefore, this statement is a public call to action, not a message addressed only to a narrow circle of specific individuals.


Brief Description of the Conflict at the Anarchist Book Fair in Brno


The person who was attacked at the book fair in Brno was helping to handle technical matters at the Pocket Edition booth. The organizing team had provided this project with a space to display its publications, and it was listed on the website among the participants and distributors. In the early evening, in the courtyard, a person associated with AFA very rudely and literally ordered the person in question to leave the book fair, claiming he had no business being there. It was evident from his verbal remarks and “body language” that he was determined to escalate his behavior to physical aggression. However, other people present prevented the physical assault.


The person who was attacked responded with a loud statement: “You’re invading my personal space, and I feel threatened. Back off and stop communicating with me aggressively.” The aggressor replied, “I don’t give a damn about your personal space.” This was followed by further verbal aggression and an attempt to physically attack the victim who then moved from the courtyard inside the building to the Pocket Edition distribution table. The aggressor immediately followed them, along with several slightly less aggressive individuals. The most active aggressor continued to intimidate and threaten physical assault. Together with the others, he justified his behavior with speculative accusations that we’ve heard before, but we don’t know of anyone who has helped clarify what happened and/or who initiated it.


“Police officers” without uniforms and “judges” without robes


Accusing and punishing someone based on speculation presented as fact is a despicable practice we know all too well from the police, prosecutors, and judges. However, the so-called anarchists and anti-fascists mentioned here take this practice to an even more extreme level. Unlike our institutional enemies, they do not rely on expert analyses or forensic science, nor do they seek factual evidence to clarify events. It is enough for them if someone says, “That person placed a fake explosive at the festival” or “This person sent a threatening message to someone online under a false name.” All it takes is to say such things, and the “court case” is immediately closed without anyone having to prove anything concrete. The person against whom the accusation is made is immediately deemed guilty and ready for punishment. title: Aydın Ekmek ve Gül’den 25 Kasım Paneli: Kadınların mücadelesi ve dayanışması büyüyor
content:
Aydın Ekmek ve Gül grubu, 22 Kasım’da saat 14.00’te Milli Aydın Bankası’nda, 25 Kasım Kadına Şiddete Karşı Uluslararası Mücadele Günü öncesinde panel düzenledi. Panelde kadınlar; şiddete, cezasızlığa, eşitsizliğe ve sömürüye karşı bir araya geldi.

Panelin açılış konuşmasını Aydın Ekmek ve Gül’den Şükriye Karalar yaptı. Karalar, 25 Kasım Kadına Yönelik Şiddete Karşı Uluslararası Mücadele Günü’nün tarihsel önemine değinerek Mirabel Kardeşlerden bugüne miras kalan mücadeleyi anlattı. Kadınların yıllardır sürdürdüğü eşitlik, özgürlük ve yaşam hakkı mücadelesinin önemini vurguladı.

Kadınların yoğun katılım gösterdiği panelde Avukat İlgin Ceribaş ve Sosyal Hizmet Uzmanı Hilal Yılmaz konuşmacı olarak yer aldı.

Avukat İlgin Ceribaş, şüpheli kadın ölümleri üzerinden cezasızlık politikasını ele aldı. Kadın ölümlerinin aydınlatılması, sorumluların ortaya çıkarılması ve adaletin sağlanması konusunda yaşanan sorunlara dikkat çekti.

Sosyal hizmet uzmanı Hilal Yılmaz ise kadınların ve çocukların karşı karşıya kaldığı olumsuz yaşam koşullarını somut örneklerle anlattı. Kadınların ve çocukların yaşadığı sorunların toplumsal boyutuna ve sosyal destek mekanizmalarının önemine değindi.

Panelde söz alan bir kadın arkadaşımız, Digel Tekstil ve Temel Conta işçilerinin direnişlerinden örnekler vererek işçi kadınların işyerlerinde yaşadıkları sorunlara dikkat çekti. Kadınların çalışma yaşamında karşılaştıkları eşitsizlikler, hak gaspları ve mücadele deneyimleri de panelin önemli başlıklarından biri oldu.

Panel, kadınların soruları, katkıları ve karşılıklı paylaşımlarıyla devam etti. Katılımcılar hem kendi deneyimlerini paylaşma hem de merak ettikleri konularda sorularını yöneltme fırsatı buldu.

Panelde şu ifadelere yer verildi:

“Aydın Ekmek ve Gül olarak bir kez daha vurguluyoruz: Kadınların yaşam hakkı, eşitlik ve özgürlük mücadelesi birbirinden ayrılamaz. Evde, sokakta ve işyerinde kadınların karşılaştığı şiddete, eşitsizliğe ve sömürüye karşı mücadelemizi büyütüyoruz. Mirabel Kardeşlerden bugüne uzanan mücadele tarihimizden aldığımız güçle kadın dayanışmasını büyütmeye devam edeceğiz. Yaşamak için ekmek, ruhumuz için gül istiyoruz!”

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Graham Purchase - Kropotkin and the Rise of Revolutionary Anarchism
content:
Author

: Graham Purchase

Title

: Kropotkin and the Rise of Revolutionary Anarchism

Subtitle

: Review

Date

: 2001, April

Source

: Scanned from Anarcho-Syndicalist Review 31 (April 2001)


 a review of


 Kropotkin and the Rise of Revolutionary Anarchism 1872-1886, by Caroline Cahm, Cambridge University Press, 1989.


 This excellent work of modern scholarship focuses upon a specific period of Kropotkin's life, 1872-1886, during which he was intensely involved in the development and propagation of European anarchism, through his actions, speeches and articles. This period of intense activism lies between Kropotkin's earlier involvement with Russian populism and his long exile in England, where he wrote the many longer books for which he remains famous today.


 During these years he travelled widely throughout Western Europe, living for long periods in Switzerland (expelled 1881) and France, where he was imprisoned for three years (1883-6). Kropotkin's travels to countries with strong anarchist movements such as Belgium and Spain influenced his thinking. He also participated in anarchist conferences in Switzerland, Germany and London.


 His achievements during this period were many and varied. Shortly after arriving in Switzerland he enthusiastically took part in a demonstration involving illegally carrying the red flag in honor of the Paris Commune. The success of the Berne demonstration rejuvenated, for a short time, the Jura federation which had fallen into decline since the death of Bakunin and his own internment in a Russian prison. This point in time also saw the beginning of Kropotkin's journalistic career. He contributed quite a number of articles to the Bulletin of the Jura Federation of the IWA during 1876-7. These articles were never published in English, nor since republished in French.


 The value of Cahm's study is that it thoroughly examines important themes within this early journalism. Eminent scholars of Kropotkin, such as Martin Miller, regard Kropotkin's writings for the Bulletin and Rebel as some of his "best" and most "neglected." This neglect is a pity, for although about half of his contributions to the Bulletin were reports upon Russian affairs, primarily the trial of 1893, the other half include interesting and important contributions upon the ills of imperialism, parliamentary socialism and Marxism, a three-part analysis of the ills of British unionism, and articles upon U.S. labor issues.


 In 1879, following the collapse of the Bulletin and L'Avant Garde (to which he contributed one article on the Pittsburgh strikes), Kropotkin founded, edited and contributed to a new newspaper, Rebel (Le Revolte), published at Geneva until 1885. Although Kropotkin's first political book Words of a Rebel (Paris 1885, edited and compiled by Reclus), contains a very readable selection of the leading articles from the Rebel, there are a few, particularly concerning unionism which might also have been reasonably included. There are also other minor articles, such as those dealing with the value and desirability of direct-action strike tactics as a method of reversing reformist parliamentary unionism in Britain and France, which are also of interest in this respect. Again Cahm, in focusing attention upon his neglected works upon the subject of reformist and revolutionary unionism, provides a valuable resource upon which to better assess Kropotkin's thinking upon these issues. This scholarship is very valuable as his complex and interesting viewpoints concerning syndicalism, unionism and anarchism have been obscured by anarchist-communist scholars with anti-syndicalist prejudices.


 Towards the end of the period under review (1872-1886) Kropotkin took a central role in the defence at the Lyon Trial of 1883, which led to the imprisonment for several years of most of France's leading anarchists, including Kropotkin himself, in a farcical display of state-justice, which, for a short time at least, led to widespread public sympathy for the prisoners and what they stood for. The imprisonment of the most active anarchists and the subsequent intense state repression of the movement meant that little remained upon his release in 1886 when he began his long exile from continental Europe in England, where he could no longer take an active part in its affairs (though he helped found and finance two subsequent French-language newspapers to which he contributed scores of articles over the next 30 years).

author: Julius Gavroche
title: Anarchism, The Star of the Antipodes
content:
by Christian Ferrer


Revista Ají

, 24/05/2020


Nothing is more mysterious than the fate of anarchism, an ideal that might seem far-fetched were it not for the fact that it is extremely sensible. Although the passage of time has dimmed its lustre, and it was even declared extinct, the “libertarian cause” has continued to demonstrate its tenacity, as anarchists seem to possess the qualities of the phoenix – the ability to be reborn from their own ashes – like avatars that are reincarnated in various neighbouring spheres and offshoots. The anarchist ideal, while once politically and culturally prominent, remains incomprehensible in our times unless one first turns the world upside down. In truth, anarchy has always had a bad press—right from the start—: a “utopia”; a messianic call, then, something wild, at times otherworldly, always piercing.


Do as you please, live as you would like people to live in the future, do not join the military, do not eat animal carcasses, you are the king’s enemy, abhor prisons, glorify sex, stand your ground, do not obey or give orders, do not humiliate and do not let yourself be humiliated, do not leave a comrade in the lurch, better an outcast than a leader, you may take sides and be part of the action but do not form a party, borders are false and the law a fiction exploited by the powerful, love is free and long live loss. Such are the slogans, or counterbalances, the decalogue of antagonism and wonder. As for the anarchists, they were said to be scarecrows, and at times the label was deserved.


It is pointless to weigh up their actions, ups and downs, and achievements solely by the yardstick that measures success or failure, because the very fact that “the Idea” – as they called the sum of their principles – has appeared in the world remains a mystery of history. It does not seem a natural occurrence. Generally speaking, even if reluctantly, people come to terms with the world as it is, soothing their inevitable unease with benefits, subsidies and a few public holidays throughout the gruelling working year. Few are those who seek to turn it on its head in the blink of an eye. Pyramids, too, are built to be climbed, not to be torn down, stone by stone. Anarchism can be seen as an unusual, forceful and unyielding response to the existence of powers separate from the community, no less than to the obstacles and prohibitions placed in the way of the will to personal self-creation—in short, to everything that discourages or derails the mad desire to live, and that is precisely why the anarchist creed advocated a multifaceted revolution: cultural, psychological and political all at once. It was to ask a great deal; it was to be overly rational; it was to live without fear, with or without organisation; it was to enjoy the feast, in unity, at least while the affinity lasted. No more than that, no less than that.


From the very beginnings of anarchism, when Proudhon, Bakunin and Kropotkin laid the foundations, various branches and offshoots very quickly emerged, each emphasising, in its own way, different aspects: mutualism, collectivism, free love, concern for the fate of nature, vegetarianism, trade unionism, individualism, religiosity without established churches, spontaneism, women’s emancipation, morality without dogma, experimental communes and a number of other challenges that, in their day, seemed risky, if not “flowers of evil”: a scent at times sharp, at others sensual, always diverse and inventive. It is also worth highlighting anarchism’s ability to influence people, ideas and groups—and sometimes crowds—who did not necessarily identify as anarchists but who felt ‘”called” to sympathise with these principles or to reconsider their own convictions. In every case, hierarchical power was regarded as a human catastrophe, an enemy of lives that might otherwise have been less oppressed.


The opponents of anarchism are well known: the clergy, the powerful, the military, the employers, the “patriots”, those in power – not to mention the communists, their old enemies from before the now-forgotten Soviet Union even existed. These opponents knew that libertarian thought emphasised issues and problems that could not be resolved within the system of domination as it stood, including, amongst others, its very early critique of technology and industrialism, its warnings about ecological excesses, its exhortations to break away from failed emotional relationships, its advocacy of sexual …

author: Freedom Editor
title: Microscopic mutual aid
content:
From the deepest root to the highest leaf and every acorn, bacteria and fungi cooperate with each other and their host to survive

1.8 billion years ago the mitochondria, “the powerhouse of the cell,” moved within a host cell for protection. Neither side was exploited, and equilibrium was achieved. To this day, DNA is segregated between the mitochondria and the nucleus reminding us of cellular cooperation.

In her work, On the Origin of Mitosing Cells (1967), Lynn Margulis posited that structures such as the mitochondria originated from smaller specialised cells taking refuge within larger cells. 60 years after Kropotkin, Margulis’ Endosymbiotic Theory challenged the expectations of Darwinian evolution and was rejected by 15 journals. Endosymbiosis is now a respected cornerstone of evolutionary biology.

Our cells and ecosystems exemplify cooperation, not competition. Mutual aid is the biochemical basis of multicellular life meeting required energy demands; the mitochondria was a volunteer, but now it is part of the cooperative powerhouse of the cell(s).

I research microbiomes of terrestrial plants, using advanced molecular techniques to untangle form and function in microscopic communities.

Mutual aid has been the foundation of my research. From the deepest root to the highest leaf and every acorn, bacteria and fungi cooperate with each other and their host to survive, ward off disease, and improve overall wellbeing. If natural selection is the play, molecular mutual aid is the stage, the lights, the assistant, the director, and the crowd.

Microbiomes are complex systems that include beneficial, neutral or pathogenic individuals. As scientific knowledge expands, we are beginning to understand that the difference between a beneficial and detrimental microbe could be triggered by environmental stress. The shift is not governed by a central mechanism, but by a quorum of functionally cooperative bacteria following a unifying imperative: “common survival at all costs”.

Capitalism is fundamentally Darwinian: proliferate or perish, outcompete your rivals, grow exponentially. However, bacteria have shown us that natural selection is not exponential, and neither should be our methods of measuring economic progress.

The Escherichia coli (E. coli) Long-Term Evolution Experiment (LTEE) is the clearest demonstration of natural selection to date. Founded by Richard Lenski of Michigan State University in 1988, LTEE has observed the equivalent of more than 2,000,000 years of human evolution over 75,000 generations taking advantage of the rapid rate of replication in E. coli. Every day 1% fractions of the previous community are transferred into fresh medium; each day represents more than six generations.

Using molecular techniques, the group was able to track the rate of evolution within their E. coli lineages. They predicted that rate of evolution would be hyperbolic: a period of exponential development followed by a plateau, an upper ceiling. However, it was discovered that there is no upper ceiling. Exponential improvement in E. coli fitness is succeeded by incremental developments. Adaptations become exponentially rarer but never cease.

Put simply, evolutionary adaptations become less dramatic, the return on investment diminishes as the E. coli was already adapted to a cosy temperature of 37°C for the equivalent of 2,000,000 human years.

On our own, human scale, we have seen epochs of exponential growth, such as the industrial or agricultural revolutions, where outputs were tangible and material. Accelerationists wish you to believe that the incessant integration of the latest greatest technology – currently AI – will usher in a new revolution despite diminishing returns. But we are already at the point of diminishing returns. Why are data centres becoming larger instead of smaller and more efficient? Why is my chocolate bar shrinking? Culturally, how much did music change between 1960-90, compared to between 1990-2020?

I have seen in my own data that pathogenic fungi are often present and quantifiable up to 25% of community composition, but no signs of disease are present. Certainly, there are outright pathogens that cause disease. But if you placed them in a hermetically sealed box with their host, their long-term existence is not feasible. They infect, they multiply, the host dies, their population dies after consuming all the resources.

Exponential growth of a singular microbe is the hallmark of disease, and we …

content:
Mardi 8 décembre de 19h à 21h, table Ronde avec Verónica Chávez, Beatriz Perea et Oriana Mora. À la Bourse du Travail - 3 rue du Château d'eau - Paris 10

e


Le 8 décembre 2026, nous avons l'honneur d'accueillir Verónica Chávez, figure majeure de la lutte des peuples autochtones, ainsi que Beatriz Perea et Oriana Mora, trois défenseuses des territoires venues d'Argentine et du Chili, qui partageront les réalités difficiles auxquelles leurs communautés sont confrontées, mais aussi la dignité de leurs luttes et de leurs résistances.


Elles viennent en Europe pour porter la lutte qu'elles mènent dans ce que l'on appelle le triangle du lithium, entre l'Argentine, le Chili et la Bolivie, où se déroule une nouvelle offensive coloniale sur les territoires des peuples autochtones.


Cette offensive se présente sous les habits de la transition énergétique, au service d'une économie qui prétend devenir «

 

verte

 

» sans pour autant renoncer au pillage.


Les territoires autochtones de cette région sont une fois de plus transformés en zones de sacrifice, où l'eau qui fait vivre les populations, la mémoire ancestrale et l'avenir de communautés entières sont subordonnés aux intérêts de ceux qui ne voient dans ces terres que des minerais stratégiques pour la transition énergétique.


La justice globale ne naît pas des discours des puissants, mais de la rencontre entre les peuples qui résistent.

author: Emma Honeybun
title: Plan to decolonize Manitoba’s child welfare system is a big task that will take time, says minister
content:
The director of Manitoba’s child advocacy office says that improving the current child welfare system needs a new approach that places control back to First Nations families.

However, doing so while First Nations are also struggling with a lack of resources and community spaces for the kids to thrive presents its own set of challenges.

“Decolonization is a huge undertaking,” said Sherry Gott, a member of Sapotaweyak Cree Nation who has been working in child welfare education for more than 30 years. “That means we must dismantle systems that have continued to colonize our people.”

Gott is the executive director of Manitoba’s Advocate for Children and Youth (MACY), a non-partisan social work office funded by the province. On Nov. 18, it published its latest annual report, which, among other findings, indicated that 53 per cent of serious injuries involving youth (aged 0 to 20) that resulted in a report were caused by sexual assault.

She said her “dream” would be an outcome where a typical CFS wouldn’t be necessary, because First Nations would have the resources necessary to support children who may be in crisis, but that those resources are currently hard to come by.

“We have to believe that we have the knowledge to be able to look at the system in a way where it supports our families,” Gott said. “So we also have to believe that we have traditional knowledge that is valuable. We must believe that we have the answers to support our families to thrive.”

According to the latest report from MACY, the agency doesn’t have the resources to keep up with a growing number of children in crisis.

She said the resources MACY currently needs the most is adequate staffing, and that the shortage can be “really taxing on our mental health, when you look at what comes through the door.”

“Issues of sexual exploitation and abuse is a really, really difficult subject to deal with. And when you have a name behind that incident, then you start to know who the family is and who the children are, who’s involved, it gets even more personal,” Gott continued. “Because you have names attached to it, and communities, Nations, where these children come from. So it is really hard to work daily at that level … It’s hard on our staff. But we try our best to keep their mental health and well-being in check.”

According to the report, the office received 506 referrals from April 2025 to March 2026, but only 300 were able to be reviewed, according to the legal definition of a serious injury.

Because of the demand, only 135 of the 300 referrals legally eligible for review have ended with complete serious injury reports, as of writing. Only 99 were assessed for potential investigation, and 36 of those assessments were reviewed further.

According to the 2025-2026 annual report from the office of provincial Minister of Families Nahanni Fontaine, 80 per cent of children in care are First Nations.

Similarly, Gott said that approximately 80 per cent of children represented in MACY’s serious injury reports are Indigenous.

MACY also completed 60 child death reports in 2025-26, although there were 71 in scope for a review.

Sixty-eight per cent of the children in the completed reports were Indigenous, and 98 per cent of the reports were linked to CFS.

The most recent reported death in care is five-year-old Baileigh Berens in Winnipeg. Baileigh had autism and was non-verbal, but had no known health conditions and her cause of death has not been determined. She was found in a dryer.

The Assembly of Manitoba Chiefs (AMC), which represents all 63 First Nations in Manitoba, held a sacred fire for the child at her mother’s house Wednesday evening.

Following the release of MACY’s annual report, AMC Grand Chief Kyra Wilson stated that “these findings are deeply concerning, but they are not new warnings.”

“First Nations families and survivors have been raising these concerns for decades. When children are placed in systems intended to protect them but continue to experience violence, exploitation, and abuse, we must hold those systems accountable,” she continued.

The AMC had called on Canada to examine “child welfare, child protection, and children in care” as part of the National Inquiry into Murdered and Missing Indigenous Women and Girls in 2018, a recommendation that made it into the final report.

However, AMC stated, “Despite these longstanding concerns, First Nations children remain disproportionately represented in Manitoba’s child welfare …

author: Soreti Kadir
title: The city beneath the capital
content:
At the end of 2010, I took a trip to Ethiopia to visit my family. At the time, my parents worked in Bole, the commercial center of Addis Ababa. As I was only 16, my movements were more or less regulated by my parents, which meant that I would travel with them into the city each day, after which it was the extent of my curiosity and creativity (and pocket money) that determined what I did until evening, when I would head back to our house on the outskirts of the city. Slowly, interactions with the staff at a nearby cafe, just a few hundred meters from the building where my family worked, became routine.

Over the two months that I was in Ethiopia, with much of this time spent in Addis Ababa, we spent most of our lunch breaks together, hanging out on the steps of the cafe, sharing stories to pass the time. One day, the conversation turned to our relationship to “Ethiopia” as a national identity. I was raised in the Oromo diaspora, a community that, in the years my mother and I migrated to Australia, was made up mostly of political refugees who fled the country after the adoption of the

Transitional Period Charter of Ethiopia

 and the official establishment of a transitional government.

This eventually led to the Tigray People’s Liberation Front monopolizing power within the Ethiopian People’s Revolutionary Democratic Front (EPRDF), a process that resulted in the isolation of those seeking political power within the EPRDF through the ballot. Given the size and economic importance of the Oromia region, it was the Oromo Liberation Front, among others, that became a key target of political violence, creating political communities in exile exactly like the one that I grew up in.

I inherited a different definition of Ethiopia, colored by memories and experiences of violence and displacement that informed my relationship to the state as a place of unbelonging for those who shared my identity. The day that the conversation with these two new friends wandered into political territory, we all engaged passionately, striving to reflect the extent of both our personal experiences and hopes for our country. They found my reflections overly nostalgic, antagonistic toward the country’s future, and unconcerned with its good. I found their insistence that we shared a national identity inaccurate and offensive. We agreed on little, and I found it exhilarating.

That evening, I was restlessly anticipating the opportunity to tell my mother about what I thought was the most exciting experience of my trip to date. In recounting the story, I almost gave my mother a heart attack. Angry, afraid, and in shock, my mother warned me sternly against ever engaging in such conversation in public again. She asked me many questions about who these men were, how I knew them, and if we’d ever had such conversations before. What I was blind to, and what was the daily lived experience of my parents, was that Addis Ababa, primarily but not exclusively, was a heavily surveilled city, the state looking for the people doing exactly what I found myself doing that day — discussing the political reality of our country.

Thereafter, I was careful, out of curiosity more than fear (being 16 with a high risk tolerance will do that), and refrained from full-fledged conversations, opting for quiet inquiry when the opportunity presented itself. Although our conversation never veered down the road of politics again, I continued to visit my friends every day and remember rushing to say a heartfelt goodbye on the day I was due to fly back to Australia.

Other parts of the country carry their own nuances and political realities, which deserve their own analysis; my focus here is the capital, Addis Ababa. That afternoon at the cafe points to something larger: in Ethiopia, to nurture spaces of connection, community-building, and care, we must first invest in collective repair — of the damage wrought by decades of state surveillance, which has defined the range and breadth of relational life the city can hold, and of the legacy of what can only be described as settler colonialism. “Where,” figuratively and literally, can this process of repair take place? It must take place in Finfinnee, geographically the same location as Addis Ababa, but sociologically and historically different, and with a capacity unique unto itself to ground and lead us to new political possibilities.

In 1886, Menelik II conquered the lands that were then known as Finfinnee and were primarily …

author: Novara Media
title: The Truth About Xinjiang
content:
Xinjiang is one of the most fought-over stories in the world. Beijing says the place’s transformation is a story of modernisation and counter-terrorism. Human Rights Watch, Amnesty and the UN’s human rights office have all describes mass internment and possible crimes against humanity.


So what is actually happening there and who can you trust?


Darren Byler is a socialist anthropologist who did his fieldwork in Ürümqi, the region’s capital.


He talks to Richard Hames about Uyghur life before the crackdown, the surveillance system that spans from tracking software on phones to continuous checkpoints to security service agents living in Uyghurs’ houses. He describes the camps and system of forced labour, and why he calls the whole system “terror capitalism”, a frontier where settler colonialism merges with the tech industry.

author: Unknown
title: Reuben Rose-Redwood, Wil Sahar Patrick - Why activists are vandalizing statues to colonialism
content:
Author

: Reuben Rose-Redwood, Wil Sahar Patrick

Title

: Why activists are vandalizing statues to colonialism

Date

: March 17 2020

Source

: Retrieved on November 14 2026 from https://theconversation.com/why-activists-are-vandalizing-statues-to-colonialism-129750


 In 2018, statues of

Edward Cornwallis

 and

John A. Macdonald

 were removed from their respective pedestals in Halifax and Victoria. Across Canada, colonial statues

have also been vandalized

 as an act of protest.


 Statues and monuments have become major

flashpoints

 of political conflict over the past decade.


 After the 2015

Charleston Massacre

, in which a neo-Confederate white supremacist murdered nine African Americans at the Emanuel African Methodist Episcopal Church in Charleston, South Carolina, a movement to remove

Confederate monuments and place names

 swept across the United States.


 Another wave of Confederate statue removals and place renamings occurred in the

aftermath

 of the Unite the Right rally in Charlottesville, Virginia in 2017.


 In South Africa, the

#RhodesMustFall movement

 led to the removal of a statue honoring the British imperialist Cecil Rhodes at the University of Cape Town in 2015. This inspired efforts to challenge Rhodes’s legacy

elsewhere

 as well.


A crowd looks on as the statue of imperialist Cecil Rhodes is removed from its perch at the University of Cape Town in 2015. Schalk van Zuydam


 Monument controversies are not unique to the 21st century.

Commemorative landscapes

 have been radically transformed during political regime changes throughout history. Following the Second World War, monuments to the Nazi regime

were toppled

. Similarly, the

fall of the Soviet Union

 and the

end of apartheid in South Africa

 led to significant changes to the memorial landscape.


The Legacies of Settler Colonialism


Settler colonialism

 is a process of colonization based upon the replacement of Indigenous or colonized peoples with a settler society. This involves both the disposession of Indigenous land and the erasure, either through assimilation or elimination, of Indigenous peoples.


 Colonial statues and place names are part of the political infrastructure of settler place-making in Canada. As a result, they have become focal points for challenging settler-colonial power and testing the limits of reconciliation.


 On Jan. 31, 2018, the Cornwallis statue was taken down from its pedestal in Halifax. As an honorific commemoration for the “founder” of Halifax, Mi'kmaw elders

have long viewed

 the statue as a sign of the ongoing dispossession of Indigenous peoples and called for its removal.


 As if answering the East Coast, the John A. Macdonald statue was removed from the entrance to City Hall in Victoria on Aug. 11, 2018. The decision to remove the Macdonald statue was made as part of the city’s

formal reconciliation process

 with the Songhees and Esquimalt First Nations.


 As Canada’s first prime minister, Macdonald was chief architect of its residential school system and promoted genocidal policies against Indigenous peoples. His monumental presence at the entrance to City Hall was a major barrier to reconciliation efforts.


 In August 2018, a second plaque was installed to replace a bronze statue of Canada’s first Prime Minister John A. Macdonald after the first was vandalized shortly after the removal of the statue from the front of City Hall in Victoria, BC. Chad Hipolito/THE CANADIAN PRESS


 A year later, the city of New Westminster followed suit, removing a statue of the

“Hanging Judge” Matthew Begbie

 from the grounds of the provincial courthouse.


 Those opposed to the removal of statues often propose adding historic plaques as a way to recontextualize statues while leaving them in public spaces. Some activists, however, have chosen a different option: vandalism.


Vandalizing Colonial Statues and Monuments


 Across Canada, contentious statues and monuments linked to settler colonialism have been targeted with vandalism. In Montréal, the

John A. Macdonald and Queen Victoria monuments

 have been regularly spray-painted. Macdonald statues have been vandalized in

Kingston

 and

Regina

 as far back

as 2012

.
