author: Mike Ludwig
title: Trump Judicial Nominee at Center of GOP Drama Signed Off on Deadly Boat Strikes
content:
Nominated to be a federal judge, T. Elliot Gaiser signed off on deadly airstrikes experts call extrajudicial executions.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Media coverage of Republican infighting over judicial nominee T. Elliot Gaiser has focused on the strong words exchanged between Texas Senators John Cornyn and Ted Cruz. President Donald Trump nominated Gaiser to become a federal judge in Texas, but Cornyn blocked a crucial committee vote on November 18 to advance the pick forward.

“Everyone knows that I am a notorious cusser and screamer and that Ted is a fragile thing,” Cornyn said on November 21 in a social media post describing a previous heated exchange between the two lawmakers. Cornyn has argued that Gaiser is not from Texas and has little trial experience, while Cruz accuses Cornyn of handing an open judicial seat to Democrats.

However, what has received far less attention is Gaiser’s role in producing the legal opinion that greenlit the U.S. military’s deadly airstrikes on civilian boats in the Caribbean and Pacific Ocean that the Trump administration has accused, without evidence, of smuggling drugs. The strikes have killed more than 200 people in what human rights groups say are effectively extrajudicial executions in blatant violation of U.S. and international law.

“We’re talking about legal opinions used to justify military strikes that have killed hundreds of people, alongside a broader pattern of putting the president’s personal interests ahead of the law,” said Michael Teter, co-founder of the Legal Accountability Center, in a statement.

Gaiser currently serves as assistant attorney general in the Justice Department, where he leads the Office of Legal Counsel (OLC). He is also Trump’s nominee for a lifetime federal judgeship in the Northern District of Texas. Cornyn used a procedural maneuver last week to block the Senate Judiciary Committee from advancing Gaiser’s nomination. However, Cornyn remains under pressure from Cruz and other conservatives to reverse course and allow a vote on Gaiser as Republicans race to confirm Trump nominees before a Democratic majority takes over in January.

Meanwhile, the Legal Accountability Center filed a bar complaint against Gaiser on November 18, calling for an investigation into his role in providing legal cover for the deadly airstrikes on civilian boats in international waters. The complaint also cites a series of opinions released by the OLC that allegedly prioritize Trump’s personal interests over federal law, including a controversial opinion declaring that the Presidential Records Act, a key oversight law, is unconstitutional and does not apply to Trump.

“Government lawyers have a duty to tell the president when the law says ‘no,’ not simply find ways to justify whatever he wants to do,” Teter said, adding that the allegations are “extraordinarily serious.”

At the center of the complaint is a secret legal opinion written under Gaiser’s leadership to provide legal justification for the Trump administration’s airstrikes on civilian boats suspected of smuggling drugs. Issued on September 5, 2025, the legal opinion followed an infamous September 2 attack in which two shipwrecked survivors of an initial U.S. airstrike were killed by a secondary (or “double tap”) strike while clinging to the wreckage in the water.

Rep. Jim Himes (D-Connecticut), who serves on the House Intelligence Committee and saw video of the strikes, pointed out that the second strike was impermissible by U.S. military manual standards. The bar complaint against Gaiser alleges he failed to exercise independent judgment and provided legal cover for unlawful killings.

While the legal opinion remains classified, court filings indicate the 49-page memo was signed by Gaiser, according to the bar complaint. Members of Congress who have seen the memo have publicly outlined its legal reasoning, which rests on a theory that the U.S. is engaged in a formal armed conflict with drug smugglers. The Washington Office on Latin America (WOLA), a human rights group, calls this reasoning “badly flawed.”

author: ACG
title: Against Labour’s Militarism: No War but the Class War
content:
The recent Budget told us which priorities Labour were setting. Billions for war, and slashing funding in other areas of spending. Arms manufacturers will receive greater government backing, and the development and manufacture of military technology will be a growing part of industrial strategy.


Chancellor Healey will be spending “£10bn of additional economic and military support—based on loans, Export Finance guarantees, and half a billion in urgent military funding for this winter.”. This is in addition to the £25 billion already put into defence by previous Tory and Labour governments. As the Budget pledged, “the government’s fully funded Defence Investment Plan will deliver stronger front-line military capability, supporting jobs, businesses and economic growth across the UK.” There will be £5 billion for advanced uncrewed systems for the rest of this Parliament, up to 2030. This includes £300 million for the StormFighter combat-air programme and £400 million for Army drone technology.


All this will mean an additional £15 billion annually on the military (rising to £36 billion a year if long term targets are met).


One of the events that triggered Starmer’s leaving of the scene, was the resignation of Healey as defence secretary.  He left because he felt that defence spending fell“well short of what is required for defence and the country at this dangerous time”. He talked about the invasion of Ukraine and the Russian threat, and talked about a Russian attack predicted by NATO by 2030. Now, three weeks after his initial resignation, Healey is Chancellor, and imposing his defence plans.


The government has re-affirmed its obligations to NATO to spend 3% of GDP by 2030, and 3.5% by 2035, the details of which will not be published until the 2027 spending review.  In addition, the National Wealth Fund and British Business Bank will put up to £5 billion over four years into defence, dual-use technologies and related national security sectors. The Innovative Defence Financing Taskforce has been established to seek additional private and international capital.


In order to pay for all this defence spending, this would be done by slashing the budgets of other departments by 1% from 2027‑28 to 2029‑30 to raise £3 billion, with £1.7 billion from the Treasury’s capital reserve.  One of the projects that will suffer is the Warm Homes Plan, which will get a cut of £1 billion. This comes at a time when many are facing higher energy bills. As was noted in the Budget statement, “… it is not necessarily the case that all departments will see real-terms increases at the next spending review”


The money is hard to find. Labour is too timid to put taxes on the rich. Already, thanks to years of austerity cuts from both Tories and Labour there is very little to spend. So what Labour will do, is attack benefits. In fact, Healey told the House of Commons after the Budget that “There will be a reduction in the benefits bill.”


This can be seen with the recent review entitled “Young People and Work” headed up by Alan Milburn, a Blairite Labour MP. This threatens the taking away of sickness and disability benefits for under-25s. They would be barred from claiming Universal Credit or the Personal Independence Payment (PIP), the main disability benefit, and instead receive a new youth allowance.


Milburn supports schemes like Sainsbury’s Modern Work Experience Programme, also endorsed by Burnham, where the supermarket chain would use 10,000 young people as unpaid labour.  


Any under-25s who fail to engage with the scheme proposed by Milburn would risk losing part of the allowance. He received the full support of Andy Burnham on this, who is open about increasing military spending, paid for by cutting benefits.


Another ominous move by Labour is the forthcoming review of disability benefits by the disability minister, Stephen Timms, another Blairite, indicating further welfare benefit cuts.


This upping of military spending and cutting of welfare spending has been prepared for by the right- wing press and think tanks. The notorious Paul Johnson called for Burnham to cut PIP, whilst talk about abolishing the triple lock on state pensions is rife in right wing rags. Alongside this is rabid propagandising for increased military spending from the likes of the Daily Mail and the Daily Telegraph. In addition, the sick, the disabled and the young are increasingly targeted as scroungers.

author: Harriet Williamson
title: US Military Set to Detonate Toxic Lead Bomb in Iowa
content:
Children, pregnant women and chronically ill people in Iowa are being advised to evacuate as the US army prepares to blow up a stockpile of munitions laced with lead on Wednesday. 


Nearly five tonnes of unstable bomb-making chemicals stored at a base in Middletown, Iowa, are scheduled for detonation despite serious risks to human health. 


The detonation is expected to send a toxic plume of lead-containing dust particles over eastern Iowa and into the neighbouring state of Illinois, where toxins will likely settle on farmland, homes and playgrounds. 


There is no safe level of exposure to lead, which is a neurotoxin. 


350 farms could be exposed

 to the toxic lead dust, according to the US Department of Agriculture. 


Children and pregnant women are particularly at risk as exposure to lead can interfere with fetal brain development, cause cognitive damage and increase the likelihood of miscarriages and premature births. 


In adults, lead exposure is linked to decreased kidney function, fertility issues and heart problems, along with

 increased risks

 of various cancers.


Iowa has the

second-highest rate of cancer

 among US states, and is one of only three states where rates of cancer are rising. 


A lawsuit was filed by environmental groups to block the detonation, but the US Circuit Court of Appeals ruled on Monday that it could go ahead.


Journalist Abby Martin called it “an emergency of [the US army’s] own making because of their own negligence and disregard”. 


She told

 BreakThrough News on Tuesday

: “I just can’t wrap my mind around the fact that an industry that has a budget of over $1tn cannot incorporate a safe disposal mechanism for these toxic chemicals it is constantly manufacturing.


“I think at the end of the day, they just know they can override local governments.”


Federal officials say the detonation is needed because the degraded material could explode on its own. 


The US army initially contracted a company to chemically neutralise the weapons after it became aware of the degrading cache at a military base in March,

the New York Times reported

. However, it cancelled the deal just two months later and decided to blow up the munitions instead. 


Environmental

assessment documents

 from the US military state that while the chemical route for disposal “offered environmental protections by avoiding a blast plume, it was eliminated from detailed study due to unacceptable risk to human safety”. This was because the process required more “hands-on” handling by workers over long days.


The Department of Health and Human Services (HSS) told pregnant women, children and those with chronic illnesses

to evacuate on Tuesday

, with HHS principal deputy assistant secretary for preparedness and response saying “you definitely want to be out of that area”.


The Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown makes medium and large calibre munitions for the US Department of Defense.

author: Kodao Productions
title: NPA-Mindoro reports failed AFP attack, 4 gov’t casualties
content:
The New People’s Army (NPA) reported the death of four government troopers in a clash at Bulalacao, Oriental Mindoro on Monday, thwarting a 1

st

 Infantry Battalion-Philippine Army strike operation.


The NPA said a unit of its Lucio de Guzman Command successfully defended itself against the raid at its temporary encampment in Sitio Gatol, Barangay San Roque, withdrawing safely after the firefight.


An ABS-CBN report of the incident quoted 203rd Infantry Brigade-Philippine Army commander Brig. Gen. Melencio Ragudo claiming only two soldiers were wounded and are at a stable condition at a hospital. The report also stated that said the clash started at around 8:35 AM.


The NPA, however, said civilians who were at the scene after the encounter reported that four soldiers were killed. The Red army likewise refuted 1st IB’s claim that firearms and equipment were seized from the guerillas.


The NPA added that its fighters spotted the approaching soldiers and opened fire on them before they could reach the camp.NPA-Mindoro spokesperson Madaay Gasic said their latest victory against the Armed Forces of the Philippines demonstrate the Red army’s will to fight and the people’s “unwavering support.” Gasic also belied Ragudo’s claim civilians tipped off the miitary about the NPA’s presence in the area.


“The people of Bulalacao and all the people of Mindoro celebrate the heroic resistance of their army against the enemy,” Gasic said. #

author: Rudi Hartono, Peter Boyle
title: ‘Rising authoritarianism and militarism’ in Indonesia under Prabowo
content:
As the Indonesian economy sinks deeper into crisis, President Prabowo Subianto's government is becoming more authoritarian. Peter Boyle spoke to Rudi Hartono, one of the founding editors of the progressive publication Merdika.id about the current political situation. Hartono, a former editor of Berdikari Online left the People’s Democratic Party (PRD) because it moved to the right.

Recent events in Indonesia — the deployment of thousands of soldiers and tanks in Jakarta following reports of electronic surveillance [wiretapping] targeting President Prabowo Subianto and other government officials and the police raid on Gadjah Mada University — are reminiscent of the Suharto dictatorship’s New Order regime. Is a new and dangerous situation developing? If so, what lies behind it?

Yes, we are witnessing clear symptoms of rising authoritarianism and militarism. Although many had predicted this trajectory since Prabowo’s election victory, the speed and intensity of the process have been striking.

Since June 2026, the military has once again been deployed to confront protests — a move that evokes memories of the New Order. Large-scale troop mobilisations occurred during the demonstrations on October 20 (marking two years of the Prabowo-Gibran administration) and October 28 (Youth Pledge Day).

On one of those days, I received a WhatsApp message containing a video of tanks and marching soldiers on the streets, accompanied by the caption: “Thank your friends [referring to former PRD members who now support Prabowo and hold positions in government] for bringing the military back onto the streets.”

Yet the presence of soldiers on the streets only completes the picture of authoritarian consolidation that has taken shape over the past two years under Prabowo-Gibran.

Today, the 1998 reformasi has become little more than an artifact. Political power is once again concentrated in the executive (the presidency).

Many of the president’s remarks in speeches have quickly turned into policy — such as the roof-tile standardisation program or foreign-language lessons. The House of Representatives (DPR) has been reduced to a chorus, much like under the New Order.

There is no genuine opposition in the DPR. Even the Indonesian Democratic Party of Struggle (PDIP), which remains outside the ruling coalition, has tended to be permissive toward the deteriorating situation.

The judiciary has suffered a similar fate: it is filled with government-aligned figures. The mechanisms of checks and balances have effectively disappeared.

It is not only the legislative and judicial branches that have been subdued. We are also seeing a process of recentralisation that is stripping regional and local governments of authority, fiscal resources, and responsibilities. Regional autonomy — one of the key achievements of the 1998 reform — is now little more than a skeleton being dragged toward its grave.

At the same time, freedom of expression is being heavily repressed. Paid "buzzers" [opinion-shapers] are deployed to drown out public criticism on social media, while the Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs actively removes critical content. Cases of threats, intimidation, and doxxing against citizens in digital spaces are common. Mainstream media have adopted self-censorship. Under former President Joko Widowo (Jokowi), certain individuals monitored the media from the outside; under Prabowo, his people have entered the newsrooms themselves to supervise from within.

The presidential wiretapping issue, which provided the pretext for mobilising more than 20,000 troops and tanks on Jakarta’s streets, cannot be read simply as a clash between two elite factions. It more closely resembles the autogolpe [“self-coup”] schemes frequently seen in Latin America.

In my view, the issue was manufactured to serve three purposes at once. First, it supplied a justification for deploying more soldiers onto the streets. Second, it diverted public attention from structural problems — economic crisis, corruption, militarism, and others — toward a security narrative. Third, it was a crude tactic to redirect vertical public anger at the regime into a drama of elite infighting.

Before the wiretapping story surfaced, the regime was already under pressure from multiple fronts: forest fires in Kalimantan, Sumatra, and Papua; mass food poisoning from the free nutritious meal program (MBG) that has affected more than 50,000 children; the militarisation and expanding role …

author: Dulce Amor Rodriguez
title: Women seek justice for Duterte drug war victims
content:
Photo by Jonathan Sta. Rosa/NCCP

Trigger warning: details of violence and death

Seeing her son crying as she was about to leave for the market, she gave him a piece of candy. She later found him dead upon coming back home.

Emily Soriano was among the women whose loved ones were killed during former president Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war. They shared their accounts of the killings, highlighting their continuing struggle for justice with leaders of the World Council of Churches (WCC).

Members of Rise Up for Life and for Rights, a network of relatives of people killed during the anti-drug campaign, recounted their experiences during a dialogue organized by the National Council of Churches in the Philippines (NCCP).

The dialogue formed part of Thursdays in Black, a WCC campaign that seeks to end violence against women.

Aside from Soriano, Normita Lopez recounted how police shot her son despite his attempt to surrender. According to her, witnesses saw him raise both hands and plead with the police not to shoot but an officer pushed him down and shot him four times in the body and once in his right hand.

For her part, Jane Lee said that people ignored their pleas for justice before the WCC facilitated her travel to bring the families’ stories to the United Nations.

Estrella Nonay said, “I didn’t know how to get justice, so I joined Rise Up because I believe that if one of us gets justice, it is also justice for my son.”

“We are sharing with you sacred stories. Now that you have heard them, you are witnesses. We invite the WCC to stand in solidarity with the families of the victims in their quest for justice,” Deaconess Norma Dollaga of Rise Up said.

Rev. Merlyn Hyde Riley, vice-moderator of the WCC Central Committee, said that the testimonies exposed deeper structural, political, economic, social, and spiritual issues behind the killings. “No human being deserves to be treated in the ways you have described your loved ones having been treated,” Hyde Riley said.

Rev. Dr. Karen Georgia Thompson, general minister and president of the United Church of Christ and president of the World Communion of Reformed Churches, also called on churches to confront state violence against poor and marginalized communities.

She said that poor and marginalized communities bear the brunt of programs designed to harm them and urged churches to uphold human rights and dignity. (DAA)

author: webadmin
title: Researched And ‘Observated’ To Death In The Barle Valley
content:
Stag chased to exhaustion and killed as the hunt invoked bogus exemptions when caught on camera.


WATCH THE VIDEO (VIEWER DISCRETION ADVISED)


The stag was pursued for hours. Credit North Dorset Hunt Sabs


On 17 October 2026, a North Dorset Hunt Saboteur witnessed the final moments of a stag pursued for hours through the Barle Valley before being shot in Marsh Wood. The stag was barely able to walk, his mouth wide open and tongue hanging out, with hounds and a gunman following behind.


Gunman James Wyatt following the stag, who by now was barely able to walk. Credit North Dorset Hunt Sabs


After they shot him, the excuses began.


Predictably, the focus turned to why the sab was there, rather than what they had just done to the animal. Perhaps the stress of having a sab witness their cruelty, made the hunters forget their well-rehearsed lines.


Wyatt was upset that his cruelty was being filmed. Credit: North Dorset Hunt Sabs.


This hunt hides behind the ‘Research and Observation’ smokescreen, but it is clearly a ruse, and the hunt even made up its own word to justify its cruelty.


Apparently, they had

‘observated’

 the stag. It’s not even a real word.


But those were the words of gunman James Wyatt. Mangled English aside, this exemption is nothing but a smokescreen for barbarism and bloodlust.


There is no research on these animals, there has never been – there are no known peer-reviewed research papers produced by hunts, from the hundreds or thousands of days spent hunting these magnificent animals.


In March 2019,

Defra told Parliament

 that it held no information about ‘research’ published under the exemption. That has not changed since. Shouting ‘Research and Observated’ over a tortured animal does not make it legal or acceptable.


James Wyatt alleged the stag was ‘researched and observated’ before being shot for his breeding behaviour. Credit: North Dorset Hunt Sabs.


After claiming that the stag was killed under the exemption, the hunter went on to immediately contradict himself – claiming that it was killed because of the stag’s breeding behaviour.


The animal – according to the hunters – had apparently been ‘servicing hinds’ for four or five years so that is why they took him out.


At first they claimed to kill this due to the ‘research and ‘observated’ exemption – then it was because of his breeding behaviour. Credit: North Dorset Hunt Sabs.


To hunt and kill an animal because of his breeding behaviour is not an exemption under the Hunting Act.


The mature stag was doing exactly what nature intended during the autumn rut. Where is the evidence to suggest this stag had been assessed and posed a problem to the wider deer population?


More importantly, how would any such concern justify pursuing him to exhaustion with dogs?


The Hunting Act sets out specific circumstances in which dogs may be used. Vague concerns around breeding are not one of them.


Other hunters warned the gunman that the hunt sab was below him on the hillside, but he fired the shot regardless, and this was followed by loud cheers.


Hunters attempted to prevent the sab from filming. Credit: North Dorset Hunt Sabs.


Hunters then attempted to shield the dead stag from the sab’s camera, before dragging his body down the hillside, the slit in his neck visible from where he had been bled.


The hunters drag the body away to be cut up into trophies. Credit: North Dorset Hunt Sabs.


The stag spent his final hours being hunted through the Barle Valley, he was exhausted, cornered and shot. He had done nothing wrong, and he was shot purely for living as a wild animal, breeding during the rut and attempting to evade those who wanted to kill him.


No words – real or made-up – should be allowed to obscure what happened to this animal and the cruelty inflicted upon him.


The government must confront the continuing barbaric cruelty and criminality that lie behind these exemptions.


Labour promised us a ban, a manifesto pledge to end this. Where is it?


A Hunt Saboteurs Association spokesperson said:


“It is not just foxes that are tormented and brutalised in our countryside by these bloodsports enthusiasts. Stag hunting is a particularly sickening form of cruelty, where terrified animals are pursued for hours, driving to complete exhaustion and then shot.


The idea that this barbarism can be passed off as ‘research and observation’ is an insult to anyone with an ounce of intelligence. These are not scientists conducting …

Stellenangebote

Animal Rights Watch e.V. (ARIWA) engagiert sich seit über 20 Jahren in Deutschland für Tierrechte und ist in der Bewegung fest etabliert. author: Marx-lover
title: The ELF and Eco-Activism
content:
This is a review of a book by the journalist Matthew Wolfe entitled Fires in the Night: The Earth Liberation Front, the FBI, and a Secret History of Eco-Sabotage, published in 2026. It's a good book!

Increasingly, it seems like it’s only a matter of time before civilization collapses. It might happen because of nuclear war, but the more likely cause is ecological chaos. Carbon emissions continue to rise and global warming is accelerating; the destruction of ecosystems, from forests to marine environments, is accelerating; countless species of animals and plants are going extinct every year because of human activity. A century from now, when the climate is much warmer than today and nature even more severely degraded, billions of people may be dying from floods, famines, scorching temperatures, lack of access to water, wars over natural resources, the collapse of urban infrastructure, and other catastrophes.

The global ruling class is doing little else but working to hasten the apocalypse, for example by expanding the use of fossil fuels and maniacally investing in data center construction. All the pleading of scientists, activists, and the general public that politicians take decisive action against global warming has availed little. The question “What is to be done?” has never, in all of history, been more urgent.

In his new book Fires in the Night, the journalist Matthew Wolfe narrates the history of a group of people in the 1990s and early 2000s who gave a bold answer to that question: the only kind of action that can meet the moment is eco-sabotage. Arson was their favorite method. The protection of animals was one of their major interests, so in addition to burning, say, car dealerships that sold gas-guzzling SUVs, they also targeted slaughterhouses, lumber companies, a large ski resort that was planning to expand into an old-growth forest, the university office of a biologist who was thought to be researching genetic engineering, and even Forest Ranger stations that were seen as complicit in timber sales. The FBI branded these people the country’s foremost domestic terrorism threat, and by 2007 most of them were in prison.

Wolfe’s book is of interest not only because it is based on incredibly meticulous research that makes it possible for Wolfe to tell the personal stories and motives of the core of activists who constituted the Earth Liberation Front (ELF)—or rather its most active cell, in Eugene, Oregon—as well as the stories of some of the federal officials and police officers whom they eluded for years. It’s a gripping and suspenseful tale, told without bias. But equally importantly, the book raises the same questions that, in a different way, Andreas Malm’s How to Blow Up a Pipeline raised in 2021: is economic sabotage in defense of the environment justified, and if so, what forms of sabotage and under what circumstances? Wolfe doesn’t answer these questions, but the history he relates demands they be taken seriously. It isn’t hard to argue that the ELF’s actions were misguided and accomplished little or nothing, but neither is it hard to argue that some kinds of eco-sabotage are defensible or even imperative.

Most readers, in any event, could probably empathize with the ELF activists (“Elves”) and even respect them for putting their lives on the line and for strictly adhering to their principles. They were always very careful to ensure that no animals or humans would be harmed by their property destruction—although it’s true that risks and uncertainty are inevitable in cases of arson. The Elves were young and idealistic, mere teenagers and twenty-somethings who met each other through the anarchist and radical environmentalist circles in Eugene. They had heard of something called the Earth Liberation Front in the UK and Europe, a decentralized, leaderless network of “cells” of anonymous eco-saboteurs, and in 1996 a few of them decided to start a new cell in the U.S. For the next five years, a dozen or so people would be behind most of the ELF incidents that the government and mass media dubbed “ecoterrorism”—despite the fact that not a single person was ever killed or injured.

title: Animal Rising Disrupts National Pig Awards in Central London Following Campaigner Arrests
content:
Animal Rising campaigners disrupted the National Pig Awards at the Royal Lancaster Hotel in central London this evening (16 November), while protesters outside blocked the main entrance. Police were called to the venue.

Despite enhanced security, six campaigners reached the event and were subsequently apprehended before being ejected from the hotel at approximately 7 pm. Around 70 protesters gathered outside as attendees arrived, holding placards reading “Free Luna” and “End Factory Farming”.

The group publicly declared its intention to shut down the awards last week, calling for Red Court, a pig factory farm in Suffolk, to release Luna, a mother pig whose life of confinement was filmed continuously for over a month by Animal Rising earlier this year. [1]

The investigation documented squalid conditions and illegal piglet thumping on the Red Tractor Assured farm. [2] Over 40,000 people have since signed a petition calling for Luna’s release to a sanctuary. [3]

The group filmed Luna confined in a narrow farrowing crate for five weeks, unable to turn around or take more than a step forward. A sanctuary has since offered her a home for the rest of her life. [4]

Red Court confirmed last week that Luna is once again in a farrowing crate. If the farm refuses to release her, she will remain there for approximately another month, confined with her newborn piglets, before she is removed and re-inseminated.

The farm has also rejected a proposed £5,000 donation to You Are Not Alone, an East Anglian charity supporting farmers’ mental health, in exchange for Luna’s release. [5]

Earlier today, Animal Rising announced that a third campaigner, Michelle Farnham, had been arrested on suspicion of burglary following the open rescue of three piglets (Leila, Nova and Maia) from Red Court.

Before the rescue, Animal Rising reported serious welfare concerns at the farm to the police, RSPCA and Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA).

APHA, the body responsible for enforcing farmed animal welfare, informed Animal Rising that the farm’s conditions, including the illegal thumping of a piglet, were normal.

Farnham attended Stoke Newington Police Station at 10 am this morning. Her fellow rescuers, Thomas Cusick and Liam Shaughnessy, had previously reported themselves to the police and been arrested. [6]

Farnham, 26, Animal Rising’s Campaign Lead, attracted national attention in September when she spent 21 days and nights locked in a farrowing crate in Trafalgar Square, highlighting Luna’s story and the suffering of animals in factory farms. High-profile visitors included Chris Packham and Green MP Adrian Ramsay. [7]

Animal Rising is campaigning for a government commitment to end UK factory farming by 2040.

title: PETA x Adventsome – vegane Adventskalender: Infos zur Verlosung und die Gründer:innen im Interview
content:
Werbung | Die

Weihnachtszeit

 rückt näher und mit ihr die Vorfreude auf kleine tägliche Überraschungen. Gemeinsam mit Adventsome verlosen wir von PETA Deutschland daher drei vegane Adventskalender voller

pflanzlicher Snacks

 und Infos zur Unterstützung gemeinnütziger Projekte. Der vegane Adventskalender zeigt, wie vielfältig, lecker und kreativ die Weihnachtszeit sein kann – mit vielen rein veganen Überraschungen. 


Über unsere Social-Media-Kanäle verlosen wir insgesamt drei vegane Adventskalender von Adventsome im Wert von jeweils 149 Euro. Mit etwas Glück können Sie sich oder Ihren Liebsten eine ganz besondere tierfreundliche Vorweihnachtszeit schenken. 


Teilnahmezeitraum: 13.11.2026 bis 16.11.2026

 


Inhaltsübersicht


									Interview mit Adventsome: Lea und Josias im Gespräch zum veganen Adventskalender


									Alle Infos zur PETA x Adventsome-Verlosung


									Lust auf noch mehr vegane Adventskalender?


Interview mit Adventsome: Lea und Josias im Gespräch zum veganen Adventskalender


Wir haben mit den Gründer:innen des Start-ups Adventsome – Lea und Josias – ein Interview geführt, um die Menschen hinter dem Projekt und den Gedanken hinter dem veganen Adventskalender vorzustellen: Welche Motivation treibt sie an, welche Rolle spielen Tiere bei Entscheidungen und wie kann ein Adventskalender über die Weihnachtszeit hinaus etwas bewegen? 


Lea und Josias – die Gründer:innen des Start-ups Adventsome.


PETA: Nehmt uns mit an den Anfang: Wie wurde aus eurer persönlichen Begeisterung für Adventskalender die Idee zu Adventsome?


Gab es einen bestimmten Moment, in dem ihr dachtet: „Genau so einen Kalender möchten wir selbst entwickeln“?

 


Adventsome:

 Die Idee kam uns, als wir uns 2017 gegenseitig Adventskalender schenken wollten, aber uns keiner wirklich begeistern konnte. Wir wünschten uns einen, der uns mit jedem Türchen aufs Neue überrascht, ganz viele unterschiedliche Produktkategorien vereint und in einer sinnvollen Verpackung kommt, die nicht nach 24 Tagen im Müll landet. Die zwei Kalender, die wir daraufhin selbst bastelten, haben uns im Dezember so viel Freude bereitet, dass wir beschlossen haben, diese auch mit anderen zu teilen. Ein Jahr später brachten wir unsere ersten 500 Adventskalender auf den Markt, die wir damals alle selbst neben der Uni verpackten – das waren ganze 12.000 einzelne Geschenke! 


PETA: Weihnachten verbinden viele Menschen mit Mitgefühl und Nächstenliebe. Welche Rolle spielen Tiere für euch dabei – und wie hat das eure Entscheidung für einen vollständig veganen Adventskalender geprägt?

  


Adventsome

: Wir lieben Tiere, haben selbst auch zwei

Katzen adoptiert

 und uns jahrelang im Tierschutz engagiert. Mit Adventsome möchten wir daher keine Produkte unterstützen, für die Tiere leiden müssen. Gleichzeitig finden wir es spannend, wie vielfältig das vegane Sortiment mittlerweile ist und wie viele innovative Alternativen es gibt. Genau den Brands, die diese Entwicklung weiter vorantreiben, möchten wir eine Bühne geben und ihnen helfen, bekannter zu werden. Unser Adventskalender soll Menschen dafür begeistern, Neues auszuprobieren und vielleicht auch die eine oder andere Gewohnheit zu hinterfragen! 


PETA: Euer Kalender verbindet 20 Produkte von Start-ups mit vier Spendentürchen. Was sollen Menschen beim Auspacken erleben – und was soll davon nach dem 24. Dezember bleiben?

 


Adventsome

: Wir wünschen uns, dass unsere Kund:innen jeden Morgen mit echter Vorfreude ein Türchen öffnen. Das schönste Feedback ist für uns, wenn uns jemand schreibt, dass er oder sie wieder kindliche Neugier verspürt. Richtige Überraschungen sind im Erwachsenenleben so selten geworden! 


Nach Weihnachten bleiben soll zunächst einmal unsere weiterverwendbare Design-Box, die wir jedes Jahr mit einer Künstlerin gemeinsam kreieren. Außerdem hoffentlich ganz viele neue Gedankenanstöße und Perspektiven und vielleicht auch das ein oder andere Lieblingsprodukt? 


Lea und Josias engagieren sich seit Jahren im Tierschutz und haben selbst zwei Katzen adoptiert.


PETA: Von Snacks über Pflege bis zu Alltagsprodukten: Wo findet ihr die Überraschungen, die es in euren Kalender schaffen?

  


Adventsome

: Die wichtigste Frage ist immer: Würden wir uns selbst darüber freuen, wenn wir morgens das Türchen öffnen? Das Produkt muss zudem vegan, unisex und alkoholfrei sein und auch darüber hinaus mit unseren Werten matchen!

title: Where Is The Hunting Ban, Labour?
content:
This fox was illegally hunted at a joint meet of the North Cotswold Hunt and the Warwickshire Hunt on Saturday 14th November. Image credit: West Midlands Hunt Sabs


In July 2024, the Labour Government made a manifesto commitment to ban trail hunting and improve the Hunting Act.


On 26 March 2026, the Government launched a consultation to determine how best to implement an effective and enforceable ban on trail hunting in England and Wales.


The consultation closed on 18 June, having received 184,000 responses. Yet months later, we are still waiting for the results and a clear timetable for what happens next.


The Government has acknowledged the risks trail hunting poses to wildlife, including the danger of hounds pursuing and killing live animals. It has also recognised concerns that trail hunting can be used as a smokescreen for illegal hunting.


This fox was hunted and killed by the Blackmore and Sparkford Vale (BSV) Hunt on Thursday 19th November. Image credit: Locals Against The BSV Hunt


Meanwhile, wildlife continues to suffer.


Foxes and other wild animals are chased, injured and killed. Our local hunt saboteur groups are out week after week, witnessing and documenting incidents and working to protect wildlife, often with little support.


But hunting also affects people. Rural residents face disruption, trespass, intimidation, road safety issues and damage to property. Their experiences should not be overlooked.


The Countryside Alliance and British Hound Sports Association continue to portray a ban on trail hunting as an attack on rural communities, livelihoods and countryside traditions.


But protecting wildlife and rural communities is not an attack on the countryside. Nor should legitimate countryside activities be used as a justification for allowing hunting with dogs to continue.


A ban must be comprehensive. Simply banning trail hunting is not enough if exemptions and loopholes allow hunts to continue pursuing and killing wildlife under another guise.


The HSA is calling for a full and effective ban on hunting with dogs, removing the existing exemptions and loopholes that allow this cruelty to continue, alongside meaningful improvements to the Hunting Act.


WE NEED THE GOVERNMENT TO ACT


We are demanding three things:


Publish the consultation results and the Government’s response.


Publish the legislative proposals for a full and effective ban on hunting with dogs and improvements to the Hunting Act, removing exemptions and loopholes.


Set a clear date for introducing the necessary legislation to Parliament.


We cannot allow this commitment to disappear into the political long grass.


Wildlife needs protection now, not at some unspecified point in the future.


TAKE ACTION


PLEASE TAKE ACTION TODAY


We need as many people as possible to contact their elected representatives and make it clear that this issue has not gone away.


Write to your MP


Ask your MP to contact the Government and demand answers to the three questions above. Ask them to press for a clear timetable and support a comprehensive ban on hunting with dogs, without exemptions or loopholes. Write to your MP

here

.


Write to the Prime Minister


The Prime Minister has spoken about building a more caring society. That must include compassion and protection for our wildlife.


Ask him to ensure the Government honours its commitment to ban trail hunting and delivers the wider legislative changes needed to end hunting with dogs. Write to the Prime Minister

here

.


Both messages can be brief. What matters is that MPs and the Prime Minister hear from as many people as possible.


Our wildlife cannot wait any longer. We need a full ban, effective legislation and an end to the loopholes that allow this cruelty to continue.


NOW IS THE TIME TO MAKE OUR VOICES HEARD.


TAKE ACTION

title: Budget 2027 : ce que les députés ont décidé pour les animaux
content:
Dernier budget de l’État avant la présidentielle, le projet de loi de finances pour 2027 est une occasion décisive de réorienter l’argent public vers un autre modèle agricole. Quel est le bilan des débats parlementaires et des décisions gouvernementales pour les animaux ?

Depuis le 13 octobre, l’Assemblée nationale a examiné en séance publique le projet de loi de finances pour 2027. Dans un contexte marqué par les canicules, les sécheresses et les incendies de l’été, le Gouvernement a annoncé plus d’un milliard d’euros pour « relancer la production agricole ». Face au dernier budget avant la présidentielle, les députés avaient un choix à faire : continuer à financer le modèle intensif ou investir dans une agriculture qui nous protège, nous et les autres animaux.

Avec Le Sauvetage du siècle, L214 défend des mesures concrètes pour atteindre la réduction de moitié du nombre d’animaux tués d’ici 2030 : aider les éleveurs volontaires à sortir de l’élevage intensif ou de la pêche, développer les cultures végétales pour nous nourrir, taxer la publicité pour les produits animaux, ou encore soutenir les cantines pour qu’elles proposent une plus grande offre végétale.

Pourtant la quasi-totalité de ces propositions a été rejetée :

L’amendement I-3588 (Marianne Maximi, LFI) visant à réserver le suramortissement fiscal des projets d’avenir agricole aux élevages avec accès au plein air, rejeté par 50 voix contre 14,

L’amendement I-3467 (Anne Stambach-Terrenoir, LFI) cherchant à exclure du crédit d’impôt recherche les dépenses visant à intensifier les productions animales, rejeté par 101 voix contre 53,

L’amendement I-295 (Claire Lejeune, LFI) proposant de porter à 35 % l’impôt sur les sociétés pour les élevages intensifs soumis à autorisation, rejeté par 60 voix contre 27.

Un seul amendement favorable aux animaux a été adopté : l’amendement I-2017 de Romain Courbon (Socialistes), travaillé avec l’association QUATRE PATTES, qui crée un crédit d’impôt de 25 % pour les investissements favorisant la sortie des cages, l’accès au plein air et la réduction des densités. Il a été adopté par 10 voix contre 7.

Les débats ont aussi révélé la difficulté d’aborder sereinement la question de notre consommation de viande. Lors de l’examen du budget de la Sécurité sociale, Sandrine Rousseau (Écologiste et social) a défendu une taxe sur la viande ultra-transformée. Cette mesure a été qualifiée par Laurent Jacobelli (Rassemblement national) d’ « amendement le plus risible », malgré les impératifs pour les animaux, la santé publique et la transition écologique. L’amendement a été rejeté par 84 voix contre 14.

Le projet de loi de finances ayant finalement été rejeté par l’Assemblée nationale, aucun de ces amendements ne figurera dans le texte, en cours d’examen par le Sénat. La seconde partie du budget, consacrée aux dépenses, n’a pas pu être débattue à l’Assemblée. Encore une fois, les intérêts des animaux sont largement ignorés.

Pour la cinquième année consécutive, des députés ont tenté de s’attaquer aux associations qui révèlent les conditions d’élevage, de transport et d’abattage des animaux. Leur méthode : supprimer les réductions d’impôt sur les dons qui leur sont faits. Autrement dit, sanctionner les donateurs des associations pour entraver leur travail d’information.

Heureusement, tous les amendements examinés à l’Assemblée nationale ont été rejetés :

L’amendement I-1603 (Stéphanie Galzy, RN) : suppression de la réduction d’impôt pour les dons à une association condamnée pour intrusion, violation de domicile ou entrave à l’activité économique, rejeté le 15 octobre par 68 voix contre 58,

L’amendement I-1798 (Kévin Mauvieux, RN) : retrait de la réduction d’impôt pour toute association condamnée définitivement, quel qu’en soit le motif, rejeté le 15 octobre par 50 voix contre 44,

L’amendement I-357 (Corentin Le Fur, DR) : extension des infractions entraînant la perte des avantages fiscaux, rejeté le 16 octobre par 49 voix contre 38,

L’amendement I-1280 (Christelle d’Intorni, UDR) : même extension, élargie aux délits de presse, dont la diffamation, rejeté le 16 octobre par 47 voix contre 37.

D’autres amendements de même nature ont été retirés ou n’ont pas été défendus en séance. Un amendement de protection proposé par Romain Courbon (Socialistes), qui visait à interdire toute restriction de la réduction d’impôt pour des motifs portant atteinte à la liberté associative, a en revanche été rejeté par 58 voix contre 36 (scrutin n° …

title: Animal Rights Radicals Destroy Several Hunting Hides in Italy amid Controversy over Hunting Law Reform
content:
Several hunting hides in Veneto have been wrecked and covered in anti-hunting graffiti. Images released by four hunting organisations show the Animal Liberation Front (ALF) signature and messages opposing the reform of Italy’s hunting legislation.

Vandalism against hunting facilities is making headlines in Italy once again. Several hunting hides (capanni da caccia) have been destroyed in the Veneto region, with their structures covered in graffiti opposing hunting and the reform of the legislation governing it in the country.

The incidents were publicly condemned this Wednesday, 4 November, by four organisations in the sector: the Cacciatori Veneti association, CONFAVI, ACR and FCR. The organisations released a gallery of photographs showing the damage to the facilities and the inscriptions left on their structures.

The graffiti includes the familiar ALF signature, standing for Animal Liberation Front (Animal Liberation Front), alongside messages calling for a boycott of the reform of Italy’s hunting law. The symbols visible in the images match those used in previous actions attributed to this animal rights movement.

The organisations accompanied the photographs with a strongly worded message directed at those responsible for the damage: “Destroying other people’s property does not defend any cause; it only demonstrates cowardice.”

The incident comes at a time of heightened tension over the reform of Italy’s hunting legislation. The bill seeks to amend Law 157/1992, which provides the basic legal framework for wildlife protection and the regulation of hunting.

The graffiti found on the Veneto hides directly links the property damage to this legislative controversy. However, the messages written on the facilities do not, on their own, identify the people who carried out the attacks. So far, no information has been released about arrests or police investigations relating to this incident either.

The appearance of the initials ALF recalls other incidents of vandalism recorded in Italy against facilities used by hunters.

One of the most notable previous incidents occurred in December 2019 in Montorfano, in the province of Brescia. On that occasion, eleven hunting hides in the municipalities of Rovato, Cologne and Palazzolo were wrecked. The damage was accompanied by threats and graffiti bearing the Animal Liberation Front signature.

More recently, in December 2025, six hides were destroyed in the Lower Valsugana area, between the municipalities of Grigno and Ospedaletto, in the province of Trento. The structures were found knocked down and marked with offensive messages directed at hunters. The ALF signature was also found in that case.

These previous incidents show that the destruction of hunting facilities is nothing new in Italy. The repeated attacks on hunting hides reveal a problem that goes beyond the war of words between supporters and opponents of hunting.

title: New Research Bolsters Evidence That Glyphosate Herbicide Can Cause Cancer
content:
The findings undermine the EPA’s longstanding conclusion that it is not likely to be carcinogenic, experts say.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

New research funded by the US government is strengthening evidence that widely used glyphosate herbicide can cause cancer and other serious health problems, a development that comes as federal regulators say they are giving new scrutiny to the chemical.

The new scientific findings also come as Bayer, which bought glyphosate-maker Monsanto in 2018, is solidifying a class-action settlement in litigation over cancer claims tied to sales of glyphosate-based Roundup and other brands.

The US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) says it is taking a fresh look at scientific studies pertaining to glyphosate safety. The agency announced in September that it was joining with the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to “expand the evidence” for the EPA’s ongoing registration review of glyphosate. The agency set Monday as the end of a public comment period on its review.

The new research, involving reviews of animal and human studies, has not yet been finalized and has yet to be peer-reviewed, but three papers were made available last week online.

In one of the most significant research findings, scientists from the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS) conducted a review of epidemiology studies and found that “the current body of epidemiology studies found a positive association between [glyphosate based herbicide] exposure and [lymphohematopoietic cancers],” such as non-Hodgkin lymphoma. The research was requested by the HHS.

In 2015, the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) classified glyphosate as probably carcinogenic to humans based on a review of a wide body of published studies, and noted a particular association to non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

The EPA has repeatedly discounted IARC’s findings and assured Americans that glyphosate is “not likely” to cause cancer. But the EPA’s position has drawn fire from scientists around the world as well as public health and environmental advocates who accuse the agency of failing to properly evaluate scientific findings and of aligning its position on glyphosate with Bayer and other industry interests profiting from the herbicide.

“Americans would be smart to heed the cancer findings of the nation’s most trusted scientific institution rather than the industry-influenced claims of the EPA,” Nathan Donley, environmental health science director at the Center for Biological Diversity, said in a press release about the new research.

“The EPA’s pesticide office has made a mockery of pesticide science for far too long,” he said. “It’s about time we have a US agency that tells the public the truth and doesn’t just parrot pesticide industry talking points.”

The NIEHS researchers also found that an evaluation of six cancer bioassays in mice and nine in rats supported cancer concerns.

“Overall, the evidence from animal studies suggests exposure to glyphosate or GBHs [glyphosate-based herbicides] is associated with carcinogenic effects in human-relevant animal models, based on treatment-related tumor responses observed across multiple studies, organ systems, and rodent species,” that research paper states.

In a third paper, the researchers noted that human exposure to glyphosate is “nearly ubiquitous,” and the chemical is commonly found in human urine. People can be exposed in a variety of ways, including through skin, inhalation, and diet.

“The available human and animal evidence for the carcinogenicity of glyphosate … indicate glyphosate may be a human carcinogen, though observed responses were generally of small magnitude and not uniformly replicated across studies,” the researchers wrote. “Given the widespread nature of human exposure to glyphosate/GBH, even small increases in risk can lead to substantial increases in disease burden at the population level. There is added concern for occupationally exposed individuals who experience exposure more frequently and at higher levels …”

Dave Andrews, chief science officer at the Environmental Working Group, called on the EPA to take “meaningful action to protect Americans from glyphosate.”

title: Line 5 Reroute Threatens the Wetlands of the Bad River Watershed
content:
Ashland County, Wisconsin — April Stone walks along a stretch of the highly controversial and dangerous

Line 5 reroute

. “This is the Line 5 reroute,” she says. “It’s a 41-mile swath of cut land going around the whole Reservation.”


The Enbridge Line 5 is a 645-mile pipeline that pumps crude oil and natural gas from Superior, Wisconsin into Ontario, Canada. This recent reroute cuts through forests, wetlands, and swamps surrounding the Bad River Reservation in northern Wisconsin.


Stone, an Ojibwe Black Ash basket weaver and member of the Bad River Band of Lake Superior Chippewa, has witnessed the loss of Black Ash harvesting areas along the Line 5 reroute. She walks into a wetland where standing water pools beneath the trees with the exposed pipeline corridor.


“There’s a small creek that’s running here,” she explains. “It’s a saturated area. It has more standing water than the uplands all around.”


It’s in these wetlands, adjacent to Lake Superior, where one can find Black Ash trees thriving.


Indigenous peoples throughout the Great Lakes have harvested Black Ash to create traditional baskets, pack frames, fishing gear, and storage containers. Stone harvests her own trees from these swamps.


“That’s where the Black Ash trees were growing,” she says. “Where I have harvested trees in the past for my baskets.”


Today, many of those trees are gone. “When they took this swath in here … they cut through the Ash swamp as well,” Stone says. She points toward Black Ash trees tagged in pink. “There are still some standing Ash trees, but many of them are cut down.”


Stone is recognized as one of the foremost Black Ash basket makers in the Great Lakes area.


She began teaching herself basketry after discovering that there weren’t any practicing Black Ash basket weavers left in her own tribal community. Stone is one of the last Black Ash basket weavers of the Bad River Band, making her work central to preserving a cultural tradition that had nearly disappeared.


Stone’s baskets embody ecological knowledge, harvesting practices, language, ceremony, and a relationship with wetlands that can not exist without healthy forests. That relationship now faces a huge threat.


The proposed Line 5 re-route was designed after the Bad River Band went to court against Enbridge for criminally trespassing on tribal land. The giant oil company’s lease had expired and was not being renewed. As a response to the court loss and despite the environmental dangers, Enbridge began constructing 41 miles of new pipeline — surrounding most of the Bad River Reservation.


Although the reroute technically avoids reservation boundaries, it remains inside the Bad River watershed and covers almost three-quarters of the Reservation boundaries. According to environmental permitting documents processed by the Army Corps of Engineers, construction of the pipeline re-route would cross 186 streams, rivers, and other waterways, covering more than 100 acres of wetlands.


The corridor also requires clearing forests through numerous wetlands where Black Ash trees grow.


Line 5 Pipeline Reroute Endangers Maple Trees and Native Lifeways


Stone says those impacts cannot be separated from what happens downstream.


Describing how water connects the entire watershed, Stone continued, “The Reservation itself makes up the lower-third portion of the entire watershed. All the water that flows from the lakes, from the streams, from the rivers… eventually all of it goes into Bad River… eventually all of it goes through the Reservation… out into Lake Superior.”


Although this wetland nourishes one of the largest freshwater ecosystems on Earth, for the Bad River Band, the watershed is not simply geography. It is home to one of the Ojibwe’s most important cultural relations — Manoomin (wild rice).


Wild rice thrives on the clean fresh lake water and is a precious food source that is inextricably tied to Anishinaabe (Ojibwe) origin stories and prophecies. The rice is legally and culturally seen as a spiritual “relative” and a foundational gift from the Creator that ensured their survival.


“Line 5 has split this swamp in two,” Stone says. But she isn’t only talking about wetlands.


“Not just here, but everywhere else along the 41-mile span where swamps exist.”


To Stone, the pipeline corridor divides more than the natural habitat. These are places where people have harvested together and passed on traditional ecological knowledge for generations.


When the swamp …

title: Peoples’ Climate Summit: COP31 has failed to deliver climate justice
content:
The Peoples’ Climate Summit, held in Antalya from November 14 to 18, has published a statement on the outcomes of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31). After more than two weeks of negotiations, the global climate conference ended without an overarching final agreement or a consensus on phasing out fossil fuels. The Peoples’ Climate Summit also sees this as a structural failure of the international climate regime and questions its democratic foundations.


Global power imbalances in climate policy


In the statement, the organizations criticized the lack of transparency in the decision-making processes at COP31, stating that the presentation of draft negotiating texts in the middle of the night made it difficult for participating countries to engage effectively in the deliberations. The Peoples’ Climate Summit highlighted an incident during the closing session as particularly revealing: “COP31 President and Turkish Environment Minister, Murat Kurum, cut off Ghanaian Environment Minister Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, who was speaking on behalf of 54 African countries. The fact that representatives of African peoples, who have contributed the least to causing the climate crisis but face its most severe consequences, are silenced reflects the power imbalances within the international climate regime. There can be no climate justice without democracy.”


False technological solutions serving the interests of the fossil fuel industry


The statement said: “While references to fossil fuels disappeared from the draft decisions over the course of the negotiations, the COP31 presidency maintained its targets for carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS) technologies, despite opposition from a coalition of 126 countries. The Peoples’ Climate Summit views the political promotion of technologies whose viability on a large scale has yet to be demonstrated as a means for polluting corporations to evade their responsibility to reduce emissions.


“Forests and ecosystems must not be reduced to carbon credits that companies can purchase to continue polluting the environment. Technology cannot replace actual emissions reductions.”


Half a billion dollars to host COP31


According to the organizations, the demand by countries of the Global South to provide $120 billion annually by 2035 for adaptation to the impacts of the climate crisis went unmet in Antalya. The Peoples’ Climate Summit illustrated the priorities that were set instead by pointing to the costs of hosting COP31. Citing data from the Electronic Public Procurement Platform (EKAP), the organizations estimate that the total value of tenders awarded and contracts signed by Turkey as part of the summit preparations up to September 2026 exceeded 25 billion lira, equivalent to approximately $500 million. According to the statement, this contrasts with just $50.2 million in new funding pledges to the international Adaptation Fund.


The total value of contracts for preparing the UN Climate Change Conference was therefore approximately ten times the amount of new pledges to the Adaptation Fund. The Peoples’ Climate Summit demanded that the Turkish government provide a detailed disclosure of all expenditures.


The hypocrisy of fossil fuel policy


 


Among the fundamental contradictions of COP31 is the continued investment in fossil fuels by Turkey and Australia, which jointly assumed leadership of the UN Climate Change Conference. On November 9, the very day COP31 began, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan announced the discovery of two new oil fields in the Gabar region of Northern Kurdistan, with an estimated potential of 135 million barrels. “The fact that a government which, in its capacity as COP31 president, brings countries together in Antalya presents increased fossil fuel production as a success exposed the hypocrisy of its climate policy on the very first day,” the statement said.


Five concrete demands to the Turkish government


The Peoples’ Climate Summit expects concrete political action from Turkey, which will hold the COP presidency until COP32: “Coal-fired power plants must be shut down, and a binding timetable for phasing out coal must be presented. New oil, natural gas and coal projects must be halted, and fossil fuel subsidies must be abolished. author: ACG
title: National Climate Change Demo in Dublin
content:
The annual Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) has been issued. This is a tool used to see how well 64 countries (those which produce 90% of global greenhouse gas emissions) are doing at mitigating the worst aspects of climate change.


Obviously some places are doing better than others. Ireland is one country that is performing worse than the last time conditions were evaluated. There are complexities in the details, as with any real-world situation. Nevertheless, there are some bottom-line problems that are impossible to ignore.


The report says: “Despite superficially strong frameworks, the CCPI country experts note that progress on climate action is nowhere near sufficient…” It also states clearly “The experts criticise the lack of implementation of existing legislation, frequent introduction of exclusions, and limited understanding of the severity of the situation.” (https://ccpi.org/country/irl/).#


oplus_0


One of the major culprits in preventing progress is data centres. Here “The experts stress that progress in renewables deployment is falling behind surging energy demand. Data centres are the main driver, as they accounted for 23% of total electricity supply in 2025 and now exceed the demand of all households in Ireland. To meet the rising demand, the government has continued to support and even expand fossil fuel use instead of reducing dependence on imports.” (ibid)


So you have a country where the government talks the talk but in reality fails to keep its commitments and prefers to cosy up with big businesses that harm the environment. There should be no huge surprise in that. The experts who composed the CCPI report are hardly radicals and their work on the subject doesn’t exist in isolation. It is an international phenomenon that can be replicated to varying degrees across the world. The data speaks for itself and the idea that powerful people look after their own interests above everyone elses is something a lot of folks recognise.


Evidence of this recognition came in Dublin, with a 5,000-strong National Climate Demo on November 14th, pre-dating the CCPI report by 4 days. In many ways the gathering was unremarkable. That’s certainly the case


in terms of the scheduling and route of the march. It took about an hour and went through the CBD and ended near the government buildings.


Oplus_131072


As with other recent demonstrations, the most impressive aspect of the action was the sheer range of people who participated. You could just about tick off an entire alphabetical bingo card of groups and individuals who joined. Everyone from anarchists to doctors, environmentalists to Palestinian protestors, Quakers to socialists and vegans. Those involved were aware of the seriousness of the issue, but there was a vibrancy to the march that manifested more as a colourful concern than a militant anger. That is probably to be expected in such a disparate crowd.


Its risky to assume too much, but given the overall tone of the demo, its likely many who joined would have favoured an approach similar to the writers of the CCPI report. Its an outlook characterised by recognition of a critical problem but calls on politicians to do this and that to ensure its resolution. For those of us with a more radical perspective, such demonstrations are an opportunity to initiate discussions and exchanges on why the latter view is faulty and to suggest alternatives.


It is probably fair to say environmental consciousness is currently high among the population at large, and especially so for those who actively join campaign groups and demos. The challenge is therefore not so much making people aware of the problem of climate change, as introducing them to ways of thinking or theories and methods they might not be familiar with.


Anarchists were approached during the November 14th action by fellow participants. The majority seemed curious about who we are and what we stand for. There used to be an active anarchist movement in Ireland from the 80s through to a few years ago (https://libcom.org/article/workers-solidarity-movement-closing-statement). Its not easy to maintain organisations and activity across time, and things are at a bit of a low ebb now. It has resulted in a bunch of folks (not always based on their generation or age) who aren’t familiar with anarchism or our organisations. It’s a shame, but we have to begin from how things are on the ground, not how we wish them to be.

title: Baclaran vendors bear the cost of ASEAN Summit
content:
By Reachelyn Esona and Roselle Ochobillo

From bustling streets to empty sidewalks.

This may be an image of order for some, but for Baclaran street vendors, it can mean another day of uncertainty over whether they will have earnings to take home.

In the first week of November, the local government of Parañaque City ordered a clearing operation in barangay Baclaran in time for the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nation (ASEAN) summit from November 15 to 17.

The Parañaque local government said that the barangay would temporarily prohibit street vendors along Roxas Boulevard, service roads, Redemptorist Road, Quirino Avenue, and beneath LRT-1 from November 2 to November 20, to clear the way for the arriving delegates.

Among those forced to leave their usual vending spots is Eduardo Bargas, 59, who’s been selling toys along Baclaran for almost 20 years to support his wife and only child. After being dislocated, he resorted to selling bottled water to earn a living despite the imposed clearing operation.

According to Bargas, they were informed about the operation as early as November 1. While larger vendors operating inside stall establishments were allowed to continue selling, ambulant vendors like him were temporarily ordered to stop their operations.

Bargas was nearly apprehended once by the authorities. Had he been caught, he said, his goods would have been confiscated. He begged the authorities not to take his items as it was all he had to live on.

Like other vendors, Bargas’s income was severely impacted by the clearing operation. He said he used to earn up to P1,000 (approximately US$ 15.63) a day before the policy was implemented. Now, he takes home only around P300 (approximately US$ 4.69).

The same concern was shared by a 50-year-old towel and sack bag vendor, Marlyn Merioles. She sells along Baclaran to sustain her elderly mother who is on maintenance medication, and her sibling who is a person with disability.

Before the clearing, Merioles was earning around P300 (approximately US$ 4.69) to P500 (approximately US$ 7.82) a day. Since the operation began, there were days she went home with empty pockets.

Merioles said she felt disheartened by the policy. Vendors, she said, are now anxious and find it difficult to sell their goods. They are constantly on their feet, keeping an eye out for patrols roaming the area. Merioles fears that she might not see them coming as her eyesight is already failing.

They were also warned that their goods would be confiscated if they were caught. Merioles said it would be a loss they could not afford because even a whole day of selling was not enough to recover the capital they had borrowed.

Merioles said it would help if the government would sustain their daily expenses. However, she said, only a few of the vendors benefitted from the financial assistance provided for the vendors.

While the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) promised P10,000 (approximately $156.35) in cash assistance to vendors affected by the clearing operations in Baclaran, some vendors said they struggled to access the financial aid because it was reportedly limited to registered voters of Baclaran.

Rochelle Maale, who has been renting a stall in Baclaran for 10 years to sell ready-to-wear clothes, was among those who did not receive the assistance because she is not a registered voter in the area.

“The distribution of funds should be balanced… What about those who have been here for a long time but didn’t get anything?”Maale retorted.

Vendors argued that the assistance should be extended to everyone affected by the clearing operations, regardless of their place of residence, since they all experienced the impact of the clearing operations.

However, for many vendors, the issue goes beyond the limited eligibility for financial assistance.

They also questioned whether the P10,000 (approximately US$ 156.35) would be enough to sustain them after nearly 20 days of restricted operations.

Maale shared that the amount was insufficient to cover their daily expenses, especially amid rising costs of goods. “Will that P10,000 even last for a few days? No, it’s still not enough. That’s why vendors are struggling to make ends meet.”

She said some vendors have resorted to taking out loans to meet their everyday needs and restore their capital.

For vendors like Maale, the struggle extends beyond the clearing operations and financial assistance. What they need is a permanent and secure …

author: Petala Ironcloud
title: Indigenous Sovereignty Is Under Attack Today in the Name of Permitting Reform
content:
A bill now moving through Congress would allow tech oligarchs to circumvent tribal opposition to their projects.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

In March 1621, months before the meal Americans now call the first Thanksgiving, the Wampanoag leader Ousamequin sat down with the Plymouth colonists and negotiated a mutual-defense treaty. His people had every reason to keep their distance: An epidemic carried by European traders had totally emptied the village of Patuxet only a few years earlier. They came to the table anyway.

That’s what reciprocity asks of you: the understanding that relationships between people — and between nations — run on ongoing giving, receiving, and responsibility.

Four hundred and five years later, the federal government has left a long record of making that table optional through ignoring treaties with tribal nations. Now it is seeking to throw out the table altogether.

The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) now moving through Congress puts forth a series of changes that would fast-track federal approvals for projects like data centers and fossil fuel infrastructure. The bill would collapse Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act by narrowing what is considered an “undertaking” –– where federal funding was the prior baseline ––and shrinking the scope of an “adverse effect”; it places review deadlines on projects, and offers program alternatives to fast-track approvals; and sets a 150-day limit to court challenges. BAAJA would render public input limited and optional, narrow what is deemed historic property, and diminish requirements for federal agencies to consult with Native nations. Despite its innocuous framing as “permitting reform,” the bill would allow tech oligarchs to legally circumvent the communities and tribes that clearly oppose expensive and extractive projects on their land.

Treaties — the supreme law of the land, alongside the Constitution — require nation-to-nation relations for all projects impacting tribal nations. BAAJA virtually eliminates whatever parity remains in this relationship.

BAAJA’s own name claims the bill is about affordability, and many proponents say it will create jobs and advance clean energy infrastructure. But the oil industry-backed bill, with roughly a page per year since that first colonial meal, pushes aside the land, water, and people who gave the Pilgrims food. BAAJA is championed first and foremost by the GOP, but it’s become a bipartisan bill. Fifteen Democrats pushed it through the Senate the same week that Capitol Police arrested Indigenous activists protesting the bill like Krystal Two Bulls, executive director of Honor the Earth. Her organization advocates against the “green colonialism” this bill is attempting to legally codify.

The Native American Rights Fund (NARF), the largest legal advocacy organization for tribes in the U.S., issued a social media statement: “You may have recently heard from certain members of Congress that BAAJA would help clean energy without weakening environmental protections or Tribal rights,” it said. “NARF attorneys reviewed the bill and found a different story: fewer safeguards, less say for Tribal Nations and the public, and fewer ways to stop harmful projects.”

Meanwhile, media pundits like Jason Hayes, a research fellow at The Heritage Foundation, promote the bill’s emphasis on expediting permitting, framing the bill as providing cost- and time-saving mechanisms, and suggesting their reversal would risk corporate resources. Ezra Klein, a self-described liberal commentator at The New York Times, backs the bill, but tramples tribes by omission, never saying “Native American,” “Indigenous,” or “tribes” as he lays out his public support.

Klein’s advocacy for permitting reform is unsurprising, considering that it is central to a bestselling book he co-wrote, Abundance. But it carries a colonial logic of unlimited extraction with a greenwashed veneer. “We need to build and invent more of what we need,” Klein says. But who is “We”? Here it’s a pronoun that excludes tribes, and refers abstractly to technology and infrastructure development without context or consequence for the builder and the alleged beneficiaries. Such framing of development is greenwashing: a marketing practice that presents a product, policy, or company as more environmentally friendly …
