content:
Auteur·e

: Agustín Guillamón

Titre

: Les comités de défense de la CNT à Barcelone (1933-1938)

Date

: 2017


 Tampon du Comité de Défense Local de Barcelone


LES COMITÉS DE DÉFENSE DE LA CNT À BARCELONE (1933-1938)


 Des Cadres de Défense aux Comités révolutionnaires de Quartier, aux Patrouilles de contrôle et aux Milices Populaires


AGUSTÍN GUILLAMÓN


 Première édition en espagnol : avril 2011. Seconde édition en espagnol : septembre 2011. Aldarull edicions. Barcelone.


 Ce livre a été traduit par le Collectif Anarchiste de Traduction et de Scannérisation (CATS) de Caen (et d’ailleurs) en avril et mai 2012, avec le concours précieux de l’auteur. Merci à S. de “La Bataille Socialiste” (

http://bataillesocialiste.wordpress.com/

) pour la mise en relation avec l’auteur. D’autres traductions subversives du CATS sont librement téléchargeables et diffusables sur son site :

http://ablogm.com/cats/


 Un premier brouillon initial (très bref) de ce travail fut publié dans le numéro extraordinaire de Solidaridad Obrera (janvier 2010) dédié au centenaire de la CNT.


 Plus de dirigeants, plus d’État Pour profiter de nos combats.


 — Raoul Vaneigem, La vie s’écoule, la vie s’enfuit


 Vivere militare est.


 — Sénèque. Lettres


 I didn’t say it would be easy, Neo. I just said it would be the truth.


 — Morpheus dans Matrix, Larry et Andy Wachowski.


 « Les révolutions sociales, ces tentatives de réorganisation de la production et de la société sur des nouvelles bases, sont extrêmement rares dans l’Histoire. Au delà des circonstances particulières dans lesquelles elles surgirent, elles nous apportent toujours une expérience irremplaçable, dans leurs succès comme, surtout, dans leurs échecs. Le grand enseignement de la révolution de 1936 a été la nécessité incontournable de la destruction de l’État ».


 Barricade construite le 19 Juillet 1936 sur le Paralelo, face à « El Molino ». Ici les Comités de Défense et le Syndicat du Bois de la CNT mirent en déroute l’armée soulevée.


1. DU RAPPORT DE SHAPIRO À CELUI D’OCTOBRE 1934


 Un rapport confidentiel, à la diffusion réduite, d’Alexandre Shapiro

[1]

, secrétaire de l’AIT, élaboré durant son séjour en Espagne en 1932-33, relatait ce qu’étaient et comment fonctionnaient les Comités de Défense, organisés exclusivement pour des tâches insurrectionnelles de choc, comme celle du 8 janvier 1933, dont il fut témoin. Ce rapport de Shapiro, sur les Comités de Défense, fut réalisé en pleine polémique entre FAIstes et trentistes

[2]

 sur l’opportunité, ou non, de la tactique d’insurrection immédiate, localiste et permanente. Shapiro fit une critique dévastatrice de l’improvisation, du manque d’organisation et de préparation de l’insurrection de janvier. Il dénonça, avec dureté, le fait qu’une même personne puisse détenir des charges aux secrétariats de la CNT et du Comité National de Défense, pour le confusionnisme que cela créait. Il démontra que, dans la pratique, s’était produite une soumission de la CNT aux décisions du Comité National des Comités de Défense (CNDC).


 Le rapport de Shapiro, qui bénéficiait de l’aide inestimable d’Eusebio Carbó, décrivait de cette manière les Cadres de Défense, existants en 1933 : « Ces Comités de Défense, qui existaient déjà depuis un certain temps, avaient comme unique but de préparer les armes nécessaires en cas d’insurrection, d’organiser les groupes de choc dans les différents quartiers populaires, d’organiser la résistance des soldats dans les casernes etc… ».


 Alors même que l’insurrection des Asturies était encore en cours, le CNCD constatait, dans un rapport

[3]

, l’échec de la tactique insurrectionnelle, défendue par le groupe Nosotros, connue populairement sous le nom de « gymnastique révolutionnaire », qu’il accusait précisément d’être responsable du manque de préparation de la CNT pour intervenir, au niveau national, dans l’insurrection d’octobre 1934. Le moment était venu de dépasser cette tactique, parce qu’elle avait démontré le caractère absurde et dangereux d’une insurrection locale à un moment inadéquat, sans une sérieuse préparation préalable, qui soumettait les libertaires à la répression étatique, sans jamais obtenir une extension populaire à tout le pays, ni l’adhésion des autres organisations, nécessaire pour affronter avec succès l’appareil militaire et répressif de l’État. Le pire de tout est que cette répression avait démantelé l’appareil militaire clandestin de la CNT, après les insurrections …

author: Reddebrek
title: Weltkrise – Weltwende. Kurs auf den Staatskapitalismus, Carl Steuermann (Otto Rühle)
content:
Weltkrise - Weltwende. Kurs auf Staatskapitalismus.

Zum vierten Male meldet der deutsche Kapitalismus seinen Bankrott an. Das erstemal erschien er in der Montur des geschlagenen Frontsoldaten. Der Weltkrieg war verloren, der Traum von einer Weltherrschaft grau- sam zerstört. Das Volk wurde geschüttelt von Hunger, Elend, Erschöpfung, Verzweiflung. Aber von einemBan- krott der Wirtschaft wollte es nichts wissen. Es wies den Hiobsboten ab und sang: Deutschland, Deutschland über alles ! Da folgte der ersten Meldung aufdem Fuße die zweite . Der sie überbrachte, sprach mit der Stimme des Revolu- tionärs . Denn dem militärischen Zusammenbruch war die Revolution gefolgt. „Sozialismus oder Untergang in Barbarei !" lautete die Losung. „Es gibt keine andere Ret- tung als östliche Orientierung, Rätesystem, Diktatur des Proletariats, Sozialisierung !" Lähmendes Entsetzen packte dieBourgeoisie. Kaumdaß sie es selber glaubte, stammelte sie unter Zittern und Beben: „Wiederaufbau ! Wir kom- men wieder hoch!" Begeistert und hoffnungsgläubig ant- wortete ihrdasEchoderMassen: ,,Jawohl,Wiederaufbau ! " Und der Revolutionär wurde blutig niedergeschlagen. Das drittemal erfolgte die Bankrotterklärung auf den

Trümmern der Inflation. Das Ende schien wirklich ge- kommen. Millionen waren zu Bettlern geworden und ver- sanken in das Nichts der Existenzlosigkeit. Aber sie klam- merten sich mit dem Mute der Verzweiflung an den Stroh- halm eines letzten Versuchs. „Deutschland kann nicht, darf nicht untergehen ! ... " Nun ist die vierte Bankrottansage da. Der Angstschrei der Weltwirtschaftskrise hat sie verkündet. Die Börsen krachen. Fundamente der Industrie wanken. Zusammen- brüche folgen. Panik greift um sich. Mehr als zwanzig Millionen Menschen stehen brotlos auf der Straße und fordern Arbeit. Fast die Hälfte aller Menschen fristet das Leben von öffentlicher Fürsorge. Überall Verschuldung, Korruption, Bankrott, Weltuntergangsstimmung. Was soll werden ? fragt verstört und kopflos einer den andern. So kann es nicht weitergehen ! versichert triviale Gassen- weisheit von Mund zu Mund. Keiner weiß Rat. Jeder weiß nur oder hat das untrügliche Gefühl: diesmal ist es ernst mit der Konkursmeldung. Es gibt keine Hoffnung und Hilfe mehr. Der Kapitalismus ist am Ende. In der Tat : das ist das Ende. Aber wo wäre ein Ende ohne neuen Anfang? Ein Untergang ohne Auferstehen ? Die Weltgeschichte geht weiter. Und so lange es Menschen gibt, die leben wollen, werden diese Menschen arbeiten, schaffen, wirtschaften, um ihr Leben zu fristen. Nicht die Wirtschaft geht zugrunde, sondern nur die Wirtschaft des Kapitalismus. Es ist die heute herrschende, in Europa und Amerika, in den fortgeschrittenen Regionen des Erdballs führende Wirtschaftsform, die zum Untergang verurteilt ist. Das Ende eines Systems. Nicht das Ende der Wirt- schaft überhaupt. Die Weltkrise wird zur Weltwende. Dem Niederbruch folgt Aufstieg. Das Chaos gebiert eine neue Ordnung. II Wirwissen noch nichts über Tempo, Art und Ausmaße der Ereignisse, die uns bevorstehen. Kennen nicht Dauer und Phasen des Prozesses, den wir durchlaufen müssen. Ahnen noch nicht die Kämpfe, die wir werden auszu- fechten haben. Nicht die Opfer, die eine erbarmungslose Entwicklung von uns verlangt. Wir tappen ins Ungewisse. Eins nur scheint uns gewiß zu sein: daß das nächste große System der Wirtschaft, das dem Kapitalismus not- wendig folgt, der Sozialismus sein wird. Zu ihm führt freilich ein langer Weg. Wahrscheinlich ein mühseliger, schwerer, opferreicherWeg mit vielen Stationen undÜber- gängen, Etappen und Zwischenräumen. Wenn nicht alle Zeichen trügen, ist die nächste Etappe dieser Menschheitswanderung eine Art Staatskapitalismus. Der Kurs der Geschichte, in deren Wirbeln wir stehen, ist auf ihn gerichtet. Folgen wir diesem Kurs!

author: Unknown
title: The PKK founding Congress and its aftermath
content:
This article is compiled from a piece written by Duran Kalkan and published in a special edition of

 Serxwebûn

marking the 30th anniversary of the founding of the PKK.


Part one can be read

here

.


Memories from the Congress


To share some details or recollections concerning the PKK founding congress, the following can be said: When the meeting had concluded and everyone was preparing to get up and leave, Leader Apo made a remark outside the formal proceedings, while everyone was still present. He said: “From now on, you will get money from your fathers, bring it in and pay your party dues.”


This was because everyone present, as delegates who had participated in the congress, had become members of the party whose establishment had just been decided. According to the party statutes that had been adopted, membership required the regular payment of party dues. Following the definition of membership used by communist parties in the actually existing socialist system, the PKK's founding statutes also defined a member as follows: “A party member is someone who accepts the party programme and statutes, works continuously in one of the party's organisational structures, and regularly pays dues to the party.”


In practice, however, none of the PKK cadres were employed in any kind of work. Individually, they had no money either. Within their communal way of life, their daily needs for food, drink and clothing were met through the party's resources. In these circumstances, rather than paying dues to the party, they were simply surviving on the resources provided by the party. For this reason, nobody had the money to pay regular membership dues. Leader Apo drew attention to this contradiction, saying: “You will get money from your fathers, bring it in and pay your dues if you want to become members.”


Yet the PKK cadres did not even maintain relations with their fathers. Everyone had broken away from their families. Thus, there was a significant difference and contradiction between the PKK as formally defined in its statutes and the PKK as it actually existed in practice. By the time of the congress, the communal way of life that had developed within the PKK meant that cadres devoted their entire lives, all twenty-four hours of the day, to party work. They had to be ready at all times to fulfil the party's duties and responsibilities and participate in its activities as fighters. This was the practical reality. However, the definition incorporated into the statutes took as its model the bureaucratic conception of membership used by communist parties. This was considered the appropriate definition for becoming a revolutionary party, and it was adopted accordingly. Yet, in the concrete conditions of Kurdistan, party-building along those lines produced no results and led to no development. The actual requirements of the practical circumstances demanded a different kind of party cadre: someone who lived continuously within a communal system and worked on party responsibilities twenty-four hours a day.


On the one hand, this demonstrated that the PKK was, in practice, detached from the actually existing socialist system and its bureaucratic structure. On the other hand, it also revealed aspects of the PKK that sought to imitate that system and had been influenced by it. This shows that, during its emergence and founding period, both tendencies existed side by side within the movement. Another incident took place after Leader Apo made this remark and smiled slightly. A person named Davut then intervened, saying, “We've forgotten something.” He suggested: “Before the congress disperses, let's also decide where and when the second congress will be held, and then we can leave.”


Leader Apo turned towards him and replied: “How can we possibly know now where and when the second congress will take place? By the time of the second congress, either we will have liberated Kurdistan or we will have disappeared.” This incident also reveals something about the different attitudes among the participants. Someone participating from a highly bureaucratic and passive political perspective, lacking a revolutionary understanding of what it meant to be a pioneering party, assumed that it was possible to make decisions four years in advance. One section of the congress participants was thus so detached from reality and from an understanding of the party and organisation.


On one side stood the party and organisational consciousness …

author: Unknown
title: Women's resistance will create a free society
content:
Free Women’s Units (YJA Star) guerrillas talked about 25 November, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, in detail and outlined the perspective of the women's struggle. The struggles waged during the 20th century secured greater rights for women, and the women's struggle gradually expanded. As the women's struggle grew, specific days were designated for women to make their voices heard more strongly. 25 November is one of the days when women take to the streets to struggle. On this day, women condemn violence against women and demonstrate how they intend to develop their struggle against it. Violence imposed on women continues systematically. The growing number of femicides that remain unresolved is a consequence of the misogynistic policies of the male-dominated mentality.


YJA Star guerrillas drew attention to how women must organize against the existing system.


 


YJA Star guerrilla Besê Serhed:

First and foremost, we respectfully commemorate all women who have paid a price for women's freedom and renew our pledge to continue the struggle. November 25, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, emerged as a result of a tremendous struggle. We are therefore proud of the gains we have achieved today. Women have created opportunities for themselves through their struggle. We know that the price of freedom is not easy to pay, but victory will ultimately be achieved despite all the difficulties. We see this in the women who have achieved their goals by making sacrifices. The progress of every woman is something we must pay close attention to, and it brings us happiness. Taking responsibility for women's advancement is one of the fundamental aspects of the struggle.


The killing of women throughout history and to the present day has been one of the greatest sources of our anger. The more universal the women's struggle becomes, the greater its gains will be. As Kurdish women, we want to advance the universal struggle of women. The process initiated by Leader Apo (Abdullah Öcalan) represents a crucial period for women in terms of expanding their areas of struggle and strengthening women's organizations. We are currently working in the mountains to advance this struggle. All women must work for their own freedom and take part in the struggle. If this struggle grows, the sphere of male domination will shrink, and men will no longer be able to attack women or children so easily. As YJA Star guerrillas, we believe that solidarity among women will grow stronger in this regard.


Our struggle is for all women


 


YJA Star guerrilla Sarya Riha:

I, too, commemorate all women who have struggled and bow respectfully before their memory. The patriarchal system was founded on the annihilation of women and has been maintained in an organized manner. Women are the foundation of society; when women are enslaved, society is enslaved as well. Women's struggle has always developed in response to the reality of male-dominated power. YJA Star and the Party of Free Women of Kurdistan (PAJK) are examples of this. Leader Apo developed the following idea concerning women: 'Free Women, Free Homeland.' This idea reveals the reality of women and their influence on life. Our struggle aims to turn this reality into practice. We wage our struggle not only through armed means but also at the level of mentality. This is why the women's movement is facing a comprehensive attack, and this reality is clearly visible. Time and place do not matter when it comes to taking part in the struggle; what matters is that every woman can struggle wherever she is.


Women's identity is universal, and raising consciousness means ensuring that all women acquire knowledge and awareness. Women's consciousness must be developed further every day and reach society as a whole. The struggle takes its most meaningful form and achieves its objective when it is waged for the whole of society. The state is responsible for the fact that femicides continue today and their perpetrators go unpunished. These murders are deliberately committed and covered up. Women must organize and further strengthen solidarity among themselves in the face of attacks by the patriarchal system. Women's movements have been established, but all women must take part in these movements. The most effective form of defense can be achieved through organization. Women must recognize their responsibility in the process initiated by Leader Apo …

title: Bayık: Öcalan developed a new paradigm for socialism and for humanity
content:
Kurdistan Communities Union (KCK) Executive Council Co-Chair Cemil Bayık discussed the conditions surrounding the establishment of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK), the sociological and political atmosphere of Kurdish society in the 1970s, the values created through half a century of struggle and the movement's strategy for the new period in a special program broadcast on Stêrk TV.


The first part of this interview can be read

here

. 


When you went to the founding congress, did you attend as a delegate? Had the delegates been selected beforehand? Were they selected region by region? How did it work?


When the PKK’s founding congress was held, delegates were appointed from every area. Each area selected its own delegates. These delegates then came and attended the congress. However, Comrade Kemal Pir did not attend because he was in prison. Comrade Mehmet Karasungur also did not attend the congress because he was engaged in the struggle in Siverek-Hilvan. Both of them were delegates. Apart from these two, all the delegates selected in the different regions were present.


Which area were you a delegate from?


I was the Elazığ delegate. I attended the founding congress on behalf of Elazığ.


Was Öcalan a delegate from Riha (Urfa)?


We did not specify which area Önder Apo [Abdullah Öcalan] represented as a delegate. Önder Apo attended on behalf of all Kurdistan.


If we go back to the group’s early days, more than half a century has passed. An unprecedented struggle has been waged. As a result of this struggle, what gains have the Kurdish people, Kurdish society, and oppressed peoples achieved? Could you talk a little about these achievements?


Things that took a hundred years to happen in other countries were accomplished by the PKK in approximately fifty years. And it did so under extremely difficult conditions. That is why everyone says that Önder Apo accomplished what everyone else said was impossible. In Turkish, they say,

“The man who turns the impossible into the possible.”

 This is a reality. It is no easy task to raise up and revive a society that has given up on itself, that has reached the point of wanting to destroy itself, and to enable that society to reclaim its own identity. Raising such a society to its feet is extremely difficult anywhere in the world. Those who have managed to do so have taken hundreds of years. Önder Apo accomplished this in fifty years. This is why it is so significant.


For this reason, the history that the PKK has developed in Kurdistan is an honourable one. It is a history of progress and achievement. The PKK developed a spirit, a belief, a will and a consciousness within Kurdish society and among Kurdish people. As a result, profound changes took place in Kurdish society. The PKK developed revolutions within the revolution itself. It did not develop just one revolution, but many. If great changes have taken place in Kurdish society, if the Kurdish people have today become a people leading the way towards democracy and freedom in the Middle East, and if everyone places their hopes in the Kurdish people, this is thanks to the PKK’s struggle. The PKK has brought many gains not only to the Kurdish people but also to humanity.


Therefore, what the PKK has done is not limited to Kurdistan alone. To understand it in that way would be incomplete, even incorrect. It is true that the PKK emerged in Bakûr (North Kurdistan) and developed its struggle there. However, over time, it also had an impact on the other parts of Kurdistan. Its influence gradually extended to Rojava and, eventually, to humanity as a whole. This is the essence of the PKK’s reality. One can understand this by looking at the struggle developed by the PKK and the outcomes it has produced. The PKK brought this people, who had been completely crushed under a policy of genocide and alienated from themselves, out of that condition. In other words, the Kurdish people reclaimed themselves. A people that had been subjected to annihilation reclaimed its own identity. A people whom everyone had declared to be “no more” declared through its struggle: “I exist, and I will continue to exist.” It made the whole world accept this.


The PKK made the existence of the Kurdish people recognised by the world and by everyone. This was not easy. It came at an enormous cost and through immense suffering. This was because everyone used to say: “There were Kurds in the past, but today there are no longer any Kurds.” Everyone …

title: KON-MED calls for greater solidarity with Southern Kurdistan
content:
The Confederation of Kurdish Communities in Germany (KON-MED) has called for strengthening national unity and solidarity, stating that “the political will and national achievements of our people in Southern Kurdistan are being targeted.”


In a written statement, KON-MED said: “Following the attacks targeting the achievements of the Kurdish people in Rojava, the political will and national achievements of our people in Southern Kurdistan are now also being targeted.


The statement continued: ‘The steps taken by the Baghdad government to increase central control over Southern Kurdistan’s border crossings, oil resources and administrative powers directly affect the achievements and status of the Kurdistan Region.


As KON-MED, we state clearly: an attack on any part of Kurdistan is an attack on the shared values and future of the entire Kurdish people. We cannot consider Rojava and Başûr, Bakur and Rojhilat separately. Today, our historical responsibility is to strengthen the spirit of national unity across all four parts of Kurdistan, bring our differences together around shared national values, and collectively defend the achievements of our people.


With this awareness, we, as KON-MED, call on our people living in Germany to participate in the democratic mass demonstrations being organised against interventions targeting Southern Kurdistan, and to demonstrate our national solidarity and collective will powerfully. Our people must take to the streets wherever they are and strengthen the struggle in the spirit of national unity. Today is the day to unite, strengthen solidarity and defend our shared future!’”

title: Bûşra Muhammed Zeki: Women's hidden wounds go far beyond what is visible
content:
Human rights lawyer and activist Bûşra Muhammed Zekî spoke to ANF on the occasion of 25 November, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. Muhammed Zekî said that violence against women was not limited to physical assault, torture, forced marriage and deprivation of rights, and that new forms of violence, such as digital threats and blackmail, had become increasingly widespread with technological developments.


Muhammed Zekî said that persistent patriarchal traditions, the lack of strong legal protection mechanisms and social pressure deprived women of their fundamental rights and prevented them from participating freely in public and social life. Muhammed Zekî said, "Women's hidden wounds far outnumber those that are brought to light."


 


'What we demand is the right to be human'


Muhammed Zekî, who has worked in the field of human rights, particularly women's rights, for more than 22 years, said that defending women's rights was part of defending human rights in general. She emphasized that the right to life, equality and living in a healthy and peaceful environment were fundamental rights for everyone.


Muhammed Zekî said, "I have been working in the field of human rights in general and women's rights in particular for 22 years. What we demand is the right to be human, the right to equality and our legal rights. We want every person to be able to lead a normal, psychologically and socially healthy life."


'Violence against women has existed throughout history and continues today'


Bûşra Muhammed Zekî said that violence against women was not a new phenomenon and had existed in various forms throughout the history of societies. She said that methods of violence had also changed alongside social conditions and technological developments.


She said that preventing women from completing their education, forced marriage, degrading women's worth and dignity, sexual assault, physical violence, torture, female genital mutilation and deprivation of the right to work were among the forms of violence against women.


Muhammed Zekî also drew attention to economic violence, saying that some women were deprived of their rights to income earned through their own labor, property and inheritance.


Muhammed Zekî said, "These forms of violence are not confined to the past; they continue today. New methods of violence emerge as conditions change." She added that violence had taken new forms alongside changing social conditions.


'Digital threats are a new form of violence'


Muhammed Zekî drew attention to digital violence and threats through social media, saying that these methods had become a new means of exerting pressure on women.


Muhammed Zekî said that photographs, videos and private recordings of women could be used for threats and blackmail, regardless of whether women had shared them themselves or whether third parties had obtained them through other means. She said that such materials were used to demand money from women and make unlawful demands.


Muhammed Zekî said that such threats placed women under severe psychological and social pressure, particularly in communities where women's dignity and their families' reputations were closely tied to social values.


Muhammed Zekî said, "Digital threats can be directed against a woman through photographs, videos and recordings. She may be asked for money, threatened with damage to her reputation and forced to comply with unlawful demands. This places women under enormous psychological and social pressure."


Muhammed Zekî said that one of the factors intensifying the impact of this form of violence was the constant judgment of women by society, pointing out that the same social standards were not applied to men.


'The dagger of honor is swiftly drawn against women'


Muhammed Zekî said that one of the fundamental problems in society was that women faced greater criticism and pressure than men over their clothing, going out, education, employment and participation in public life. She said that women's behavior was often judged in terms of family and tribal honor.


Muhammed Zekî said that this approach deprived women of a free life and imposed restrictions on their choices and decisions. She continued: "In our society, many social and moral values are tied to women's existence. The dagger of honor and dignity is drawn very quickly against women. title: Kanada’dan diplomatlarına flört uygulaması ve ilişki yasağı hazırlığı: Düzenleme Çin ve Rusya’yı kapsayacak
content:
Kanada Dışişleri Bakanlığı (Global Affairs Canada), yüksek riskli ülkelerde görev yapan diplomatlara yönelik yeni güvenlik tedbirleri hazırlıyor. Kanada merkezli National Post gazetesinin üç diplomatik kaynağa dayandırdığı habere göre, hazırlanan düzenleme kapsamında diplomatların görev yaptıkları ülkelerin vatandaşlarıyla romantik ilişki kurması ve flört uygulamalarını kullanması yasaklanacak.

Düzenlemenin, özellikle istihbarat servislerini Kanada açısından tehdit olarak değerlendiren ülkelerdeki diplomatik temsilcilikleri kapsaması bekleniyor. Çin ve Rusya'nın bu ülkelerin başında geldiği belirtiliyor.

Yılın başından bu yana üzerinde çalışıldığı aktarılan politikanın ana hatlarının büyük ölçüde tamamlandığı, ancak henüz resmen yayımlanmadığı bildirildi. Kanada'nın Çin ve Rusya'daki diplomatik temsilciliklerinde görev yapan personelin önemli bölümüne düzenleme hakkında yaz aylarında bilgi verildiği, ancak uygulamanın ne zaman başlayacağının açıklanmadığı kaydedildi.

Haberde, Kanada Dışişleri Bakanlığının flört uygulamalarını yabancı istihbarat servislerinin kişisel bilgilere ulaşabileceği potansiyel araçlar olarak değerlendirdiği belirtildi.

Diplomatların romantik ilişkilerinin istihbarat faaliyetleri aracılığıyla baskı ve şantaj unsuru haline getirilebileceği, kişisel ilişkiler üzerinden hassas bilgilere ulaşılabileceği endişesi düzenlemenin gerekçeleri arasında gösteriliyor.

Hazırlanan politikanın, diplomatların üçüncü ülke vatandaşlarıyla ilişki kurmasını ise yasaklamayacağı aktarılıyor.

Kanadalı diplomatlar halihazırda yurt dışında birlikte yaşayacakları partnerleri için onay almak ve evlilik ya da birlikte yaşama öncesinde güvenlik incelemesinden geçmek zorunda.

National Post'a konuşan kaynaklara göre, düzenleme diplomatik personel arasında tartışmalara yol açtı. Özellikle dört yıllık görev süreleriyle yurt dışında çalışan bekar diplomatların kısıtlamalardan duyduğu rahatsızlık gündeme geldi.

Kanada'nın eski Rusya Büyükelçisi Alison LeClaire, güvenlik gerekçesiyle böyle bir düzenleme yapılmasını anlaşılır buldu ancak uygulamanın denetlenmesinin güç olabileceğine dikkat çekti.

Kanadalı eski diplomat ve Senatör Peter Boehm ise düzenlemenin diplomatların özel yaşamlarını tamamen sınırlandırmak anlamına gelmediğini, yurt dışında kurulan ilişkilerde daha dikkatli olunmasını amaçladığını belirtti.

Kanada Dışişleri Bakanlığı sözcüsü Rachael Dolan, taslak düzenlemenin varlığını doğrudan reddetmedi. Dolan, bakanlığın güvenlik tedbirlerini düzenli olarak yeniden değerlendirdiğini ve değişikliklerin zamanı geldiğinde duyurulacağını bildirdi.

Kanada'nın hazırlığı, ABD'nin 2025 yılında Çin'de görev yapan kamu personeline yönelik aldığı benzer kararı da gündeme getirdi.

Associated Press'in Nisan 2025'te duyurduğu karara göre ABD, Çin'deki diplomatlar, kamu çalışanları, güvenlik izni bulunan yükleniciler ve aile üyelerinin Çin vatandaşlarıyla romantik veya cinsel ilişki kurmasını yasakladı. Daha önce var olan ilişkiler için istisna başvurusu imkânı tanındı.

Soğuk Savaş dönemindeki uygulamaları hatırlatan bu tür kısıtlamalar, istihbarat faaliyetleri ve karşı istihbarat güvenliği gerekçesiyle yeniden gündeme geliyor.

Kanada'nın hazırladığı düzenlemenin kapsamı, yürürlük tarihi ve uygulama koşulları ise henüz kesinleşmiş değil.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: KDP ve YNK, Bağdat’ın kararlarını görüşmek üzere bir araya geliyor
content:
Kürdistan Demokrat Partisi (KDP) ile Kürdistan Yurtseverler Birliği’nin (YNK) üst düzey heyetleri, Irak federal hükümetinin Kürdistan Bölgesi’ne yönelik son kararlarını görüşmek üzere bugün Süleymaniye'de bir araya gelecek.

KDP heyetinde Kürdistan Bölgesi Başkanı Neçirvan Barzani, Başbakan Mesrur Barzani ve partinin bazı siyasi büro üyeleri bulunacak. YNK’yi ise parti başkanı Bafil Talabani, Başbakan Yardımcısı Kubad Talabani ve bazı siyasi büro üyeleri temsil edecek.

Görüşmede Bağdat yönetiminin kararlarının yanı sıra iki parti arasındaki ilişkilerin ve bölgedeki siyasi gelişmelerin değerlendirilmesi bekleniyor.

Irak Başbakanı Ali Falih Zeydi, 24 Kasım’da Kürdistan Bölgesi’ndeki sınır kapılarının federal yönetimin denetimine alınması ve petrol ihracatının Irak Petrol Bakanlığı’nın iznine bağlanması yönünde kararlar aldı. Kararlar, Kürt güçlerinin güvenliğini sağladığı bazı petrol sahalarının yönetiminin de bakanlığa devredilmesini öngörüyor.

Bağdat yönetimi, bu adımlara gerekçe olarak devlet bünyesindeki Kuzey Petrol Şirketi’ne ilişkin petrol kaçakçılığı iddialarını gösterdi. Irak Federal Yüksek Mahkemesi de 25 Kasım’da federal güçlerin, Kürdistan Bölgesi dahil ülkenin bütün uluslararası sınırlarında konuşlandırılabileceğine hükmetti.

Bağdat ile yaşanan gerilim sürerken KDP ile YNK arasındaki yeni hükümetin kurulmasına ilişkin anlaşmazlıklar da çözülmüş değil.

YNK Yönetim Konseyinin 25 Kasım’da Bafil Talabani başkanlığında yaptığı toplantının ardından konuşan parti sözcüsü Karwan Geznay, hükümet müzakerelerinin başlaması için iki taleplerinin bulunduğunu açıkladı.

Geznay, 4 Kasım’daki parlamento oturumunda oluşturulan başkanlık divanının feshedilmesini istedi. Ayrıca baskı, tehdit veya çeşitli vaatlerle oturuma katılmalarının sağlandığını ileri sürdüğü milletvekillerinin görevlerinden ayrılmasını talep etti.

YNK, Kürdistan Bölgesi’nin 10’uncu hükümetinin kurulmasına ilişkin taleplerini korurken Bağdat ile yaşanan sorunların çözümü için KDP ile görüşmeye açık olduğunu bildirdi.

Süleymaniye'deki görüşmenin ardından 1 Aralık’ta Bağdat’ta ulusal diyalog toplantısı yapılması planlanıyor. Irak Yüksek Yargı Konseyi Başkanı Faik Zeydan’ın çağrısıyla düzenlenecek toplantıda, federal hükümetin kararları sonrasında derinleşen krizin ele alınması bekleniyor.

Toplantıya Irak Cumhurbaşkanı Nizar Amedi, Başbakan Ali Falih Zeydi ve Meclis Başkanı Heybet Halbusi’nin yanı sıra Neçirvan Barzani, Mesrur Barzani ve Bafil Talabani’nin katılması öngörülüyor. Irak merkezli The New Region ajansının edindiği bilgilere göre ABD’nin Irak Özel Temsilcisi Tom Barrack da toplantıda yer alacak.

title: [Brochure] Sous la fumée - Canicule et anarchie
content:
L'été 2026 paraît déjà loin, et pourtant les canicules et les feux de forêt qui ont fait rage ont laissé des marques durables. Les prochains étés ne s'annoncent pas meilleurs, alors tu as devant toi «

 

Sous la fumée

 

», une brochure pour revenir sur ces catastrophes et proposer des pistes pour y faire face dès maintenant.


«

 

Nous ne pouvons pas rester spectateurs d'un monde qui se réchauffe d'année en année sous les effets de la société industrielle. Survivre en été ne devrait pas être conditionné au fait d'avoir une clim. Se balader dans une forêt ne devrait pas être conditionné au fait que 10 canadair aient éteint un incendie. Boire de l'eau ne devrait pas être conditionné au fait qu'un camion-citerne nous ravitaille. Nous étions déjà exploités, c'est maintenant notre existence même qui est menacée. Une existence qui se retrouve aussi toujours plus dépendante de l'État. Il faut briser cette spirale. Aucune douche de deux minutes au lieu de cinq, aucune course à la biocoop plutôt qu'à carrefour, aucune pétition et aucun bulletin de vote n'y changera quelque chose. Le problème est trop grand, alors nous devons développer une résistance qui le soit tout autant.

 

»

title: Ephéméride des luttes : 27 novembre
content:
Le nucléaire tue et réprime dans l'éphéméride des luttes du 27 novembre, et ce n'est pas faute d'avoir lutté contre lui. Aujourd'hui, ceux qui nous gouvernent tentent tout pour contenir notre colère. Mais ça leur pète parfois à la gueule.


1884 :

 A Chicago, première apparition du drapeau noir anarchiste lors d'une manifestation.


1917 :

 A Seattle, une rafle d'arrestations vise les militant-e-s anarchistes et anarcho-syndicalistes.


1920 :

 En Russie, Trotsky, chef de l'Armée rouge, donne l'ordre d'attaquer Makhno et les révolutionnaires anarchistes collectivistes qui tenaient une grande portion de territoire partout sur le territoire russe.


 A Barcelone, ce sont les escadrons de la mort du gouverneur qui assassinent le militant anarcho-syndicaliste de la CNT José Canela.


1964 :

 A Rome, cocktails molotov contre le Séminaire Espagnol et contre le Collège Pontifical Espagnol pour lutter contre la dictature franquiste.


1971 :

 Près de Newry en Irlande du Nord, l'IRA déclenche une fusillade contre une patrouille de l'armée britannique, faisant deux morts chez ces derniers ; en parallèle, un autre soldat est abattu par l'IRA à Belfast.


1974 :

 A Chelsea, l'IRA fait sauter deux bombes à vingt minutes d'intervalle au Musée de l'armée.


1981 :

 A Toulouse, les vitrines de deux agences d'interim qui propose de l'emploi sur le site de la centrale nucléaire de Golfech sont pulvérisées par des charges d'explosifs, revendiqué “actif toujours – radioactif jamais”.


2010 :

 Dans le Xème arrondissement de Paris, une fête d'un squat d'artistes réunissant près de 1000 personnes tourne à l'affrontement lorsque la police intervient pour tenter de gâcher la soirée de clôture avant expulsion.


2011 :

 A Donetsk, les anciens liquidateurs (les travailleurs envoyés sécuriser les lieux suite à la catastrophe) de la centrale nucléaire de Tchernobyl sont en pleine grève de la faim, lorsque la police fait irruption, faisant un mort parmi eux. Il s'appelait Gennady Konoplyov.


 En Allemagne, 1300 personnes qui bloquaient les rails pour empêcher le passage d'un convoi chargé de déchets nucléaires sont arrêtées.


2012 :

 A Maribor, deuxième plus grande ville de Slovénie, de grandes manifestations ont lieu contre la corruption du maire, exigeant le départ de plusieurs politiciens. La très forte présence policière provoque une émeute : au total, 14 véhicules de police sont détruits lors des affrontements.


2013 :

 A Santiago du Chili, une manifestation suite à la mort du syndicaliste Juan Pablo Jiménez débouche sur des affrontements au cocktail molotov sur la Alameda, l'une des principales artères de la ville et où se trouve le palais présidentiel.


 A Villa Gobernador Gálvez et à Rosario en Argentine, de grands affrontements éclatent alors que la foule tente de piller un supermarché pour subvenir à leurs besoins, suite à la hausse du coût de la vie.


2014 :

 A Athènes, le groupe 'nuits de feu' dépose du matériel explosif devant les locaux de la poste grecque en solidarité avec les anarchistes en grève de la faim Nikos Romanos et Yannis Michailidis.


2018 :

 A Paris, "Stuart, Kevin et Bob"

incendient

 une voiture du service technique de la Préfecture de Police ainsi qu'un véhicule d'Enedis (ex-EDF).

 du 27 novembre.

author: The Canadian Press
title: Marcel Colomb First Nation in Manitoba declares state of emergency over water
content:
A First Nation in northern Manitoba has declared a state of emergency over what it says is unsafe drinking water.


Marcel Colomb First Nation

 says its drinking water has taken on a sulphur smell this past week, and people have become ill.


The Assembly of Manitoba Chiefs says it stands with the First Nation and is calling on the federal government to immediately respond.


Grand Chief Kyra Wilson says citizens of Marcel Colomb should not have to live with uncertainty over the safety of their water.


She says it’s part of a larger problem, with Indigenous Services Canada confirming six First Nation communities in the province continue to face long-term drinking water advisories.


Indigenous Services Canada did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

author: The Canadian Press
title: Watchdog clears N.B. RCMP in shooting death of First Nations man in January
content:
New Brunswick’s police watchdog has cleared an RCMP officer of criminality in the shooting death of an Indigenous man earlier this year.


The Serious Incident Response Team issued its findings Friday in the January shooting death of a member of the Neqotkuk First Nation, later identified by the community as Bronson Paul.


The report says a man was shot and killed on Jan. 18 after police responded to a domestic disturbance in the community, also known as the Tobique First Nation.


It says the man kicked down the bathroom door and emerged with two broken pieces of wood with sharp ends.


When the man attacked, one officer deployed a stun gun, which the report says was ineffective.


It says the man charged a second time, then turned and charged at a second officer who fired six shots, hitting the man five times.


The report says the office’s use of force was “proportionate, necessary and reasonable in the circumstances.”


Neqotkuk Chief Ross Perley said in an interview that the report contains “untruths” including a claim that RCMP did not have an agreement with the First Nation’s leadership to contact its local tribal security when responding to calls.


Perley said the First Nation did have an arrangement in place, and it was not followed.


“There’s several mistakes that were made. At this point we feel that SIRT is a sham,” Perley said in an interview Friday.


Read more:


Neqotkuk First Nation wants Indigenous-led policing agency after fatal RCMP shooting


Police watchdog in New Brunswick and Nova Scotia hiring Indigenous investigator

Watchdog clears N.B. RCMP in shooting death of First Nations man in January

author: Daron Letts
title: Military marches on with Iqaluit forward operating location
content:
Contracts for the $5-billion forward operating location planned for Iqaluit by 2040 are scheduled to be out for tender by early 2028, according to the Department of Defence.


“I don’t think it’s wishful thinking. I think it could happen in 2028,” said project director Mike Speiser during an interview Thursday. “I’m confident.”


Iqaluit will be the last of four future forward operating locations to be built. Work in Whitehorse, Inuvik, and Happy Valley-Goose Bay, N.L., are scheduled to be tendered throughout 2027.


Delays at any of the other locations could push back Iqaluit’s tender date, Speiser added, but not by much.


“Instead of January-February, it could be spring of 2028,” he said.


The construction phase is set to begin in 2031, with site preparation beginning in 2029.


Iqaluit is last on the list because Canada’s strategic threat comes from Russia and China to the west, said Air Force Col. Patrick Dubé during an interview.


To the east, Happy Valley-Goose Bay already has more infrastructure in place, leaving Iqaluit with the most development and logistics planning needs, he added.


The Defence Department posted an advance procurement notice in April to inform industry that contract bids will soon be accepted across all four locations.


The successful companies will be responsible for overseeing subcontracts to carry out the work. Bidding in Nunavut requires adherence to article 24 in the Nunavut Agreement, which requires the federal government to provide support to Inuit firms to enable them to compete effectively for government contracts.


Iqaluit’s facility will be designed to host a fleet of visiting southern aircraft ranging from fighter jets and transport planes to marine patrol and search-and-rescue aircraft.


It will serve as the staging point for southern-based aircraft to reach remote locations across the Arctic, as part of the federal government’s North American Aerospace Defence Command

modernization plans

.


The proposed site, north of the city’s existing runway, will feature warehouses, maintenance buildings, barracks for 600 soldiers, munitions storage, and airstrips, among other structures.


The project will include some

dual-use

 infrastructure, which the municipality will build with federal funding, use and maintain, Dubé said.


Although plans are fluid, dual-use developments

may include an enhanced fire hall, increased wastewater capacity, and a multi-use building with a classroom, garage, and space to house an emergency preparedness control centre.


So far, an archeological study is complete and will soon be shared with the Inuit Heritage Trust, said project manager Chris Middleton during a public engagement session

Thursday

 at the cadet hall.


A traditional use study will soon follow, guided by wisdom from elders, he said.


An environmental site assessment and species-at-risk study are also on deck.


Members of the public with questions or concerns have somewhere to turn in the city, said Maj. Jorim Disengomoka, head of the Canadian Forces’ presence in Iqaluit, during Thursday’s public engagement.


Disengomoka moved to Iqaluit on Nov. 5 and is scheduled to remain for three years.


“I’m not going anywhere,” he said. “You can come to me and talk to me and I will relay your concerns. I will make myself available.”


He invited residents to visit his office at building 2050 on Hubbard Lane, near the port.

title: Peyman Viyan: Women are no longer victims but pioneers of struggle
content:
Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK) Co-Chair Peyman Viyan said in an assessment marking 25 November, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, that violence against women in Iran was not limited to isolated incidents but was systematically perpetuated as a result of the state's male-dominated and gerontocratic mentality. Viyan emphasized that women must intensify their struggle against these policies on the basis of self-defense and self-organization.


 


Peyman Viyan said that the struggle against violence against women was not limited to 25 November: “The struggle waged through women is a struggle for society as a whole. Women's struggle against male violence extends to every day of the year because violence against women is also perpetrated in different forms every day.”


‘The regime's ideology seeks to destroy society through women’


Viyan said that women in Eastern Kurdistan (Rojhilat) and Iran were subjected to multiple forms of violence and drew attention to the ideological objectives behind this violence. She described Iran's system of governance as male-dominated and gerontocratic, saying: “The mentality underlying the Iranian system, based on male dominance and the rule of older men, is subjecting the whole of society to a spiral of annihilation. Women bear the brunt of this violence. The policies of the Islamic Republic seek to destroy society through women.”


The Jin, Jiyan, Azadî revolution dealt the greatest blow to this sexist and religious fundamentalist ideology


Viyan said that the Jin, Jiyan, Azadî (Woman, Life, Freedom) revolution, which developed under women's leadership, dealt a severe blow to the sexist and religious fundamentalist ideology of the Iranian regime: “The Jin, Jiyan, Azadî revolution dealt the greatest blow to this sexist and religious fundamentalist ideology. It dealt a major blow to the aging mentality that maintains its grip on power by every possible means and to the ideology of the Iranian regime. This struggle and quest continue within society today.”


Peyman Viyan said that the regime was attempting to hollow out the concept of Jin, Jiyan, Azadî and the revolution itself, adding that attacks against women were not limited to physical violence but also continued on psychological and intellectual levels. Viyan said: “This is systematic and premeditated violence against women. The mentality that established the system legitimizes this violence through Sharia and laws. It maintains its power through the domination it imposes on women.”


‘The male-dominated system grants men the right to kill women’


Viyan said that femicides and suicides in Iran were particularly prevalent in Kurdistan, where the strength of the women's struggle and the development of social consciousness enabled such incidents to become public more quickly. She said that numerous femicides in other parts of Iran went unreported: “Every day across Iran, women are murdered without anyone knowing or hearing about it. This is why I say that it is a systematic order. The system itself is governed through violence.”


Peyman Viyan emphasized that violence against women was rooted in a mentality that regarded women as men's property. She said that fathers, older brothers and husbands believed they had ownership rights over women and that the regime's policies legitimized this mentality.


Viyan said that policies of impunity for femicide in Iran also reinforced this mentality: “Even someone imprisoned in Iran for killing a woman is effectively rewarded and released after a short period. This is because men are granted ownership rights; fathers, older brothers and husbands regard women as their property. The policies of the Iranian regime legitimize this notion of ownership and grant the male-dominated mentality the right to kill women every day.”


Viyan said that eliminating women's leadership in society would also lead to the collapse of society itself: “A society in which women are neither leaders nor bearers of wisdom is a society that has collapsed, become hollow and lost its essence. It becomes a society stripped of its moral and political substance. However, women are resisting and fighting against this situation today.”


‘Women no longer define themselves as victims’

title: The prison regime's impasse in the Peace and Democratic Society Process
content:
Understanding the actual course of political crises and efforts to find a solution in Turkey requires more than examining speeches delivered in parliament or statements made behind the scenes of diplomatic negotiations. One of the most concrete indicators of this process is the treatment of political prisoners.


The Peace and Democratic Society Process, which began with the call made by Nationalist Movement Party (MHP) leader Devlet Bahçeli on 22 October 2024 and entered a new stage with Abdullah Öcalan's call on 27 February 2025, has entered a new phase with the dissolution of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK), steps towards disarmament and the publication of the framework law. However, the Turkish state's failure to introduce concrete measures despite the steps taken throughout the process reveals a significant contradiction. One of the areas where this contradiction is most apparent is the situation of political prisoners. Sentence enforcement practices, isolation and disciplinary punishments imposed on prisoners largely remain unchanged, while repression has intensified in some areas.


Explaining this situation in terms of "bureaucratic resistance" or "state habits" means overlooking the essence of the issue. Prison policies in Turkey have never been merely a technical matter administered by judicial or penal institutions. On the contrary, these policies have been one of the direct means through which the state exercises its power relations with the Kurdish Movement, maintains its bargaining capacity and implements its strategy of disciplining social opposition.


The fact that prison conditions remain unchanged and practices targeting political prisoners continue as the process advances is neither a matter of negligence nor delay. It is precisely a means of preserving political asymmetry on the ground.


Sentence enforcement under administrative tutelage


One of the primary demands of the Kurdish Movement and democratic circles since the beginning of the process has been the establishment of legal guarantees and the elimination of inequalities in sentence enforcement law. However, the reality on the ground points not only to the need for legal reform but also to a regime of administrative arbitrariness in which even the implementation of existing laws is suspended.


The release of hundreds of political prisoners who have completed their legally prescribed sentences is now being postponed not through court rulings but through assessments conducted by Administration and Observation Boards, composed of prison directors, prosecutors, psychologists and administrative personnel.


The crucial point here is the function of these boards. They operate as instruments for producing political outcomes without assuming political responsibility. The government and state institutions adopt the flexible and inclusive language required by the Peace and Democratic Society Process outside prisons, while prisoners' releases are postponed for periods of three or six months on vague grounds such as "lack of good conduct," "failure to demonstrate remorse" and "institutional security." These practices maintain psychological pressure on prisoners while also restricting the political movement's room for maneuver outside prisons.


The sentence enforcement regime is thus being detached from the legal principle of predictability and transformed into a "mechanism of bargaining and discipline" that can be activated or suspended according to political circumstances. The government's attempt to transfer responsibility to the bureaucracy by saying, "We are conducting the process; releases are at the discretion of the judiciary and the boards," points to a deliberate division of responsibilities.


Fragmenting collective memory through S- and Y-type prisons


Prisons have never been merely places of confinement in the political history of the Kurdish Freedom Movement. They have been spaces of resistance where collective consciousness, shared memory and political agency were constructed, from the military coup of 12 September 1980 to the 1990s, and from hunger strikes to defense statements. The model of S-type, Y-type and high-security closed prisons that the state has rapidly expanded in recent years must be understood as a spatial response to this historical memory.


This new generation of prisons, consisting of single-person or small-capacity cells, where even the view of the sky in exercise yards is restricted by wire mesh and …

title: Guerrillas celebrate the 48th anniversary of the founding of the PKK
content:
On the occasion of the 48th anniversary of the founding of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK), members of the People’s Defense Forces (HPG) and Free Women’s Troops (YJA Star) held a commemorative and cultural event in the Qandil region. In addition to political speeches, the program featured musical and theatrical performances.


The event opened with a speech by HPG commander Seyîdxan Dersim, who extended his greetings on November 27 to PKK founder Abdullah Öcalan, the Kurdish people and the guerrilla forces, and commemorated PKK cadre Haki Karer and those fell in the freedom struggle in Kurdistan.


Seyîdxan Dersim addressed the historical significance of the founding date. He said that November 27 represented not merely the founding of a party but marked a historic transformation in the development of the Kurdish people’s political consciousness and resistance. In this context, he also commemorated figures from the PKK’s history, including Kemal Pir, Mahsum “Egîd” Korkmaz and Zeynep Kınacı (Zîlan).


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/79ccb789_20261127104611_2026-11-27-qendil-ozgurluk-gerillari-27-kasimi-buyuk-bir-cosku-ve-heyecanla-kutladi-1.mp4


Transition to a new historical phase


Seyîdxan Dersim stated that a new stage of social reconstruction and reorganization had now begun with the conclusion of the phase of national resistance

.

He identified securing Abdullah Öcalan’s physical freedom as a central task.


Following the speech, guerrillas presented a cultural program featuring songs, theatrical performances and traditional circle dances. The music group Koma Awazê Çiya also performed at the event.


On the sidelines of the event, members of the HPG and YJA Star spoke about the significance of the PKK’s historical legacy and the prospects for the ongoing Peace and Democratic Society Process. They attributed the emergence of the process to Öcalan’s efforts, the sacrifices of the Kurdish movement and the PKK’s history of resistance.


The event concluded with songs, Govend dances and chants.

title: KCK: We will do our part to protect the gains of Southern Kurdistan
content:
On November 24, the government in Baghdad announced a series of decisions aimed at strengthening federal control over border crossings and the energy sector. These include closing officially unrecognized border crossings, transferring control of oil fields in territories disputed between Baghdad and Erbil to the federal Oil Ministry, and tightening oversight of oil transportation and exports.


The Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) subsequently warned in a joint statement against interference with the constitutional rights of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, describing any violation of those rights as a red line.


The Co-Presidency of the KCK (Kurdistan Communities Union) Executive Council released a statement regarding the latest developments in Southern Kurdistan (Northern Iraq), describing the Baghdad government’s decision as a restriction of fundamental aspects of life and a direct interference with the functioning of the Kurdish federation.


The KCK statement on Saturday includes the following:


“The Iraqi Prime Minister announced that a decision had been made to transfer the oil fields and customs crossings in Southern Kurdistan to the central government. He demanded that the oil fields and customs crossings in Southern Kurdistan be handed over to the central government. This means transferring all the financial resources of the Southern Kurdistan federation to the central government. When a society and political system are deprived of financial resources, they can be rendered completely dependent. Particularly today, financial resources play an important role in establishing and sustaining economic, social, cultural and political systems. In this respect, the Baghdad government’s decision amounts to restricting fundamental aspects of life and directly interfering with the functioning of the Southern Kurdistan federation.


'Southern Kurdistan struggled for decades to secure its fundamental national rights'


The fundamental reason for the problems arising today among different ethnic, religious and national communities is the persistence of the centralized model of governance of the 19th and 20th centuries. This inevitably creates problems in political and social life. Following the establishment of Iraq, the central government’s approach of exercising power and domination led to serious conflicts with the Kurds, who rejected these policies and resisted them. However, when the decision was made to keep Southern Kurdistan within Iraq following the 1924 report of the Mosul Commission established by the League of Nations, the same commission also adopted a decision recognizing the Kurds’ right to self-government and education in their mother tongue. Yet because the Iraqi government failed to implement this decision of the Mosul Commission, Southern Kurdistan struggled for decades to secure its fundamental national rights. In 2003, the hegemonic centralist regime was overthrown, and a new constitution was drafted. Under this constitution, a more democratic political system replaced the former centralized model of government, and the Southern Kurdistan federation was recognized as a constitutional entity.


‘The Iraqi government should abandon this misguided course’


The Iraqi government’s return to a centralist approach and its efforts to restrict the rights of the Southern Kurdistan federation amount to the reimposition of the old centralist model. Yet this approach led to serious conflicts between Iraq and the Kurds for decades. In this respect, the Iraqi government is taking a misguided step. This decision will also create serious problems for Iraq’s stability and democratic unity. It would be in the best interests of both Iraq as a whole and the Kurds for the Iraqi government to abandon this misguided course and act in a manner that strengthens Iraq’s democratic unity.


'What Southern Kurdistan needs is a democratic national unity government'


Democratic Kurdish unity is extremely important to prevent the Kurds from facing such situations. The Kurds, too, must abandon centralist approaches in politics and adopt democratic unity as their guiding principle. What Southern Kurdistan needs at present is a democratic national unity government that includes all political parties. A government representing all Kurdish political parties and social groups, rather than just one or two parties, would strengthen the Kurds and the Southern Kurdistan federation. The parties’ …

title: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards reportedly preparing for an attack on Kurdish parties
content:
According to a statement by the Kurdistan Human Rights Organization, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) is preparing to attack Kurdish parties from Eastern Kurdistan (Rojhilat).


The IRGC reportedly deployed large numbers of troops, along with drones and heavy weapons, to the cities of Sardasht, Marivan, Kamyaran, Ravansar and Javanrud in Rojhilat over the past week.


The statement noted a visible increase in the military activity of IRGC forces in these cities.


The main mission of these forces is reportedly to monitor the positions and forces of Kurdish opposition parties in the highlands of Sardasht, Marivan and Shaho and to attack these locations with artillery fire and drones.


The organization also reported an increase in military deployments following the recent deaths of numerous members of the Basij and IRGC forces.

title: 15 families of the disappeared contact IHD after the discovery of human remains in Silvan
content:
Following the discovery of numerous human remains in a cave in the Silvan district of Amed (Diyarbakır) province, 15 families of victims of enforced disappearance in the 1990s have so far contacted the Human Rights Association (IHD) in Amed. The relatives hope that DNA comparisons will make it possible to identify the deceased and finally provide them with certainty about the fate of their family members. The IHD expects more families to come forward.


During an investigation ordered by the public prosecutor’s office, nine intact skulls, 36 skull fragments and hundreds of other bone fragments were recovered on Tuesday from the three-level cave in the Qesra Fila area. The human remains were transferred to the state-run Forensic Medicine Institute (ATK) in Istanbul for forensic examination. The identities of the deceased, the age of the bones and the circumstances of their deaths remain unknown.


Given the numerous cases of enforced disappearance, unsolved murders and serious human rights violations in Silvan, particularly during the 1990s, the Human Rights Association (IHD), the Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD) and the Amed Bar Association consider the discovery particularly significant for confronting the past. The organizations are calling for a comprehensive investigation that also examines how the cave was used in the past and any possible links to human rights violations committed by the state.


According to the IHD’s findings, there are at least 303 mass graves in Kurdistan that have yet to be opened. The recent discovery in Silvan is not included in this figure.

title: Arab guerrilla fighter: Leader Öcalan’s philosophy has given women great courage
content:
On the occasion of November 25, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, millions of women took to the streets to condemn femicides and violence against women.


Speaking to ANF on the occasion, Nergêz Şawîş, an Arab member of the YJA Star guerrillas, said they regarded November 25 as a day of resistance:


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/dd1b8384_20261125140215_2026-11-26-behdinan-nergez-sawis-gerilaya-yja-stare-ji-sideta-li-ser-jine-re-na-1.mp4


“Women are stronger than men because of their creative nature, and they have always proven themselves through their will and existence. The male-dominated mentality, however, oppresses women. This is why it attacks women’s legitimate rights every day. We are fighting against this denial of women’s rights. Our primary goal is to eliminate this dominant mentality. Leader Apo [Abdullah Öcalan] also states that society cannot be liberated unless women are liberated.


Society as it exists today can organize itself thanks to the existence of women. This dominant mentality is particularly widespread in Arab society. Therefore, I call on our Arab community to join hands and stand in solidarity. If you want to understand society, you must first understand women and recognize the importance of their role within it. We do not want this situation to continue. We will carry on our struggle until the very end to put an end to it. Why are women so strong within the movement today? Because Leader Apo introduced the concept of the free woman to everyone and demonstrated how influential women’s power is in life. Leader Apo showed what kind of stance women should adopt in everything, from ideological work to military activities. Women’s resistance has also been highly effective in the mountains. Leader Apo’s philosophy has given women great courage and has always placed them at the forefront because he knows that only women can bring about success. Society’s liberation will be achieved through women.


Examples of this include Comrade Sara (Sakine Cansız), martyr Zilan, martyr Bêrîtan and thousands of heroic women who have been inspired by Leader Apo’s ideas. All of his efforts are aimed at empowering women, ensuring their participation in every sphere, enabling them to believe in themselves and act through their own strength. As an Arab woman, I was inspired by the comradeship within the movement. I was also deeply impressed by women’s participation in all areas of work.”


Şawîş also addressed Arab women. She said that the role of women in the movement’s activities and the solidarity she had witnessed had influenced her decision to join the movement.

author: Rizomatica
title: Comunicado de Nelson Alonso Llempi, PPM caso Grollmus en huelga de hambre
content:
«Marri marri kom pu che, pu longko, pu machi, pu peñi, pu lamuen:


Inche Nelson Alonso Llempi, del lof Huape tuwun, padre e hijo de familia, junto a otros 10 peñi, hemos tomado la difícil decisión de iniciar una HUELGA DE HAMBRE EL DÍA 23 DE NOVIEMBRE, como medida de protesta frente a la condena desproporcionada que nos ha impuesto el Tribunal de Cañete, que en conjunto supera los 1.055 años de prisión.


Nos enfrentamos a un juicio que consideramos profundamente injusto, donde la Fiscalía sustentó sus acusaciones únicamente en cuatro supuestos testigos sin nombre ni rostro, sin una corroboración científica o técnica que respaldara sus declaraciones.


Ni nosotros ni nuestras defensas hemos tenido certeza sobre la identidad y existencia de estos supuestos testigos.


¿Cómo se puede condenar a personas a semejantes cantidades de años de prisión sin que exista la posibilidad de conocer y cuestionar debidamente a quienes nos acusan?


Para nosotros, este proceso representa una persecución de carácter político, que busca castigarnos y silenciar nuestra lucha.


Hoy, frente a esta injusticia, hemos decidido llevar adelante esta huelga de hambre, entendiendo que es uno de los pocos medios de protesta que tenemos a nuestro alcance desde la prisión.


NUESTRA EXIGENCIA ES CLARA:


– La nulidad de este juicio que consideramos injusto.- El respeto a nuestro derecho a un debido proceso.


Justicia frente a las graves irregularidades que denunciamos.


– Nuestra libertad y el respeto a nuestra dignidad.No estamos tomando esta decisión por voluntad de sufrir. Lo hacemos porque sentimos que se han cerrado los caminos para ser escuchados y porque no estamos dispuestos a aceptar en silencio una condena que consideramos injusta.


Hago un llamado a la solidaridad frente a este proceso de persecución injusto e ilegal que tiene como único fin detener la justa lucha de nuestro pueblo mapuche. Que nuestra voz salga de estos muros. Que nuestra lucha llegue a cada territorio. Que la injusticia no quede en el silencio.


No pedimos privilegios, exigimos justicia.


No buscamos compasión, exigimos que se respeten nuestros derechos y nuestra dignidad.


¡POR LA NULIDAD DEL JUICIO!¡POR LA JUSTICIA Y LA DIGNIDAD DEL PUEBLO MAPUCHE!


¡Marichiwew!


Nelson Alonso Lliempi, Cárcel de Concepción. Noviembre 27 de 2026.»


*ENVIADO A LA RADIO

Radio Kurruf

.

author: Savanna Craig
title: Canada donates to preserve tropical forests, remains top importer of Brazil’s gold
content:
Ngrenhkarati Xikrin walks along the Bacajá river, a waterway once used to fish, to swim, and a vital lifeform for her people, the Xikrin tribe. Now the river is contaminated.

 


“Today I am here to show you the Bacajá river. Look at the colour of the water,” she says, pointing to the white, muddied river.


“This is how it is: white, dirty, contaminated.”

 


Xikrin points the finger at the Belo Monte dam, a large hydroelectric dam complex on the Xingu River in the state of Pará, Brazil. The Bacajá river connects to the Xingu river. Indigenous

researchers from the Juruna tribe

 have found that not only does the dam diminish flow to the Bacajá river, but the decreased water flow has led to a proliferation of cyanobacteria. Mild reactions

include

 skin irritation, while extreme reactions can involve liver or kidney damage and paralysis. 


 

Canada donates to preserve but top importer of gold extracted from Brazil


Prime Minister Mark Carney announced Canada will give $560 million to the

Tropical Forest Forever Facility

. The money will be allocated to communities that are already doing the work to preserve their tropical forest. The $560 million comes from existing funds within Global Affair’s international climate finance budget. 20 per cent of these funds must be given to Indigenous and local communities.

 


While donating funds to preserve these forests, Canada is the top importer of Brazilian Gold, an industry located within them.

 


“We see them investing to protect our forests,” says Sol Juruna. “They are the ones who extract the most gold.”

 


Juruna is from the Arara-Juruna tribes that live along the Xingu River. She is part of the the Middle Xingu Indigenous Women’s Movement, leading the fight to protect the region from extraction and degradation.

 


The movement organizes against a gold mine project planning to extract near the Xingu river. Canadian mining company Belo Sun is vying to build the Volta Grande gold mine project in the Xingu river. This will be the largest open-pit gold mine in Brazil.

 


“There’s a huge green spot in the Bacajá River due to the hydroelectricity of Belo Monte,” says Juruna, referring to the cyanobacteria. “We know that the Belo Sun project, if it enters here in the Greater Volta do Xingu, will end up killing the river.”

 


In an email to

APTN News

, Belo Sun says it has consulted with two Indigenous communities along the Xingu river, stating the company has met “with the Juruna and Arara peoples, in accordance with the communities’ consultation protocol and plan.” 

 


Juruna says these consultations have not been legal, contributing to divided views within her community. She claims some, even family members, are threatening her.

 


“While protesting, I was threatened by a relative of mine,” says Juruna. 

 


Juruna says Belo Sun’s discussions with some community members have generated fighting not only within communities, but within families, including her own.  

 


“We have four or five different Indigenous peoples who live in the Volta Grande do Xingu,” says Ana Alfinito, a legal advisor for Amazon Watch. The group works alongside Indigenous communities to help preserve their land and the Amazon.

 


With only two tribes being approached for discussion, Juruna says, “It’s leaving the other peoples from outside, the other Indigenous communities from outside.” 

 


Belo Sun did not grant us an interview, instead sending a written letter.

 


In it, the company says the project is designed to operate without drawing water from or adversely impacting the Xingu river, adding that a further independent technical review is planned.

 


The future of the project is to be determined

 


The company’s installation license was temporarily

suspended

in October by Brazil’s supreme court. This is the second time their permit has been suspended. Belo Sun had their license related to construction and environmental licenses

previously

suspended in 2022 by a lower court after it raised concerns about consultations with communities along the Xingu river. The license was then reinstated in February 2026. 

 


Still, Amazon Watch and the Middle Xingu Indigenous Women’s Movement continue to fight against Belo Sun, until it forfeits its project in Brazil.
