author: Amy Goodman
title: After Nearly 50 Years in Prison, Leonard Peltier Says the Struggle Continues
content:
The longtime Indigenous activist discusses his conviction, childhood in boarding school and commitment to Indigenous sovereignty.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

In September 2025, Democracy Now! host Amy Goodman sat down with longtime political prisoner and Indigenous activist Leonard Peltier for his first extended television and radio broadcast interview since his release to home confinement in February 2025. Before his commutation by former President Joe Biden, the 82-year-old Peltier spent nearly 50 years behind bars. Peltier has always maintained his innocence for the 1975 killing of two FBI officers. He is expected to serve the remainder of his life sentences under house arrest at the Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa Nation in Belcourt, North Dakota. In a wide-ranging conversation, we spoke to Peltier about his case, his time in prison, his childhood spent at an American Indian boarding school and his later involvement in the American Indian Movement (AIM) and more.

“We still have to live under that, that fear of losing our identity, losing our culture, our religion,” Peltier says about his continued commitment to Indigenous rights. “The struggle still goes on for me. I’m not going to give up.”

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: In this special broadcast, we spend the hour with longtime Indigenous activist Leonard Peltier. Last February, he was released from a federal prison in Florida after spending nearly half a century behind bars for a crime he says he did not commit. President Biden, on his last day in office, commuted Peltier’s life sentence to home confinement. Biden’s decision followed mounting calls by tribal leaders and supporters around the world in a decadeslong, community-led campaign fighting for his freedom.

In the 1970s, Peltier was involved with the American Indian Movement, known as AIM. In 1975, two FBI agents and one young AIM activist were killed in a shootout on the Pine Ridge Reservation in South Dakota. Two AIM members were later arrested for killing the agents. At the trial, the jury acquitted them. Leonard Peltier was arrested later, tried separately and convicted. Peltier has always maintained his innocence.

Notable supporters of Leonard Peltier over the years have included South African President Nelson Mandela, Pope Francis and Amnesty International. Supporters of Peltier say his trial was marked by gross FBI and federal prosecutorial misconduct, including the coercion of witnesses, fabricated testimony and suppressed exculpatory evidence.

After being released in February, Leonard Peltier returned home to live on the Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa Reservation in Belcourt, North Dakota. On September 12th, Leonard Peltier celebrated his 81st birthday. People gathered throughout the day, visiting him and calling from around the world to celebrate. That night and the next day, we spoke to Leonard Peltier in his living room in his first extended TV/radio broadcast interview since his release from prison.

AMY GOODMAN: Hi. I’m Amy Goodman, host of Democracy Now!, in the home of Leonard Peltier, just recently freed from prison after 49 years. LEONARD PELTIER: Plus two months. AMY GOODMAN: Plus two months. LEONARD PELTIER: Yeah. AMY GOODMAN: I’ve spoken to you so many times, Leonard, in prison, in various prisons, several of them supermax prisons. It is quite astonishing to be here with you in person. Tell us where we are. Where are we sitting? LEONARD PELTIER: We’re sitting in my home, that was given to me by my supporters. This was not given to me by the tribe, or the government had nothing to do with it. I was released by Biden under a commutation of my sentence and home confinement. Actually, what happened was, I was — I was taken out of one prison cell and really put into another type of prison. But this is my home now. This is my home. So it’s a million times better. AMY GOODMAN: Wait, what do you mean when you say you were taken out of your prison cell after more than 49 years, and you’re saying that you’re not completely free? LEONARD PELTIER: No, no, I’m on very restrictive restrictions. Even to go to the post office, I got to call my — I call her my handler. I have to call her to go to the post office. Then, when I get back, I have to call her and tell her I’m back. Or if I go anything, if I go shopping or whatever, I have to do that. If I have to go a hundred miles …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Neuquén: en el corazón de Vaca Muerta la población se calefacciona con leña y no tiene agua de red
content:
Radio Gráfica recorrió Neuquén y recogió testimonios sobre las consecuencias del modelo de explotación de Vaca Muerta. En localidades cercanas a uno de los principales yacimientos de hidrocarburos del país, vecinos y vecinas todavía deben calefaccionarse con leña o garrafas y dependen de camiones y bidones para acceder al agua potable.


Escuchar el reporte de Radio Gráfica


El informe, titulado El saqueo de Vaca Muerta, reúne las voces de referentes sociales, integrantes de comunidades mapuches y especialistas que cuestionan que la riqueza generada por la actividad hidrocarburífera no se traduzca en mejores condiciones de vida para la población local.


La docente y militante Soledad Salaburu puso el foco en la contradicción entre la magnitud de la producción de gas y las condiciones de vida de quienes habitan la provincia. “Vaca Muerta es la tercera, en Neuquén, en la producción de gas mundial y no tenés gas en el pueblo. La gente tiene garrafas, se calefacciona con leña”, señaló.


El acceso al agua potable es otra de las problemáticas que atraviesan a las comunidades. Lef Nawel, integrante de la Confederación Mapuche de Neuquén, explicó que el abastecimiento depende de camiones, mientras que las empresas petroleras cuentan con infraestructura propia para garantizar el suministro de agua a sus operaciones.


“El agua la traen camiones, contrario a la realidad de todas las petroleras que tienen agua atrás de los acueductos que abastecen de agua a las petroleras”, afirmó.


Liliana Romero, del Lof Futa Xayen, también describió las dificultades que enfrentan para acceder al agua segura. Según relató, la contaminación de las napas impide utilizar el agua de pozo para consumo humano.


“Acá abajo también nos traen agua en bidón porque contaminaron toda la napa de agua. Antes nosotros teníamos. Es más, nosotros para regar todas las plantas y para bañarnos sacamos agua de acá del pozo, pero para tomar, tomamos esas aguas que nos traen en bidón”, contó.


El informe también recupera propuestas para discutir otro modelo energético, que priorice las necesidades de la población y el desarrollo industrial nacional. Juan Manuel Ramos, del Movimiento para la Recuperación de Nuestro Petróleo, planteó la necesidad de avanzar hacia un esquema que garantice energía accesible y agregue valor a los recursos naturales mediante la industrialización en el país, en lugar de concentrarse en la exportación de materias primas.


Por su parte, Fernando Gómez, de Infonativa, sostuvo que Argentina debe recuperar la capacidad de definir su propia política energética. “La Argentina necesita recuperar lo básico, lo esencial, que es volver a definir desde nuestros propios zapatos qué modelo energético queremos. Vaca Muerta no puede quedar presa del apetito del redespliegue norteamericano”, expresó.


El trabajo de Radio Gráfica pone en discusión quiénes se benefician de la explotación de los recursos energéticos y qué impacto tiene ese modelo en los territorios donde se desarrolla. El informe completo

está disponible en el canal de YouTube de Radiográfica FM 89.3

.

title: Pentagon Weighs $15 Billion Loan to Startup With Ties to Trump Jr.
content:
The startup plans to use AI and robotics to build factories producing munitions, drones and other military equipment.

The startup plans to use AI and robotics to build factories producing munitions, drones and other military equipment.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

In what would rank among the largest government loans in U.S. history, the Pentagon is considering extending $15 billion to a California-based startup with financial ties to Donald Trump Jr., according to interviews and records reviewed by ProPublica.

The award would be one of the biggest the federal government has given to a firm connected to the Trump family and would go to a defense contractor with a largely untested track record.

The startup, Hadrian Automation, has attracted over a billion dollars in private investment in recent months on the promise that it can build factories that use AI and robots to more efficiently produce precision components for defense, aerospace and other industries.

If approved, the loan would be almost twice the value of the entire company, based on estimates from a round of financing this summer. Hadrian announced that round of investment included “major participation by 1789 Capital,” the venture capital firm that Trump Jr. joined as a partner after his father was elected in November 2024. 1789 also invested in the company in 2025.

A spokesperson for 1789 Capital said it holds a “minority stake” in Hadrian, but the total size of its share has not been disclosed.

The potential loan is 10 times the size of the largest deal the Pentagon has made in a recent lending spree.

According to Pentagon documents, a loan to Hadrian would be used to build a dozen “automated factories” in a partnership with other defense companies and potentially commercial ones to expand production of munitions, drones and other equipment.

The U.S. military has been dealing with a severe shortage of some types of munitions because of the wars in Ukraine and Iran, though it’s unclear if the factories are an attempt to address those particular shortages.

The size and structure of the deal would form an interdependence between the company and the federal government that could run afoul of long-standing guidance on how to protect taxpayer money, former Defense Department officials said. The government would use taxpayer money to vastly expand a fledgling defense contractor, which it would then presumably award contracts to, essentially paying the company money that it could use to repay the loan.

Pentagon staff have also raised several concerns about Hadrian, including its ability to expand and hire fast enough, the documents show.

The loan is under consideration weeks before Democrats take control of both chambers of Congress. The party’s leaders have vowed to use their new oversight powers to scrutinize the raft of contracts and other actions by the Trump administration that have financially benefited the Trump family and others who work in the administration or have ties to it.

Since the start of President Donald Trump’s second term, firms in which his elder sons hold stakes have won billions of dollars in federal backing. ProPublica recently reported on the Trump administration awarding nearly $40 million to one company to screen for Ebola and other infectious diseases. We also revealed how a White House aide intervened to secure a Pentagon loan of $620 million to Vulcan Elements, a rare earth magnet startup, a few months after 1789 Capital invested in it.

Responding to a question about whether the White House, Trump Jr. or 1789 lobbied for the loan, the Pentagon said in a statement that no company receives preferential treatment. “Outside affiliations, investors, or political connections play absolutely no role in the Department’s funding decisions.”

A Pentagon spokesperson also cast the loan discussions with Hadrian as being in “early stages” and disputed that the potential deal was for $15 billion. The spokesperson characterized the size of the Hadrian loan that is under discussion as not extraordinary, saying multibillion-dollar deals with other companies had been agreed to but not yet announced.

In a statement, 1789 Capital said it does not get involved in government contracts sought by the companies it invests in but is excited about Hadrian. “Our thesis is to invest in American companies that are rebuilding …

author: Dominique Gené - Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: Indigenous services minister asks Nunavik leaders to identify priorities for Ottawa
content:
Indigenous Services Minister Mandy Gull-Masty is asking Nunavik’s regional leaders to identify their most pressing priorities so she can bring them to Ottawa.


Gull-Masty, who is also the Liberal representative for Nunavik in Parliament, joined the Kativik Regional Government’s quarterly council meeting in Kuujjuaq by Zoom on Thursday.


“I’m here to teach the government what the needs are in the region,” Gull-Masty told councillors. “I have good working relationships with many ministers. I have a good working relationship with the Prime Minister’s Office. So, you have a very strong voice for the region.”


Several councillors identified housing as a priority, calling for long-term federal commitments.


Puvirnituq Coun. Lucy Qalingo asked that rehabilitation centres for survivors of sexual abuse to be prioritized. Kangirsuk Coun. Minnie Annahatak echoed that need.


“We’re to be intergenerational curse-breakers,” Annahatak said.


Annahatak also called for improved access to health and social services, specialized equipment for search and rescue and funding for municipal infrastructure.


Kuujjuaq Coun. Jonathan Grenier raised concerns about old infrastructure in Nunavik, such as the airport in Kuujjuaq, which was built in 1942 by American forces before being handed over to the Canadian government in 1945.


“That shows the lack of investment in our region,” Grenier said. “It seems easy for provincial and federal governments to set our priority lists aside and focus on the broader population, where there are more votes and greater visibility for projects.”


He also asked for funding to build a new fire hall in Kuujjuaq.


“The old fire hall is 75 years old, and now we’re now facing a situation where we don’t have anywhere to put our equipment and vehicles,” he said.


Gull-Masty acknowledged the challenges councillors raised and said she wants to meet with each municipality and review their community and strategic plans to better understand their needs.


She said she would work with other federal ministers and the Quebec government to improve service delivery in Nunavik.


“It’s important that we work together and that Nunavik has a strong voice when decisions affecting the region are being made,” she said.

author: Publicación Abierta
title: México_Oaxaca: De las barricadas a los algoritmos
content:
México_Oaxaca


De las barricadas a los algoritmos: el legado de la APPO en la comunicación comunitaria


Kiado Cruz reflexiona

, en el número más reciente de la revista 

El Topil

, sobre los aprendizajes de la revuelta del 2006 y los nuevos desafíos para defender la memoria, las lenguas y la autonomía de los pueblos frente al control de las plataformas digitales.


A veinte años del movimiento social de 2006, la experiencia de la 

Asamblea Popular de los Pueblos de Oaxaca (APPO)

 mantiene vigentes sus enseñanzas sobre comunicación comunitaria, organización colectiva y defensa de la autonomía, aunque ahora enfrenta nuevos desafíos relacionados con el control algorítmico y la inteligencia artificial.


En su reflexión titulada 

De la barricada a la red algorítmica: lo que nos dejó la APPO en comunicación comunitaria

, el comunicador Kiado Cruz, de SURCO-INDIGITAL, recuerda cómo la toma de medios, las radios comunitarias, el video independiente y las plataformas digitales se convirtieron en herramientas fundamentales para romper el cerco informativo y documentar la resistencia popular.


Uno de los ejemplos fue Oaxaca Libre,

 portal de contrainformación que surgió el 14 de junio de 2006 como respuesta a la criminalización de la protesta y la necesidad de comunicar lo que ocurría en las calles. El proyecto funcionó como un espacio colectivo para compartir información, resguardar testimonios y construir una narrativa propia del movimiento.


Cruz identifica tres aprendizajes centrales de aquella experiencia: 

apropiarse de la tecnología para ponerla al servicio de la comunidad,

 construir información desde la confianza y el testimonio directo, y documentar la resistencia para generar solidaridad y preservar la memoria histórica.


Sin embargo, 

también reconoce errores, 

como privilegiar las imágenes de enfrentamientos y barricadas sobre las experiencias cotidianas de organización, convivencia y construcción comunitaria.


Actualmente, advierte, el desafío ha cambiado. Mientras en 2006 la lucha consistía en romper el monopolio informativo, hoy enfrenta la concentración de las plataformas digitales, 

la desinformación y el extractivismo de datos

, lenguas y conocimientos comunitarios por parte de corporaciones tecnológicas.


Ante este escenario, plantea fortalecer la soberanía tecnológica mediante servidores comunitarios, redes propias, software libre y mecanismos de gobernanza colectiva que protejan los datos como patrimonio de los pueblos.


Su reflexión concluye con una idea central: el legado de la APPO sigue vigente porque comunicar no consiste únicamente en transmitir información, sino en defender la memoria, la autonomía y el tejido social. 

Comunicar es sembrar soberanía.

El Topil 59. A 20 años de la APPO: ¿qué nos dejó? – EDUCA

author: Publicación Abierta
title: Cosas que he pensado antes de ir a votar
content:
Albano-Dante Fachín Pozzi


Lo más importante de las campañas electorales no ocurre en los mítines de los partidos ni en los debates televisivos, sino a pie de calle.


Todos lo hemos vivido estos últimos días: en el trabajo, con los amigos, con la familia y con los vecinos. Durante estos días, todos juntos dedicamos más tiempo de lo habitual a «hablar de política» y, aunque en muchas conversaciones puedan escucharse auténticas barbaridades, creo que esta «politización de las conversaciones» es muy positiva para la salud de la sociedad.


Personalmente, he intentado seguir de cerca la campaña, leer todo lo que ha escrito gente cuyo criterio considero valioso y hablar y debatir con las personas de mi entorno personal y político. Con todo esto en mente, he escrito el texto que sigue a continuación.


Espero que, independientemente del sentido de su voto, los lectores encuentren alguna reflexión o algún dato interesante.


Escribo este texto teniendo absolutamente claro que, pase lo que pase en las elecciones del domingo, el lunes los catalanes seguiremos teniendo un problema: España.


Gobierne la España de derechas o la España de izquierdas, el lunes los catalanes seguiremos estando obligados a entendernos para hacer frente a España. Votemos lo que votemos el 29N.


El miedo sirve para mantener a la gente bajo control. Esto lo saben desde hace siglos todos los opresores. Los españoles también. Por eso colgaron la cabeza de Moragues dentro de una jaula durante nueve años en las murallas de Barcelona.


El miedo ha sido una herramienta fundamental de los españoles para controlar Cataluña. Y por eso siguen haciendo todo lo posible para meternos el miedo en el cuerpo. El PP y VOX nos meten miedo con sus propuestas, y también nos lo meten el PSOE y quienes le dan su apoyo. Todos nos necesitan asustados.


En España viven de esto y, en Cataluña, unos cuantos también viven muy bien: si los catalanes tienen miedo, hacer política resulta muy fácil: no hace falta cumplir ningún pacto, no hace falta realizar inversiones, no hace falta respetar nuestra lengua… Para controlar a los catalanes basta con enseñarles la cabeza de Moragues cuando se acercan las elecciones.


Entiendo el mecanismo y no culpo a quienes sienten miedo. Todos tenemos miedo. El miedo se contagia como la peste y ninguno de nosotros es inmune. Y de eso se aprovechan quienes viven de nuestro miedo. Sí, el PP y VOX dan miedo, pero el PSOE —y quienes le dan su apoyo— son especialistas en propagar ese miedo para después vendernos su protección.


NOTA:

 Para ilustrar este mecanismo, inicialmente se me había ocurrido utilizar la imagen de los vendedores de alarmas, que primero te meten el miedo en el cuerpo hablando de los robos y después te venden alarmas para defenderte de los ladrones. Pero la imagen no es correcta. En realidad, estamos ante mafiosos que durante el día te venden protección y que, si no la aceptas, por la noche vendrán ellos mismos a quemarte el negocio.


Gobernar a un pueblo asustado es fácil. No hace falta cumplir nada, no hacen falta resultados, no hay que dar explicaciones. No hace falta nada. Solo hay que dar miedo.


Hace ocho años que el PSOE gobierna gracias a los votos de millones de catalanes. ¿Y qué han recibido los catalanes a cambio?


Podría escribir páginas enteras, porque los incumplimientos son tantos y tan sistemáticos que ya hemos perdido la cuenta. De hecho, esto también juega a favor del PSOE y de quienes le dan su apoyo: los incumplimientos son tantos y tan graves que mucha gente ha dejado de verlos.


Ya sé que puede resultar un poco repetitivo, pero tenemos el deber democrático de señalar este escándalo. Podría escribir páginas enteras, pero solo voy a escribir 280 palabras. Se lee en dos minutos:


Mentiras.

 En enero de 2020, Rufián presumía así del pacto con el PSOE: «Calendarizado. Inicio en 15 días. Con garantías. Acuerdo final refrendado por el pueblo de Cataluña». Y todavía añadía: «Esto es lo que haremos».


No cumplieron ni siquiera los quince días. La mesa debía reunirse todos los meses y, cuatro años después, Sánchez todavía anunciaba la cuarta reunión. ¿Y aquel acuerdo final que debíamos votar los catalanes? Nadie ha vuelto a saber nada de él.


Incumplimientos.

 En 2020, ERC entrega dos veces sus votos a Sánchez a cambio de que la Generalitat gestione los fondos europeos. Cuando llega el decreto, Cataluña no tiene ningún papel. ERC vota en contra y el decreto se salva gracias a la abstención de VOX.

author: Publicación Abierta
title: Los derechos no son obligatorios: carta a los trabajadores que votan a la derecha
content:
Hoy quiero dirigirme a una parte concreta de nuestra clase. No a los banqueros, ni a los dueños de las grandes superficies, ni a los fondos buitre, que votan a la derecha sabiendo perfectamente lo que hacen. Me dirijo a esos trabajadores y trabajadoras que, cobrando una nómina y madrugando como el que más, van a votar al PP o a VOX y que, además, se molestan cada vez que se aprueba un nuevo derecho para la clase trabajadora. A ellos quiero darles una noticia que, por lo visto, nadie les ha contado: los derechos no son obligatorios.


Diez días para despedir a tu madre


El Gobierno aprobó este martes, en el último Consejo de Ministros antes de las elecciones, la ampliación del permiso por fallecimiento de un familiar, que pasa de dos a diez días laborables y que ahora se denomina permiso por duelo. Una medida que llevaba más de un año sobre la mesa, que la patronal recibió con la cara larga de siempre y que el PP ya amenaza con derogar, despachándola como «papel mojado».


Y ya oigo a algunos compañeros en el vestuario, junto a la máquina del café o en el grupo de WhatsApp: que si es electoralismo, que si es otra paguita, que si así no hay quien levante este país. Pues tranquilo, compañero. Nadie te va a obligar a coger esos días. Si mañana se muere tu madre y tú prefieres fichar a la hora de siempre, ficha. Ni siquiera tienes por qué ir al entierro. Nadie va a ir a buscarte a casa para obligarte a dedicar diez días al duelo. El derecho está ahí para quien lo necesite y quien no lo quiera, que no lo utilice.


Lo que no puedes hacer es negárselo a la compañera que acaba de perder a su hijo ni al compañero que tiene que cruzar media península para enterrar a su padre y volver con el alma destrozada a reponer lineales. Dos días no dan ni para el tanatorio, el entierro y el papeleo. Cualquiera que haya pasado por ello lo sabe. Y cuando no hay tiempo para el duelo, lo que llega después es una baja por puro agotamiento emocional, que al final pagamos todos.


Un derecho no te quita nada: te da una opción


Esta es la trampa en la que la derecha lleva décadas haciendo caer a una parte de la clase trabajadora: presentar cada derecho como si fuera una imposición. Un derecho no es una obligación. Es una puerta que se abre. Puedes cruzarla o no, pero cerrársela a los demás es una canallada.


Pasa exactamente lo mismo con el derecho al aborto. El derecho al aborto no obliga a ninguna mujer a abortar. Quien tenga unas creencias religiosas que no se lo permitan, que las siga con total libertad: nadie se lo va a impedir ni va a llamar a su puerta para obligarla a hacer lo contrario. Lo que no puede hacer es imponer su fe a las demás. El derecho al aborto solo permite a quien quiera ejercerlo decidir sobre su propio cuerpo y su propia vida, con garantías y en la sanidad pública. No en una clínica clandestina ni cruzando la frontera, como tuvieron que hacer muchas de nuestras madres y abuelas cuando podían permitírselo, mientras las mujeres pobres se jugaban la vida.


Y pasa lo mismo con el divorcio, que tanto combatieron los mismos de siempre: nadie está obligado a divorciarse. Y con el matrimonio entre personas del mismo sexo, que el PP llevó al Tribunal Constitucional: a ningún heterosexual se le ha obligado a casarse con alguien de su mismo sexo. Ninguno de esos derechos le ha quitado nada a nadie. Solo han hecho la vida un poco más digna a quienes los necesitaban.


Lo que de verdad es obligatorio


¿Saben qué sí es obligatorio? Lo que nos imponen sin preguntarnos. Es obligatorio volver a trabajar con una hernia porque la mutua te da el alta antes de tiempo. Es obligatorio aceptar un salario que no llega a fin de mes porque, si no, hay cola en la puerta. Es obligatorio trabajar hasta caer reventado y, si les dejamos, hasta los setenta años, como sueña Aznar. Es obligatorio pagar un alquiler abusivo porque los fondos buitre han convertido la vivienda en un casino. Eso sí son imposiciones. Y, qué casualidad, ahí la derecha nunca habla de libertad.


La libertad, para ellos, es la libertad del patrón para despedir barato, la del fondo buitre para desahuciar y la de la mutua para mandar al enfermo a trabajar. Nunca la libertad del trabajador para enterrar a su madre con dignidad.


Quien vota contra sus derechos vota contra sí mismo


Que nadie se engañe: si mañana gobiernan el PP y VOX, esos diez días corren peligro. Ya lo han advertido. Y no solo esos. Irán a por los permisos, las bajas, las pensiones y el salario mínimo …

author: Freedom Editor
title: “Anarchy in the UK” turns 50
content:
It would be several years before a genuine anarcho-punk movement emerged, with bands such as Crass and Conflict, but the Sex Pistols’ provocation remains memorable

Barely a month after the release of The Damned’s first single, New Rose, on Stiff Records – generally regarded as the first genuine punk single in history – and eight months after the Ramones’ debut single (Blitzkrieg Bop), the Sex Pistols’ Anarchy in the U.K. was released on EMI on 26 November 1976. The A-side featured the title track, while the B-side contained I Wanna Be Me. Originally, No Fun was supposed to appear on the B-side. Unfortunately, the reasons for this change of plan remain unknown.

The release of the record was followed by a disastrous tour, characterised above all by a series of cancelled gigs.

The Sex Pistols, who were essentially a boy band assembled through auditions for Malcolm McLaren and Vivienne Westwood’s SEX boutique, are generally regarded as the “ultimate punk band” – the group that shaped the genre or, at the very least, British punk as it emerged in 1977, even though the importance of bands such as The Clash was certainly no less significant. Their importance, however, extends beyond this musical legacy: it was with the Sex Pistols that the term “anarchy” made its entrance into the punk scene. Their manager, Malcolm McLaren, repeatedly explained in interviews that part of the band’s strategy for success was based on the deliberately provocative use of this term.

Other punk bands would subsequently follow this path, notably The Exploited with I Believe in Anarchy, first released as a single in 1981. The band remains controversial to this day because of antisemitic statements made by its singer Wattie, whom the Dead Kennedys even singled out in their classic Nazi Punks Fuck Off!. It would take several more years before a genuine anarcho-punk movement emerged, with bands such as Crass and Conflict.

In 2012, Johnny Rotten, the Sex Pistols’ singer, publicly declared that he was not an anarchist. This came as no surprise: it had been known for a long time, and his public statements in recent years have repeatedly confirmed it, particularly when he distanced himself, at least indirectly, from the iconic song God Save the Queen by playing down its significance.

As far as its actual content is concerned, Anarchy in the U.K. is not a particularly substantial piece of writing. It relies on clichés, above all that of the violent anarchist. More interesting, and yet rarely pointed out, is the fact that the single was dedicated to two historical figures: Che Guevara and Buenaventura Durruti, the famous Spanish anarchist. This decision was probably Malcolm McLaren’s, and despite all the criticism that can be levelled at him, one has to acknowledge his general knowledge.

author: Joshua Carroll & James Crump
title: Jewish Group Launches Bid to Lift UK’s Terror Ban on Hamas
content:
The Jewish Network for Palestine (JNP) has applied to the UK government to reverse the proscription of Hamas under the Terrorism Act.


The activist group filed the de-proscription application on Thursday under Section 4 of the act. 


JNP, which has about 600 members and supporters, argues the ban had been used by the government to “silence Jews”.


Under the act, expressing support for a proscribed organisation is a criminal offence punishable by up to 14 years in prison. But what constitutes an expression of support has been

 liberally interpreted

 by some police forces, especially since Palestine Action was banned under the same law last year.      


JNP’s chair, David Cannon, said the proscription of Hamas has made it difficult to discuss its 7 October 2023 attacks in Israel. He

told Al Jazeera

 that JNP has avoided talking publicly about

false Israeli narratives

 surrounding the attacks for fear of running afoul of the law. 


“Now, all of these things needed to be discussed, but the UK government’s proscription of the political wing of Hamas has made referring to such evidence risk the accusation of supporting Hamas, which is not what we’re saying. We’re saying that we want to discuss these issues,” Cannon said.


In 2024, JNP co-founder Haim Bresheeth, who is 80 and a British-Israeli anti-Zionist filmmaker, was arrested under the Terrorism Act after he said in a speech in London that Israel “cannot fight the resistance” and “cannot win against Hamas”.


The investigation against Bresheeth, who is the child of Holocaust survivors, was later dropped without charge.


Another JNP member, Tony Greenstein, 72, was charged under the act after he wrote “full support for the Gaza ghetto uprising” on social media in the wake of 7 October. In August this year he was found not guilty of inviting support for Hamas. 


Cannon told

 the National

: “Five years ago we were told this ban was needed to protect Jewish people. Instead, it has been used to raid the home of a Jewish writer whose family died at Treblinka, and to detain an 80-year-old son of Auschwitz survivors for political speech opposing a genocide.


“We do not support Hamas,” he added. “We are asking the Home Secretary to end a law that is being used to silence Jews who speak up for Palestinians.”

author: Unknown
title: Lotta newsletter # 2
content:
// BULLETIN ANARCHISTE // 2 // AOUT 2026 // GRATUIT //


Bienvenue dans ce deuxième numéro du bulletin d'information LOTTA. Le numéro précédent a été très bien accueilli. Grâce à la collaboration de groupes issus de différentes régions du monde, la revue a été publiée non seulement en anglais, mais aussi en tchèque, hongrois, italien, français et espagnol. Ce vif intérêt a également permis à ce deuxième numéro de compter davantage de pages et, par conséquent, de contenir plus d'informations.


Dans ce numéro, nous mettons une nouvelle fois l'accent sur le soutien aux déserteurs, aux personnes qui échappent à la mobilisation ou qui sabotent la machine de guerre. Dans nos entretiens, nous donnons la parole à ceux qui ont fui la guerre, ainsi qu'à ceux qui apportent un soutien concret aux réfugiés. Un sujet connexe concerne la détérioration des conditions de vie des réfugiés ukrainiens et russes qui se sont enfuis vers les pays de l'UE pour échapper à la guerre et à la mobilisation. Cependant, nous ne nous concentrons pas uniquement sur les sujets liés à la guerre en Ukraine. Nous offrons également une tribune aux camarades d'Iran et à ceux qui s'engagent dans la résistance contre le sionisme et les massacres qui ont lieu à Gaza.


Si nous nous attachons à rendre compte d'actes spécifiques de résistance anti-guerre tels que la désertion, les émeutes et autres actions directes, nous ne souhaitons pas pour autant négliger l'analyse et la théorie. Car ce n'est qu'en ayant une bonne compréhension de la réalité, du contexte plus large et des processus à l'œuvre que nos actions concrètes peuvent être efficaces. Les analyses de ce numéro portent principalement sur la critique des illusions pacifistes et la critique du militarisme, masqué par la rhétorique anti-guerre. Nous analysons également le contexte géopolitique et l'escalade des tensions inter-impérialistes qui rapprochent le monde d'une Troisième Guerre mondiale.


Dans les guerres, les armées d'État cherchent à forcer l'autre camp à capituler ou à lui imposer les termes d'une paix formelle, ce qui implique toutefois toujours des préparatifs en vue du prochain cycle guerrier. Notre perspective ne se concentre donc pas seulement sur le sabotage de l'effort de guerre en temps de guerre, mais aussi sur le sabotage de la paix capitaliste, qui revient toujours à faire la guerre par d'autres moyens. En bref, le but de notre lutte est de transformer les guerres entre États — et leur « paix » — en une lutte de classe contre les États. Nous ne voulons pas d'un retour au statu quo d'avant-guerre, mais la destruction révolutionnaire de tous les États.

Zahlreiche Frauenrechtsorganisationen hatten zu der Demonstration im Bezirk Beyoglu auf der europäischen Seite der Stadt am Abend aufgerufen. Daraufhin hatte die Bezirksverwaltung ein 24-stündiges Verbot aller Versammlungen und Demonstrationen, Pressekonferenzen sowie das Verteilen von Flugblättern und Sitzstreiks erlassen. Trotz des Verbots sind zahlreiche Menschen in Istanbul auf die Straße gegangen, berichtet ARD-Korrespondentin Bettina Dunkel. Die Polizei sei mit einem Großaufgebot im Einsatz. Es gebe „keine große Demonstration“ mit Tausenden Menschen, sondern viele kleinere Protestgruppen. 11

 de novembre: jornada de vaga per l’emergència social


67 

detencions durant la jornada


3 

persones empresonades


El passat dia 11 de novembre es va convocar una vaga per tal de denunciar la situació d’emergència social que viu el país i que s’ha tornat insostenible. L’accés a un habitatge digne i el cost de la vida s’han convertit en una cursa d’obstacles que expulsa el veïnat dels seus barris i pobles i condemna milers de famílies a la precarietat.


Les persones i col·lectius sotasignants volem fer públic, a través d’aquest manifest, la defensa del dret fonamental a la vaga com una eina irrenunciable de justícia social, dignitat laboral i democràcia real, i exigim el respecte absolut i la garantia del seu exercici lliure i efectiu, sense coaccions, amenaces ni represàlies.


Malauradament aquesta exigència torna a ser necessària a dia d’avui perquè durant la jornada de vaga hi va haver 67 detencions i tres persones estan empresonades als Països Catalans, donat que el vaguista empresonat de Castelló ja ha estat posat en llibertat.


En lloc d’oferir solucions reals a l’emergència social, les institucions i els poders econòmics responen amb multes, identificacions arbitràries, càrregues policials, processos judicials i campanyes d’estigmatització contra les persones que es manifesten.


Per tot això:


Exigim la llibertat immediata i sense càrrecs de totes les persones preses per participar en la vaga del dia 11 de novembre.


Expressem tot el suport a les famílies i l’entorn de les persones preses.


Reclamem l’anul·lació de les multes i l’arxivament dels processos judicials oberts contra activistes pel fet d’exercir el dret de protesta i de vaga.


Denunciem la persecució policial, judicial i mediàtica contra les persones que exerceixen el dret de vaga per exigir un sostre i unes condicions de vida dignes.


Reclamem el respecte efectiu del dret de vaga i de protesta i, sobretot, exigim solucions urgents a la crisi de l’habitatge i del cost de la vida.

title: Vivir la fuerza. Simone Weil y la Columna Durruti
content:
Año publicación: 

2025

Autor / es: 

Xavier Artigas, traducción de Lorena Franco. - Prólogo de Myrtille Gimenóloga

https://www.pepitas.net/libro/vivir-la-fuerza

Una excelente publicación, que no sólo recupera el diario de Simone Weil durante la revolución en España, sino que le da contexto destruyendo mitos sobre su presunto rechazo a la revolución, o sobre su presuntamente justificado rechazo a la revolución, aunque quizás al precio de dar peso a otro mito no menos consolador de almas bellas: el de una CNT que traicionó a la revolución por burocrática. Esperamos volver a ello en alasbarricadas.org (Super8).


 


«A medida que avanza, nuestro historiador aficionado contribuye a esbozar, paso a paso, una forma de relacionarse, de reflexionar y de actuar propias de la crítica social de los años treinta, cuando abundaba un intenso deseo de emancipación del capitalismo»

. —Del prólogo de Myrtille Gonzalbo


«Imagino varias lecturas (y lectores) posibles de este libro. Los amantes de la historia de la Guerra Civil pueden disfrutar de la reconstrucción rigurosa del encuentro, a la vez brevísimo e imperecedero, cargado de consecuencias, entre Simone Weil y la Columna Durruti. Los amantes de la filósofa francesa pueden saborear —por primera vez en muchos casos— los detalles de su viaje a España, los antecedentes que lo hicieron posible, los personajes con los que se cruzó, los paisajes que atravesó, las escenas que vivió y la idea que se hizo de ellas. En mi caso, deleitándome también con estas dos primeras lecturas, con el inmenso trabajo histórico-detectivesco de Xavier Artigas, me he dejado guiar por una tercera: la pregunta por el valor político del viaje de Simone Weil. ¿Qué busca Simone Weil en España?»

. —Del epílogo de Amador Fernández-Savater


Este libro aborda la figura de la filósofa francesa Simone Weil en su dimensión política, desmantelando el mito que ha dominado la proyección de su pensamiento durante décadas, y que describe a Weil como una pensadora trascendente y apolítica. Una rigurosa investigación histórica reconstruye la breve pero intensa participación de Weil en la Guerra Civil española y ofrece una nueva perspectiva que reivindica el compromiso revolucionario de la filósofa.


	 


Vivir la fuerza

 reconstruye con precisión la evolución política de Weil y documenta su recorrido desde el sindicalismo revolucionario francés hacia posiciones libertarias, lo que permite explicar de manera coherente su participación en la Guerra Civil. Esta experiencia fue decisiva para el desarrollo de su concepto de «la fuerza», que articularía posteriormente en uno de los textos más importantes de su trayectoria filosófica:

La Ilíada o el poema de la fuerza

.


Vivir la fuerza

 no solo recupera la figura de Weil como pensadora política comprometida, sino que también aporta una mirada nueva sobre un momento histórico clave y contribuye a reimaginar las posibilidades de emancipación social.

author: Dalia Abu Ramadan
title: In Gaza, We Have No Feasts to Give Thanks For
content:
As Americans feast on Thanksgiving, we are still facing widespread malnutrition and acute hunger in Gaza.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

I grew up believing that food was readily available, that having access to it was something ordinary and something I could always count on. I never imagined that one day I would be deprived of it, or that I would find myself wishing for a single loaf of bread despite having the money to buy one. Yet I, my family, and my people were deprived of food for prolonged periods throughout Israel’s war on Gaza. Although the war has publicly been declared over, we continue to suffer its consequences — only now they unfold away from the headlines, behind the scenes.

I had always heard that we were a people living under siege, but I never imagined that human cruelty could reach such depths. I thought the worst cruelty could bring was the use of weapons. It never crossed my mind that hunger itself could be turned into a weapon against us; that food, one of the most basic necessities of life, could become a means of deprivation and suffering. How can human beings strip others of their right to food with so little regard for their humanity?

No human being has the right to decide that another human being or an animal should be starved! How can we advance technologically while regressing as human beings?

Although famine conditions in Gaza have eased since the ceasefire, the consequences of the war have not. Many of these consequences remain hidden from the world. As of October 15, around 90 percent of Gaza’s population still relied on humanitarian food assistance amid the collapse of livelihoods and widespread loss of purchasing power, leaving families struggling to secure even their most basic needs. For many, food aid is no longer supplementary support; it has become a lifeline. Yet that very lifeline is now under threat, at a time when most people in Gaza remain unable to meet their own food needs.

On October 19, the World Food Programme (WFP) announced that funding shortages had forced it to cut its food assistance in Gaza by around one-third, meaning that approximately 500,000 people would lose access to essential assistance. These cuts were not the result of declining humanitarian needs, but of a shortfall in international funding.

Since the ceasefire was announced in October 2025, the WFP had been providing assistance to approximately 1.6 million people in Gaza every month through food parcels, wheat flour, bread, hot meals, nutritional support, school snacks, and cash assistance. By October 2026, however, the food program had reduced the number of people it supported to 1.1 million.

The World Food Programme announced that 500,000 people would lose access to essential assistance.

The WFP’s acting executive director, Carl Skau, told Australia’s ABC News that traditional donors, including the United States and European countries, had reduced their contributions. He also pointed to multiple humanitarian crises competing for limited funding and what he described as “donor fatigue.” Skau stressed that the cuts were not due to an inability to bring food into Gaza or a decline in people’s needs, but rather to a lack of funding.

A single disruption, seemingly small in itself, can push an entire population closer to famine.

On October 20, 2026, flour became scarce across Gaza after the WFP could no longer fund the bakeries that had been supplying bread to the population. That day, my uncle went to the market to see what he could find to feed his family. He was stunned to discover that flour was nowhere to be found. Wherever it was available, it was being sold at exorbitant prices because of the shortage.

He called my father and said, “Can you imagine, Imad? There’s no flour, no chicken, no eggs, nothing. They told me flour has become incredibly expensive, and most of the other goods are spoiled.”

“There is nothing we can do. We are in the same position as everyone else,” my father replied. “We don’t know how much longer we will have to keep thinking about stockpiling flour and food in case of a sudden famine that could last for days. We simply don’t know what might happen, and we can no longer count on food remaining available.”

That was the hardest day we had faced in terms of food since the so-called ceasefire was declared. We felt a level of despair we had never …

author: Ben Smoke
title: The Government Claims It Consulted Green Groups on Data Centres. The Evidence Says Otherwise
content:
As the government steams ahead with plans for more data centres, who is it talking to? And who is getting shut out of the discussion? It has repeatedly claimed they have engaged with environmental organisations on AI data centre policy, but no evidence exists to back up this claim.


In July 2026, Novara Media asked the now defunct Department of Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT) whether they had engaged with environmental organisations in the creation of their AI Growth Zone policy.


The department did not give an “on the record” comment, but responded “on background”, claiming to have engaged with environmental organisations through a range of channels, including correspondence and conferences.


Information given on background is reportable but not attributable. It’s used as a way of giving journalists information without publicly tying oneself to it. It is supposed to be an agreement between a source and a reporter, but big tech companies have been accused of increasingly using it as a way of

obfuscating the truth

.


A claim like the one made by DSIT is a big one – it’s the difference between a data centre policy shaped by a whole host of voices (sceptics, supporters, experts and more) and not. It was a claim given without evidence or corroboration, so we asked for some.


We were told that if we wanted a “formal” list of environmental organisations engaged with, we would have to submit a Freedom of Information request. So this is exactly what we did. Two in fact. One request asked for any information on environmental organisations DSIT had engaged with on data centre policy as a whole. Another, narrower request asked specifically about environmental organisations DSIT engaged with as policy was being written between July 2024 and January 2025. On both occasions, the FOI requests were denied on the basis that even assessing whether the department held information on this would take more than the legally capped 24 hours of work to find.


Every government department releases transparency returns each quarter, showing who ministers and senior civil servants met. As we waited for the FOIs to come back (organisations have 20 working days to respond), we manually checked the DSIT transparency returns and found no environmental organisations appeared in this time frame in relation to AI Growth Zone policy.


We reached out to 20 of the biggest and most respected environmental organisations in the country to ask whether they had engaged with the government on AI data centre policy in this period. Of the nine that responded, including Greenpeace, Friends of the Earth, the RSPB, the Rivers Trust, none had been consulted.


While we waited for answers, a

new report

 from Spotlight on Corruption revealed that local authorities and communities were shut out of creating policy around data centres whilst special interests and big tech were prioritised. The report found zero evidence of engagement with environmental organisations in the six months between Labour taking office in 2024 and the announcement of their AI data centre policy in January 2025.


To conduct this research, Spotlight on Corruption searched through transparency returns for 11 government departments. The report also found that 84% of ministerial stakeholder meetings on data centres were with businesses or private sector trade associations. The report documented the revolving door between the government and many of those businesses, revealing 38 ministers and senior civil servants had been hired by AI companies.


It also revealed that no environmental organisations were invited to join the AI Energy Council which was established in April 2025 and tasked with assessing “how the government’s AI ambitions could be powered through clean energy sources”. Microsoft, Google and Amazon Web Services all had representation on the council. The council’s “sustainability working group”, which met only once between April 2025 and July 2026, also did not include any representatives from environmental or sustainability NGOs. Those

invited to attend

 included Google, Amazon Web Services, Microsoft, asset management company Brookfield, data centre company Equinix and a number of energy companies and universities.


During last month’s budget a new “data centre covenant” was announced, aiming to protect the environment and communities as data centres expand, amid concerns around their environmental impact – from

water

and

energy

title: NRW-Polizeigesetz weitet Befugnisse der Polizei und des Verfassungsschutzes gewaltig aus
content:
Dossier


„…

Elektronische Fußfesseln, zusätzliche Videobeobachtung in den Städten, Ausweitung vorsorglicher Gefängnisaufenthalte – die schwarz-gelbe NRW-Regierung will künftig härter gegen Terror und Alltagskriminalität vorgehen. (…) Geprägt ist das erste „Sicherheitspaket“ der Landesregierung von Anti-Terror-Vorschriften; sie sollen Fahndern die Arbeit erleichtern. Die Befugnisse der Polizei werden beim Zugriff auf verschlüsselte E-Mails und bei der Überwachung von Messengerdiensten großzügig gelockert. (…) Die geplante Neufassung des Polizeigesetzes soll den Sicherheitsbehörden außerdem die Möglichkeit schaffen, sogenannte Gefährder länger vorsorglich einzusperren. So wird der Unterbindungsgewahrsam von derzeit 48 Stunden auf bis zu einen Monat ausgedehnt

…“

Artikel von Florian Pfitzner vom 18.02.2018 bei der NOZ online


, siehe dazu

die Bündnisse dagegen

 und hier dazu:


Wenn jede Kamera zum Auge des Verfassungsschutzes wird: Verfassungsbeschwerde von Digitalcourage gegen das neue Verfassungsschutzgesetz NRW


„Seit April 2026 hat der nordrhein-westfälische Verfassungsschutz neue Überwachungsbefugnisse. Besonders weitreichend ist der Zugriff auf öffentliche und private Überwachungskameras. Zusammen mit automatisierter Datensammlung und künstlicher Intelligenz entsteht ein Überwachungspotenzial, das wir für unvereinbar mit unseren Grundrechten halten. Deshalb bereiten wir eine Verfassungsbeschwerde gegen das neue Verfassungsschutzgesetz NRW vor. (…)


Das neue Verfassungsschutzgesetz in NRW räumt dem Inlandsgeheimdienst weitgehende Überwachungsbefugnisse ein. Die einzelnen Maßnahmen sind bereits jede für sich genommen weitreichend. In ihrem Zusammenspiel ermöglichen sie eine potenziell nahezu lückenlose Überwachung des analogen öffentlichen Raums. Hinzu kommt die Möglichkeit, den digitalen öffentlichen Raum automatisiert nach personenbezogenen Informationen zu durchsuchen und gewonnene Erkenntnisse mit künstlicher Intelligenz auszuwerten.


Der Verfassungsschutz erhält damit Überwachungsmöglichkeiten, deren Ausmaß wir bisher vor allem mit autoritären Staaten verbunden haben.


Ein Überwachungsnetz, das längst existiert


Besonders problematisch ist § 20 des neuen Verfassungsschutzgesetzes. Die Regelung erlaubt es dem Geheimdienst, vorhandene private und öffentliche Überwachungskameras im öffentlich zugänglichen Raum mitzunutzen. Er darf sich in Echtzeit auf Kameras aufschalten und Betreiber.innen dazu verpflichten, Bild- und Tonaufzeichnungen live auszuleiten oder vorhandene Aufnahmen herauszugeben. Das kann sogar Aufzeichnungen betreffen, die bis zu einem Jahr vor der Anordnung entstanden sind.


Damit wird aus den dezentral betriebenen Kamerasystemen von Verkehrsberieben, Geschäften, öffentlichen Einrichtungen und weiteren Stellen ein zentralisiertes Netz potenzieller nachrichtendiesntlicher Videoüberwachung geschaffen, das grade in Städten flächendeckende Ausmaße annehmen kann. Und die Betreiber.innen können verpflichtet werden, dabei mitzuwirken. Hiervon sind zwangläufig viele Menschen betroffen. Das ist in besonderem Maße problematisch, weil das Gesetz keinen hinreichenden Schutz für besonders sensible und grundrechtlich geschützte Lebensbereiche vorsieht: Demonstrationen sowie berufliche Kontakte von Journalist.innen, Rechtsanwält.innen oder Seelsorger.innen können grundsätzlich erfasst werden. (…)


Dass die Überwachung möglicherweise nie stattfindet, macht die Sache nicht harmlos. Denn niemand kann wissen, ob der Verfassungsschutz gerade auf eine Kamera zugreift oder später die Aufnahmen anfordert. In NRW gibt es seit April de facto keinen geschützen öffentlichen Raum mehr. Das kann ausreichen, damit Menschen ihr Verhalten ändern. Vielleicht geht die junge Frau beim nächsten Mal lieber nicht mehr auf eine Demonstration. Vielleicht verzichtet sie darauf, mit bestimmten Menschen gesehen zu werden. Vielleicht bleibt sie ganz zu Hause. (…)


Die neuen Befugnisse zur Videoüberwachung sind nur ein Teil des Problems. Das Gesetz erlaubt dem Verfassungsschutz große Mengen personenbezogener Daten automatisiert zu sammeln und auszuwerten. (…)


Insgesamt ist dieses Gesetz ein Skandal: Es gibt einem weitgehend im Verborgenen arbeitenden Geheimdienst Überwachungsbefugnisse an die Hand, die eine nahezu lückenlose Beobachtung des öffentlichen Raums ermöglichen und damit grundlegende Freiheitsrechte gefährden, und in Richtung Überwachungstaat weisen.


Wir wollen das nicht hinnehmen

title: KDP forces detain journalist and two civilians in Soran
content:
In a statement, a relative of journalist Ebdo Rostayî reported that KDP security forces had detained Rostayî and two other civilians. The detentions were reportedly carried out because the civilians had been asked to share their views on the situation in the region and the decisions made by Elî Zeydî.


In a statement, VAR Media Institution reported that its Soran correspondent, Ebdo Rostayî, had been abducted by security forces while carrying out his journalistic duties.


The statement said: “The Soran Autonomous Administration Security Forces are responsible for the safety and well-being of our colleague Ebdo Rostayî.”

title: MP Cengiz Çiçek: Targeting ill prisoners is an ideological attack
content:
The vigil launched outside the Ministry of Justice to demand the medical treatment and release of ill prisoners entered its 10th day. The vigil is led by the MED Federation of Legal Solidarity Associations of Prisoners’ Families (MED TUHAD-FED), with the support of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) and the Free Lawyers Association (ÖHD).


DEM Party MP for Istanbul Cengiz Çiçek addressed the vigil on Wednesday, saying that the action was not only a political but also a moral responsibility. Çiçek said that the action represented an insistence on upholding all human values and that human values, law, justice and peace were necessary for everyone.


Çiçek said that a former minister had been released on health grounds after 18 days, while thousands of political prisoners had been held in prison for decades, describing this as a political choice by the government.


Çiçek emphasized that the Peace and Democratic Society Process was not merely about ending armed conflict but also encompassed the struggle against systemic and structural inequalities.


Çiçek said that the Kurdish question could not be reduced to weapons and must be addressed as a question of democracy and law. He added that the issue of ill prisoners was not limited to the individuals whose names had been made public.


Çiçek said: "The reality of ill prisoners is not limited to the people whose names have been mentioned. Through these people, an attack is being carried out against the ideas and philosophy that oppose this system, raise the cry of rebellion and voice dissent. This is an ideological attack. It is a political attack."


Çiçek said that the authorities are using treatment to force ill prisoners to abandon their struggle, adding, "No. We will not surrender."


'We did not call for peace in the grave'


Çiçek said that the struggle for justice for ill prisoners was also a struggle for peace and democracy, emphasizing that the demand for peace voiced by Kurds and democratic circles did not mean accepting a dishonorable peace.


Çiçek added: "We Kurds, democrats and revolutionaries did not mean that we were begging for peace when we called for it. We did not call for peace in the grave. We have never regarded a peace in which we receive the lifeless bodies of our people from prisons as genuine peace. Nor did we call for a dishonorable peace."


Çiçek underlined that they were active participants in the struggle for democracy while assuming responsibility for ensuring a permanent end to armed conflict within the framework of the Peace and Democratic Society Process. He added that they maintained this position under the leadership of the mothers wearing white headscarves.


'Let us strengthen the struggle together'


Çiçek addressed all sections of society dissatisfied with the government's policies and current practices, saying that the vigil should not be regarded solely as the struggle of families whose relatives were in prison.


Çiçek said that the action was a call to collectively strengthen the struggle for a democratic republic and democracy. He urged all opposition groups to support the vigil and strengthen the struggle.


The vigil outside the Ministry of Justice continue today at 2 p.m.

title: KNK calls on Southern Kurdistan’s political parties to protect national gains
content:
The Executive Council of the Kurdistan National Congress (KNK) issued a statement concerning the protection of the constitutional rights and powers of the Kurdistan Region.


The KNK said it had been closely following the Iraqi Prime Minister’s recent remarks, and drew attention to statements and initiatives aimed at restricting the management of oil, natural resources and other revenues.


Emphasising the need for political and economic stability in both federal Iraq and the Kurdistan Region, the statement said that Iraq’s strength and the continuation of its democratic system depend on respecting the will of the people and protecting everyone's constitutional rights.


Pointing out that the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) is the result of the Kurdish people's struggle and the sacrifices made by the people of Kurdistan, the statement said: "Any attempt to undermine the constitutional rights of the Kurdistan Region regarding oil and non-oil revenues contradicts the principles of federalism and cooperation and will weaken the understanding and trust between Erbil and Baghdad.


We also emphasise that the Kurdistan Region's share of the Iraqi budget, as well as the salaries and financial entitlements of employees and citizens in Kurdistan, must not be entangled in political disputes. These must be guaranteed as fundamental constitutional rights."


The statement also said that, in order to strengthen stability in Iraq, Article 140 of the 2005 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Iraq must be fully implemented. This is necessary to normalise the situation in the Kurdish territories outside the Kurdistan Region and to put an end to policies of demographic change and marginalisation.


The KNK called on the President of Iraq, the Speaker of Parliament, the Prime Minister and the Iraqi Federal Government to address the rights of the Kurdistan Region within the constitutional framework and with a sense of responsibility. It added that a proper solution could be achieved through constructive national dialogue.


The statement concluded with the following appeal: "We call on all political forces and parties in Kurdistan, particularly the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), as well as all citizens, to resolve their internal conflicts and disagreements and to act in unity, with a common national position and the highest sense of responsibility, in order to protect our constitutional gains and the status of the Kurdistan Region."

title: Gülderen Varlı: Women's freedom is a fundamental condition for peace
content:
Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) MP for Van (Wan) Gülderen Varlı spoke to ANF on International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. She talked about the Peace and Democratic Society Process, women's freedom, violence against women, ecological problems and women's role in decision-making mechanisms, saying that a democratic society could only be built if women had an equal and free say in every sphere of life.


Gülderen Varlı emphasized that the Peace and Democratic Society Process, initiated by Abdullah Öcalan's call, must be addressed in conjunction with women's freedom, saying that women had established an important tradition of struggle within the Kurdish freedom struggle.


 


'The women's struggle is rooted in a historical legacy'


Varlı said that the women's struggle was rooted in a historical legacy: "Our struggle is a women's struggle. Within the Kurdish freedom struggle, we come from a 50-year tradition of struggle. The women's struggle extends from the Mirabal sisters to the present day and has grown through the struggle waged by women like Sakine and many other women comrades."


Varlı added that 25 November was not only a day of struggle against violence against women but also an occasion to discuss how a democratic society should be built. She drew attention to women's role in establishing a shared, equal and free life, saying that "women are struggling to ensure that both they and those around them can live freely. Women will also play their part in creating a democratic and free country."


'Women's right to speak and decide is the foundation of democratic society'


Varlı said that systematic violence against women was the result of a system shaped by the male-dominated mentality and the state. She said that women's participation in social life and decision-making mechanisms was decisive for democratization and continued: "Women have been subjected to systematic violence for centuries. This violence is the result of a system shaped by the male-dominated mentality and the state. Women's participation in social life, their ability to have a say, take part in governance and express their consciousness and ideas will ensure that the process develops in a democratic direction."


Varlı emphasized that women must not merely voice their demands but also act as subjects directly involved in decision-making and governance processes. She said, "If we all live together in this world and in this country, we must have a collective voice. We, as women, must also be represented in decision-making mechanisms, governance and every sphere of life." She added that women would play a leading role in building social peace during the democratic society process and that the demand for peace voiced by the Peace Mothers and women in every sphere of life for years was an important part of this struggle. She continued: "Despite all the exploitation, torture and violence we have experienced, our demand is peace. Once peace is achieved, it will once again be women who build the social fabric of peace between the two sides. Women will also actively participate in this process."


'Peace is possible through a life where women are not killed'


Varlı said that the Peace and Democratic Society Process could not be assessed solely in terms of silencing the weapons and ending deaths, drawing attention to the continuing femicides and violence against women. She said that discussions on peace must be accompanied by concrete steps to guarantee women's right to life and that genuine peace could not exist in an environment where women disappear and are killed: "We have been discussing the democratic society and peace process for two years. Many politicians and people from different sections of society are expressing their views on this issue. However, as we discuss peace today, we must also bring the violence experienced by women onto the agenda on the occasion of 25 November. Women are being killed today. Women are falling from the balconies of their homes, disappearing or being murdered. First, there are reports of missing women, and then it emerges that these women have been killed."


Varlı underlined that mothers had endured immense suffering for years because of the children they had lost in the conflict and that peace was therefore extremely valuable. title: KCK on the 48th anniversary of the PKK’s founding: A new beginning in the freedom struggle
content:
The Co-Presidency of the Executive Council of the Kurdistan Communities Union (KCK) issued a statement on the occasion of the 48th anniversary of the founding of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK). In the statement, the KCK reviewed the historical achievements of the movement led by the PKK and placed the party’s dissolution and the transition to a new political strategy of struggle within the continuity of the Kurdish freedom struggle.


The KCK statement on Thursday reads as follows:


“We congratulate Leader Apo [Abdullah Öcalan], our people, their friends, and all forces engaged in the struggle on the 48th anniversary of the founding of the PKK. We commemorate with gratitude and respect our martyrs, who made the emergence of the PKK and its 52-year struggle possible.


Leader Apo initiated the efforts to establish the party in memory of our esteemed martyr Haki Karer. On November 27, 1978, he convened the first congress and founded the PKK, which would go on to lead the struggle of the Kurdish people.


The PKK has led the longest-running freedom struggle in the history of the Kurdish people. Under its leadership, profound transformations have taken place among the Kurdish people, the likes of which have not been seen anywhere else in the world. The Kurdish people were raised from their deathbed and became the most dynamic force for freedom in the Middle East. The Kurds, once regarded as backward, have now become a shining example not only for the Middle East but for the entire world.


Our homeland, once regarded as a buried, imaginary Kurdistan, is now a region where an exceptionally vibrant freedom struggle is being waged. All the achievements and the strength of resistance in Northern, Southern, Eastern, and Western Kurdistan are owed to the freedom struggle led by the PKK.


The Kurdish people’s freedom struggle has faced attacks on a scale unprecedented anywhere in the world. We have lost tens of thousands of martyrs, while hundreds of thousands of Kurds have been subjected to severe torture and thrown into prison. The Kurds have set a record in world history for political imprisonment. Thousands of villages were burned down and destroyed, and Kurdistan was depopulated. Nevertheless, the freedom struggle led by the PKK continued uninterrupted for 52 years and achieved tremendous gains.


As the freedom struggle repelled all attacks aimed at its annihilation, the Turkish state found itself facing serious problems both domestically and internationally. Under conditions of non-conflict, it entered into a process of political discussions with our freedom movement. State representatives held dozens of talks with Leader Apo on Imrali. Delegations from the Kurdish side also participated in these talks.


The fact that the Turkish state, which has long denied the existence of the Kurdish people and sought to subject them to physical and cultural genocide, recognizes Leader Apo and our movement as interlocutors is a significant political development. All the talks on Imrali are also being conducted as a form of political struggle.


The Peace and Democratic Society Process, which has been underway for two years, and the new strategy of political struggle have also developed on the foundations of the 52-year struggle. The values created over these 52 years and the reality of our people struggling for their freedom are our greatest source of strength. Today, the Kurds are neither without advocates nor without leadership or strength of their own. We now have a leader who guides not only the Kurdish people but also the pursuit of a free and democratic life in the Middle East and throughout the world. We have a leader who is supported by women because he has developed a path toward women’s liberation. We have a leader who has developed a new social science. Today, we have a leader who enables the Kurdish people to raise their heads as high as the stars.


As Leader Apo said, the PKK is an unfinished novel, a folk song, a poem. The dissolution of the PKK marks a new beginning in the freedom struggle. Just as the Kurdish people entered the struggle alongside the PKK with youthful spirit and enthusiasm and achieved great gains, they will also achieve great gains through the Peace and Democratic Society Process. By attaining a free and democratic life, the Kurds will also pave the way for all peoples of the Middle East to achieve a free and democratic life. title: HPG: Our determination to carry our people’s struggle to victory is stronger than ever
content:
The HPG (People’s Defense Forces) Press Liaison Center released a statement marking the 48th anniversary of the founding of the PKK (Kurdistan Workers’ Party)


The HPG statement on Thursday includes the following:


“Happy National Resistance Day and the 48th anniversary of the founding of the PKK to Leader Apo [Abdullah Öcalan], the leader, founder, first self-sacrificing militant, and greatest contributor to our Freedom Movement; to the families of our martyrs, our patriotic people, the valued friends of our people, the prison resistance fighters, and all our comrades struggling in every sphere!


The PKK is a Party of Martyrs that emerged on the basis of keeping alive the memory of Comrade Haki Karer and fulfilling his goals, and has pursued this cause without interruption for half a century.


The Army of Martyrs, which pioneered the PKK, has, throughout 48 years of struggle, created great values, honorable principles, profound human virtues, high moral and spiritual values, the Apoist spirit of self-sacrifice, and a life so meaningful that it is worth dying for. These sacred values of ours have taken concrete form in the path of the martyrs as our most fundamental source of strength. We commemorate with respect, love, and gratitude all our revered martyrs who created this reality through their sweat, lives, and blood, represented by our great Party Martyr, Comrade Haki Karer.


Forty-eight years ago, the Kurdish people were on the brink of extinction. They faced a reality marked by policies of denial, annihilation, and genocide, in which their very existence had become a matter of debate and even imagining independence and freedom was out of the question. Rescuing the Kurdish people from this situation, shaking off the dust of death that had settled over them, raising them to their feet, breathing life into them, giving them the will to act, enabling them to struggle, proving their existence, and leading them toward freedom required an extremely arduous resistance.


At the same time, there was a need for courageous cadres with an iron will and a spirit of self-sacrifice who could lead this historic resistance, shoulder the burden of the oppressed Kurdish people who had been left without support and of the Kurdistan Freedom Struggle, assume this responsibility, and carry the struggle forward.


Recognizing this historical reality, Leader Apo made a historic breakthrough alongside the Apoists he had organized around him. On November 27, 1978, in the village of Fis in the Lice district of Amed, he made the decision for the Kurdish people’s National Resistance and founded the PKK, which would lead our national resistance.


Every year, every month, every day, and even every hour of this half-century-long epic National Resistance Struggle has been etched into history through magnificent acts of resistance and heroism. Apoists who joined this struggle from all parts of Kurdistan, from abroad, and from other peoples demonstrated unprecedented resistance and heroism, creating an entirely new history and a new reality for the people. Leader Apo’s emergence marked a turning point in Kurdistan. The PKK’s struggle said “stop” to the policies of denial, annihilation, and genocide. Through its relentless resistance, it proved the existence of the Kurdish nation and compelled everyone to acknowledge it.


It brought about a profound revolution in understanding, conscience, and mentality in Kurdistan. It created an entirely new language, culture, discourse, style, and pace. It established the ethics and principles of a free life. Through the intellectual and social revolution it fostered among the Kurdish people, the National Resistance Struggle led by the PKK completely changed and transformed society. By carrying out a revolution within the revolution, it brought forth the reality of free women. This reality took shape as a guerrilla force, developed into an army and a party, and became a guiding philosophy, a set of principles, and a science.


Throughout our 48-year National Resistance Struggle, we have lost nearly 50,000 martyrs, including the PKK’s founding leadership cadres, pioneers, guerrillas, fighters, militia members, friends, and civilians. Each of our martyrs demonstrated extraordinary courage and became a monument of honor in whom we take eternal pride, our most sacred value, and an immortal pioneer who continues to guide us. title: Nine intact skulls and hundreds of bone fragments recovered from cave in Silvan
content:
Following the discovery of numerous human remains in a cave in the Silvan district of Amed (Diyarbakır) province, initial findings have emerged from the crime scene investigation ordered by the prosecutor’s office. Nine intact skulls, 36 skull fragments, and hundreds of other bone fragments were recovered from the cave. The identities of the deceased, as well as the dates and circumstances of their deaths, remain unknown.


The Human Rights Association (IHD), the Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD), and the Amed Bar Association provided information on the progress of the investigation at a joint press conference held at the IHD offices. Given the history of state violence and enforced disappearances in the region, the organizations consider the discovery particularly significant for efforts to address the past.


Prosecutor’s office notified following tip-off from local residents


Zeynep Karayılan, Co-Chair of the ÖHD in Amed, reported that a delegation from the three organizations had conducted an initial on-site investigation on November 19 following a tip-off from local residents received by the IHD. During the investigation, numerous human bones and skulls were discovered and documented on different levels of the three-story cave.


On November 23, the organizations contacted the prosecutor’s office in Silvan and requested the launch of a comprehensive investigation. That same evening, the Turkish gendarmerie informed the organizations that a crime scene investigation had been scheduled for the following day. An eleven-member delegation from the IHD, ÖHD, and the Amed and Mardin bar associations subsequently went to the Bayrampaşa Gendarmerie Station on November 24. However, only one representative from each organization was permitted to participate in the investigation.


Recovery operation under difficult conditions


The cave is located in a rural area known locally as Qesra Fila, according to the bar association. The area is accessible by off-road vehicles and is also frequented by people engaged in livestock farming in the surrounding area. After the site was secured and searched for possible explosive devices, ventilation measures were initiated.


The entrance to the cave is extremely narrow, and its three levels extend deep underground. Due to these conditions, representatives of the legal organizations were unable to enter the cave themselves and observed the operation from outside. Under the supervision of two prosecutors, four forensic crime scene investigators and two members of the Disaster and Emergency Management Authority (AFAD) descended into the cave. The low oxygen levels, particularly on the third level, made the recovery operation difficult.


Nine skulls, hundreds of bone fragments, and a blue button


Human remains were found on all three levels of the cave. In addition to nine intact skulls, 36 skull fragments, and hundreds of other bone fragments, a blue button was also recovered. Soil samples were also collected from all three levels. The recovery operation was documented through photographs and video recordings.


The work at the site ended at approximately 5:15 p.m. The recovered items, secured in a total of seven bags, were then taken to the central gendarmerie station in Silvan. There, the human remains were counted, sorted, and documented in the presence of prosecutors and representatives of the legal organizations.


Müslüm Dalar, a board member of the Amed Bar Association, announced at the press conference that the human remains have since been transferred to the state-run Forensic Medicine Institute (ATK) in Istanbul. The forensic examinations conducted there are expected to shed light on the age of the bones, the identities of the deceased, and the circumstances of their deaths.


The history of enforced disappearances in Silvan


For the human rights and lawyers’ organizations, it is crucial that the investigation not be limited to the forensic identification of the deceased.


Karayılan stated: “At present, it is, of course, not yet known to whom the bones belong, what period they date from, or under what circumstances these people lost their lives. However, the fact that such remains have been discovered in Silvan, where enforced disappearances, unsolved murders, and serious human rights violations occurred on a large scale, particularly in the 1990s, is of extraordinary significance for investigating past events that still remain unresolved.”
