title: Fidan Ataselim: Repression and violence rise as democracy is eroded
content:
The We Will Stop Femicide Platform (KCDP) took to the streets across the country ahead of 25 November, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, to protest the cover-up of the growing number of suspicious deaths of women under the slogan, "Stop the cover-ups, shed light on suspicious deaths of women." Families of women killed by male violence stood at the forefront of demonstrations in Istanbul's Kadıköy district, demanding an end to systematic impunity and the effective implementation of Law No. 6284. We Will Stop Femicide Platform Secretary General Fidan Ataselim spoke to ANF and said that the increase in femicides and suspicious deaths of women cannot be separated from the policies of the Justice and Development Party (AKP), adding, "Violence increases as democracy is eroded."


'Women's deaths are being concealed in the name of protecting the family'


KCDP Secretary General Fidan Ataselim, who has been fighting against femicide for years, said that they took to the streets on this year's International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women to draw particular attention to the growing number of suspicious deaths of women. Fidan Ataselim said that the increase in male violence against women cannot be considered independently of the AKP's policies: "This is a consequence of the government's 'Decade of Family and Population' policies. We repeatedly warned against this, but they did not listen. Women are most often killed within the family by the men closest to them. If you say that 'the family is important,' not only are women killed, but their deaths also begin to be concealed. Indeed, femicides and suspicious deaths of women have increased as a result of these family-centered policies."


'A strong response to rights violations can prevent further violations'


Fidan Ataselim said that 247 femicides and 289 suspicious deaths of women were recorded in the first ten months of 2026 alone, pointing out that suspicious deaths of women have increased significantly, just like femicides. Fidan Ataselim said that violence against women cannot be explained solely through family policies and must be considered in conjunction with the restriction of democratic rights and freedoms in the country: "Everything is so interconnected and forms part of a whole. Those who support the appointment of trustees, those who support the annulment of elections and those who profiteer from funding, when you consider them all together, you see that once you begin to undermine democracy, you also undermine every relationship in which democracy plays a role. For example, the family is promoted as the smallest unit of society and the foundation of property ownership, creating conditions in which women are disregarded within the family and subjected to treatment that goes even beyond slavery. The AKP's definition of the family is limited to families that resemble them and conform to their mindset and interests. They want a uniform family model. We already see this in their overall policies. Repression and violence increase as democracy is eroded. This repression and violence increase not only against women but against society as a whole. However, the first targets of this repression and violence are women, who are relegated to the very bottom of all inequalities. Beyond women, we also see what LGBTQ+ people are experiencing today. They said, 'My family is safe,' and shelved the entire issue of freedom of association. That is why we always say that no one can disregard equal citizenship. There is such a thing as equal citizenship, the right to organize and freedom of expression. When were these rights of ours shelved? Yet they are able to do this in practice through repression. That is why I say that repression and violence increase as democracy is undermined. This repression and violence are not only increasing but are also being concealed, as we see in suspicious deaths of women. This situation cannot be separated from the struggle for democracy. If a strong response is mounted when such rights violations occur, further violations can be prevented. However, when no response is possible, these violations spread, as they do today. The attitude of saying, 'This person is not one of us, that person is not one of us,' ultimately leaves everyone in the same situation, with trustees being appointed everywhere."

title: '1001 Signatures for a Democratic Republic and Peace' initiative issues four-point declaration
content:
The '1001 Signatures for a Democratic Republic and Peace' initiative, formed by artists, academics and human rights defenders, will publicly announce its “Seven Climates, Seven Regions” campaign, launched as part of its signature drive, at a press conference to be held at the Taksim Hill Hotel in Istanbul’s Beyoğlu district today.


In a statement, the initiative said it would put forward a concrete vision for peace and the peace process under the slogan: “A better country is possible for all of us, across seven climates and seven regions.”


The statement emphasised the need to strengthen collective voices and determination in order to heal the wounds of the past, develop solutions to present-day problems together and build the future collectively.


The four-point declaration issued by the initiative highlights the following demands:


"- In the context of the ongoing peace process in Turkey, we support disarmament as an initial step and the complete removal of all forms of violence from the country's and society's agenda.


- Recognising that the root cause of the problem lies in the denial of Kurdish existence, we support demands for equal citizenship to be constitutionally guaranteed, for rights relating to education and instruction in one's mother tongue to be recognised, and for efforts to address historical injustices.


- We support efforts to establish the Republic of Turkey on the foundations of a free, democratic state governed by the rule of law, as well as demands for the full implementation of European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) rulings.


- We support ensuring that the actors involved in resolving this conflict, which has persisted throughout the history of the Republic of Turkey, are able to negotiate under free and equal conditions. We also support the implementation of the principle of the

Right to Hope

, in line with ECtHR rulings and the demands of the Council of Europe's Committee of Ministers."

title: Applications for violence and rights violations in Amed increase by 36%
content:
The Amed Network Against Violence has published its 2026 Violence Report, covering the period from 23 November 2025 to 23 November 2026.


Speaking at the presentation, held at the Tahir Elçi Conference Hall of the Amed Bar Association, lawyer Zilan Esen stated that, according to the network’s shared database, 7,145 applications had been recorded in the city. This represents a 36% increase compared with the previous year, when 5,253 applications were registered.


According to the report, applications relating to psychological violence increased by 34.4%, economic violence by 58.7%, physical violence by 43.7% and sexual violence by 27.2%.


Cases of intentional homicide rose from 4 to 17, an increase of 325%, while attempted intentional homicide cases increased from 14 to 18. In addition, five suspicious deaths were recorded.


Reports of torture and ill-treatment increased from 9 to 80, cases of pressure by law enforcement from 3 to 22, and incidents of ill-treatment in prisons from 4 to 14.


The report also stated that four assaults and one murder targeting LGBTI+ people had been recorded.


The network called for the Istanbul Convention to be reinstated, the effective implementation of Law No. 6284, effective investigations into cases of violence against women, and the expansion of free legal assistance and shelter services.


The statement concluded with the slogan “Jin, jiyan, azadî” (Woman, life, freedom).

author: Unknown
title: Bihar Munzîr: Violence and killings persist where women are not free
content:
Bihar Munzîr, an executive of the People's Development Organization (PDO), spoke to ANF about the situation of women in Southern Kurdistan (Başûr) as events and marches are taking place this week for the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. Bihar Munzîr drew attention to femicides, cases of self-immolation among women, child marriages and shortcomings in the implementation of laws, saying, "Femicides and cases of self-immolation remain at high levels. Last year, 69 women were killed."


Femicides and cases of self-immolation remain high


Bihar Munzîr said that violence against women remains at high levels in Southern Kurdistan, with femicides and cases of self-immolation among women constituting some of the most severe forms of violence. According to the organization's statistics, 69 women were killed in the Kurdistan Region last year by close family members, including their husbands, brothers or fathers.


Munzîr also addressed child marriages, saying that numerous attempts had been made to introduce legislation incompatible with human and children's rights following amendments to Iraq's Personal Status Law. However, she said that the legislation was not directly implemented in the Kurdistan Region.


Perpetrators of femicide go unpunished


Munzîr said that there were serious shortcomings in the implementation of laws in the Kurdistan Region, particularly in cases involving femicide and violence against women, and that disputes were often settled through tribal reconciliation mechanisms. She added that perpetrators either went unpunished or had their prison sentences reduced, emphasizing the need for sanctions that would prevent such crimes from recurring.


Munzîr underlined that there were numerous shortcomings and problems in the implementation of laws, adding, "Tribes and relatives of perpetrators frequently interfere in cases involving femicide and violence against women." She stressed that laws in the Kurdistan Region still failed to guarantee equality between women and men in certain areas and drew attention to the issue of polygamy. She explained that a man who was already married in the Kurdistan Region could officially register a second marriage elsewhere.


Patriarchal society makes decisions about women's lives


Munzîr said that one of the fundamental problems in the Kurdistan Region was women's inability to make decisions about their own lives and drew attention to the influence of tribes and patriarchal social structures over women's lives. She said that these structures remained the determining forces rather than strong women's institutions and the rule of law.


Munzîr added that women remained subject to social control when they could not make their own decisions about their lives, education and employment. "If a woman is not free, if someone else makes decisions about her life and controls her, she becomes an easy target for violence and killing," she remarked.


Munzîr said that women's and human rights organizations were carrying out important work to document violations against women, prepare reports, exert pressure and raise public awareness despite institutional shortcomings. She said that these efforts needed to be supported by a more comprehensive program and strategy.


A free and safe society must be built


PDO executive Bihar Munzîr drew attention to the campaign launched by the March 8 Network and other organizations against femicides and cases of self-immolation among women. She said that the campaign, conducted in the Kurdistan Region, Kirkuk (Kerkûk) and abroad, was a long-term initiative and emphasized the importance of raising public awareness through the media, art and various activities.


Munzîr added that everyone must assume their responsibilities and that institutions must be mobilized to prevent femicides and cases of self-immolation among women. She called for the construction of a society in which women and all people are free and safe.

author: Sofia Amaral
title: O final anticlimático da COP31, com Claudio Angelo
content:
26 de novembro de 2026 · Coordenador do Observatório do Clima faz um balanço da COP31

Na Turquia, o consenso não prevaleceu e a COP31 terminou sem um acordo depois que União Europeia, Panamá, Reino Unido e outros países se recusaram a assinar a decisão final. Mas será que esse desfecho anti-climático é um fracasso ou não aceitar um acordo ruim é também uma forma importante de resolução? O Bom dia, fim do mundo dessa semana recebe Claudio Angelo, que é coordenador de política internacional do Observatório do Clima e já acompanhou catorze COP para um balanço da COP31. Ouça agora.

No quadro “Se é pra falar de economia…”, Eliane Barbosa reflete como o fracasso da COP31 pode nos ajudar a repensar o que produzimos.

title: İstanbul Boğazı'nda gemi trafiği askıya alındı
content:
Rusya'da insansız hava aracı (İHA) saldırısına uğradıktan sonra Giresun açıklarına kadar sürüklenen 'Fortis' isimli kuru yük gemisi, İstanbul Boğazı'ndan geçiriliyor. Boğaz trafiği çift yönlü olarak geçici süreyle askıya alınırken, geçiş dronla havadan görüntülendi.

Rusya'nın Novorossiysk Limanı'ndan Mersin'e gitmek üzere hareket eden Rus bayraklı kuru yük gemisi 'Fortis', ekim ayında Karadeniz'de İHA saldırısına uğrayarak hasar aldı. Saldırının ardından 3 bin 300 tonluk geminin 10 mürettebatı tahliye edildi. Giresun açıklarına sürüklenen gemi, Keşap kıyılarına alınarak kurtarma ve soğutma çalışmaları yapıldı. Marinsal 3 isimli römorkör tarafından çekilerek İstanbul Boğazı'na getirilen gemi, Kıyı Emniyeti Genel Müdürlüğü'ne bağlı Kurtarma 3, Kurtarma 9 ve Mehmetçik römorkörleri eşliğinde boğazdan geçiriliyor.

Gemide yapılan incelemenin ardından hurdaya ayrılmasına karar verildiği, Aliağa tersanelerine götürüldükten sonra söküm işleminin gerçekleştirileceği öğrenildi. Geminin geçişi nedeniyle İstanbul Boğazı'nda gemi trafiği çift yönlü olarak geçici süreyle askıya alındı.

author: CNT Granada
title: Victoria sindical: Sedena
content:
Tras la ruptura del diálogo por parte de la empresa SEDENA con la Sección Sindical de CNT, la convocatoria de concentración del 17 de julio y el éxito de la movilización, retomamos las reuniones con la empresa y conseguimos avances importantes en nuestras reivindicaciones: el abono de las cantidades adeudadas correspondientes a la prórroga extraordinaria de abril a agosto de 2025, el reconocimiento de 30 minutos de formación computables en la jornada en los turnos de tarde seguidos del turno de nocturna y la implantación de un protocolo frente a las altas temperaturas.


Lo que vemos aquí, es que las trabajadoras han conseguido mediante la lucha aquello que la empresa se negó a escuchar desde un primer momento. Seguimos adelante, porque sabemos que la fuerza de la clase trabajadora reside en su capacidad para organizarse y luchar colectivamente. No nos conformamos con lo alcanzado, seguimos organizadas, manteniendo la presión y defendiendo que cada derecho se conquista desde la acción sindical y la lucha colectiva.


Juntas somos más fuertes.


¡¡La lucha es el único camino!!


La entrada

Victoria sindical: Sedena

 se publicó primero en

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

.

author: Unknown
title: Şavşat Belediyesi'nden zorunlu emekli edilen 10 işçi için işe iade kararı
content:
Artvin – Şavşat Belediyesi'ndeki sözleşmeleri yenilenmeyerek zorunlu emekliliğe sevk edilen 10 işçi, işe iade talebiyle açtığı davayı kazandı. Belediye-İş Sendikası Rize Şube Başkanı Yaşar Kaspar, “Mahkeme, Şavşat Belediyesi’nin haksız ve hukuksuz uygulamasına dur demiştir. İşçilerimizin bir an önce görevlerine başlatılmasını talep ediyoruz” dedi.

Son yerel seçimlerinin ardından CHP’den AKP’ye geçen Şavşat Belediyesi’nde, sözleşmeleri yenilenmeyen ve zorunlu emekliliğe sevk edilen 10 işçi, işe iade talebiyle açtığı davaları kazandı.

Kararın ardından işçiler ve Belediye-İş Sendikası temsilcileri basın açıklaması yaparak belediye yönetimine mahkeme kararının uygulanması ve işçilerin görevlerine başlatılması çağrısında bulundu.

Belediye-İş Sendikası Rize Şube Başkanı Yaşar Kaspar, 10 işçinin işe iade davasının işçilerin lehine sonuçlandığını belirterek, “Mahkeme, Şavşat Belediyesi’nin haksız ve hukuksuz uygulamasına dur demiştir. Belediye başkanından ve yönetiminden arkadaşlarımızın işe başlatılması için gerekli işlemleri bir an önce yapmalarını talep ediyoruz. Burada ödenecek tazminatlar ve paralar Şavşat halkının parasıdır. Belediye başkanının cebinden ödeyeceği paralar değildir. Mahkeme, diğer duruşmamızda olduğu gibi haksızlığa bir kez daha dur demiştir” ifadelerini kullandı.

Belediye-İş Sendikası Rize-Artvin Şubesi yöneticisi ve Şavşat Belediyesi işyeri temsilcisi Vural Şimşek ise sürecin yalnızca hukuki değil, vicdani ve ahlaki boyutlarının da bulunduğunu ifade etti.

Şimşek, belediye çalışanlarının yıllarca Şavşat halkına hizmet ettiğini belirterek, “Biz büyük bir aileyiz. Biz bu ailenin dağılmasının ve parçalanmasının vicdani, ahlaki ve hukuki boyutlarıyla ilgili Şavşat kamuoyunun ve Türkiye kamuoyunun aydınlanmasını istiyorduk. Bu ailede herhangi bir hukuksuzluk yoktu, yüz kızartıcı bir suç işlenmemişti. Herkes yıllarca Şavşat halkına hizmet etmişti. Yargının vermiş olduğu karara gerçekten teşekkür ediyor ve saygı duyuyoruz. Arkadaşlarımızın bir an önce işe iade edilmesi için Sayın Belediye Başkanımızın ve yönetiminin harekete geçmesini istiyoruz. Kırgınlık ve dargınlıkların daha da büyümesine izin verilmeden, bu meselenin çözüme kavuşturulmasından yanayız” dedi.

İşe iade kararı verilen işçilerden Aşkın Kamacı da, “Şavşat Belediyesi’nden haksız yere işimizden edildik. Sokağa koyulduk diyebilirim. 20 aylık hukuk mücadelemiz sonucunu verdi. Bir ay içerisinde işe başlamamız gerekiyor. Belediye başkanından işimizi istiyoruz. Aynı belediyede çalışmak istiyoruz. Bizler mağdur edildik, mağduriyetimizin giderilmesini istiyoruz. Hukuka saygımız sonsuzdur. Belediye başkanının da hukuka saygılı olmasını temenni ediyorum” ifadelerini kullandı.

author: Unknown
title: Pakistan'da inşaat halindeki altı katlı binanın çöktü: 3 kişi öldü, 14 kişi yaralandı
content:
Pakistan'ın güneyindeki Sindh eyaletinde inşaat halindeki bir binanın çökmesi sonucu ölenler ve yaralananlar oldu.

Geo News kanalının haberine göre, Karaçi kentinde altı katlı bir bina inşaatı çöktü. Arama kurtarma yetkilileri, çöken binanın enkazında kalan 3 kişinin öldüğünü, 14 kişinin yaralandığını duyurdu.

Polis, bina sahibi, müteahhit ve yetkililerin de aralarında olduğu 10 kişi hakkında bilinçli taksirle ölüme neden olma ve ihmal suçlamalarıyla dava açıldığı, bu kişilerden 4'ünün gözaltına alındığı bilgisini paylaştı.

Sindh Eyaleti Başbakanı Murad Ali Şah, basına yaptığı açıklamada, bina için tek kat izni alındığını ancak altı kat yapıldığını söyledi.

Şah, sorumlular hakkında işlem yapılması çağrısında bulundu.

author: CNT Villaverde Alto - Comarcal Sur de Madrid
title: Ante las elecciones del 29N: tu candidato, el sindicato
content:
Ante la convocatoria de elecciones generales del próximo 29 de noviembre, desde CNT Comarcal Sur interpelamos al conjunto de nuestra clase, las trabajadoras, las desposeídas, las perseguidas y represaliadas a posicionarse activamente en un solo sentido:

la organización activa desde el sindicalismo

.


Consideramos que

no nos encontramos en el momento de llamar a la participación de nuestra clase en un sentido u otro del juego electoral

, ya sea ejerciendo la abstención masiva o concediendo el apoyo a quien pueda sernos de mayor interés práctico, pues creemos que la coyuntura actual no permite grandes movilizaciones organizadas, al tiempo que, hoy por hoy, pueden existir intereses contrapuestos entre distintos sectores de nuestra clase que empujen a optar por distintas vías de participación o no participación en el baile de collares que llevará el perro del capital.


No obstante, creemos indispensable posicionarnos y animar a toda nuestra clase a hacerlo en el mismo sentido. Apostamos, como no podía ser de otro modo, por el Sindicato. A nuestro juicio, la independencia de clase debe construirse desde una organización al margen de los vaivenes electorales, una organización que no aspire a la gestión del Estado ni a servir a los intereses del capital ya sea desde su ala izquierda o derecha: una organización, en definitiva,

independiente en todos sus aspectos como lo es CNT

. Abogamos, como siempre hemos hecho, por una CNT

sin subvenciones

 de ningún tipo, así como

sin liberados

; una CNT compuesta de principio a fin por compañeras de clase,

militantes que construyen día a día el Sindicato

 y lo impulsan en la dirección que consideran más juiciosa desde

la toma colectiva de acuerdos en una estructura que se despliega desde abajo hacia arriba

, donde no pueda haber dirigentes que secuestren el poder de decisión, sino una afiliación militante que, de forma verdaderamente democrática, impone la línea política para su organización.


Esta es, en suma, la independencia de clase a la que aspiramos a través de la organización activa. La organización mediante un Sindicato que despliega a la par el trabajo político necesario para alcanzar sus objetivos revolucionarios mientras, en el día a día, desarrolla el necesario trabajo de base en los centros de trabajo para

defender los intereses de nuestra clase

 y, sobre todo,

organizar a las trabajadoras en una forma alternativa de sindicalismo

 que nos oriente hacia la consecución de objetivos mucho más grandes.


Ante la pantomima electoral, nosotras decimos: Sindicato

. Si ocho años de legislatura progresista nos han demostrado algo es que, sin duda, no puede confiarse en absoluto en la palabra del ala izquierda. No debe olvidarse jamás que quien ha reprimido a las compañeras docentes y estudiantes de la Comunidad de Madrid a lo largo de las siete semanas de Huelga Indefinida ha sido

el cuerpo policial directamente dependiente del gobierno del Estado

. Mismo cuerpo que ha agredido tanto por la fuerza como por el uso de gases lacrimógenos y pimienta a las compañeras en los piquetes informativos del pasado 11N en la jornada de Huelga General,

llegando a producirse detenciones y encarcelamientos a lo largo del país

.


Si el ala progresista del parlamento pretende agitar el espantajo de la derecha para cosechar votos, no podemos olvidar por un momento que el monstruo no está a las puertas,

se encuentra ya entre nosotras

. Encarnado en un gobierno que

nunca derogó la ley mordaza

 durante ocho años en el poder, un gobierno que

ha enviado tanquetas contra trabajadoras

 en huelga, que

ha infiltrado agentes

 de policía en colectivos de distintos signo, que

jamás se molestó en atajar de raíz el problema de la vivienda

, limitándose a posicionarse tímidamente cuando pudo comprobar que la movilización en la calle había alcanzado tal punto que podía servir a sus intereses particulares. Tanto con este caso como con el de la Huelga General del 11N, jamás permitiremos que este gobierno pretenda ponerse a la cabeza de su éxito: fueron las organizaciones políticas de base en la calle la que impulsaron sendas oleadas consecutivas, organizadas de forma unitaria y ajenas por completo a los intereses partidarios, teniendo claros sus objetivos

gobernase quien gobernase

.


Sabemos igualmente bien cuál es la alternativa que se esboza al actual gobierno saliente. Lo sabemos, precisamente, porque

la llevamos sufriendo y combatiendo en la Comunidad de Madrid

 los últimos …

author: Unknown
title: Kağıthane’de tamirciyi darbedip araçla kaçırdılar iddiası: 2 kişi tutuklandı
content:
Kağıthane'de devriye ekiplerinin durdurduğu 3 kişinin yanındaki motosikletin çalıntı çıkmasının ardından, aracı tamir ettiği belirtilen Suriye uyruklu Moussa El A.'nın çalıştığı depoya gelen şüphelilerce tekme ve yumruklarla darbedildiği öne sürüldü. İddiaya göre El A.'yı otomobil bagajına koymakta başarılı olamayan grup, yaşanan arbede sırasında kendisini zorla otomobile bindirerek kaçırdı. Saldırganların elinden kurtulmayı başaran El A.'nın şikayeti üzerine yürütülen işlemlerde Yusuf Bilal Y. ve Vedat Y. tutuklandı.

Saldırı, 8 Ekim Perşembe günü saat 23.00 civarında Gürsel Mahallesi'nde yaşandı. Alınan bilgilere göre devriye ekipleri, hal ve hareketlerinden şüphelendikleri 3 kişiyi durdurdu. Ekiplerin, yanlarındaki plakasız motosikletin kime ait olduğunu sorması üzerine, aracın Moussa El A.'dan alındığı ve Umut T.'ye satmak için bir araya geldiklerini ileri sürdü. Şasi numarasının silindiği tespit edilen motosikletin, motor numarası üzerinden yapılan incelemede çalıntı olduğu ortaya çıktı.

Motosikletin çalıntı olduğunun belirlenmesi üzerine Yusuf Bilal Y.'nin, tamirci Moussa El A.'nın bulunduğu depoya gittiği öne sürüldü. Aracı El A.'nın sattığını savunan Yusuf Bilal Y.'nin saldırısının ardından, bir müddet sonra Ö.Y.'nin babası 38 yaşındaki Vedat Y. de depoya geldi. El A.'yı dışarı çıkararak darbeden zanlıların, kendisini zorla otomobile bindirmek istediği iddia edildi. Otomobile binmek istemeyen El A.'nın şüphelilerden polis çağırmalarını talep ettiği, bunun üzerine şüphelilerin telefonla olay yerine başka kişileri çağırdığı kaydedildi.

Sokakta 4-5 kişinin tekme ve yumruklarla vurduğu öne sürülen El A.'nın otomobilin bagajına konulmak istendiği, direnmesi nedeniyle sokakta arbede çıktığı aktarıldı. Yaklaşık 2 dakika süren ve bağırışların duyulduğu arbedenin ardından El A.'yı bagaja sokamayan grubun, onu zorla otomobile bindirerek bölgeden uzaklaştırdığı ve araç içinde de darbettiği iddia edildi. O anların güvenlik ya da cep telefonu kamerasına yansıdığı belirtildi.

Kaçırıldığı kişilerin elinden kurtulan El A., motosikletin çalıntı olduğunu saptayan polis ekiplerinin bulunduğu noktaya gitti. Vedat Y.'nin kendisine vurduğunu ifade eden El A., şüphelilerden şikayetçi oldu. M.G. ve Ö.Y. Kağıthane Çocuk Büro Amirliğine, diğer kişiler ise işlemleri için polis merkezine sevk edildi. Soruşturma kapsamında yakalanan Yusuf Bilal Y. ve Vedat Y., sevk edildikleri mahkemece tutuklanarak cezaevine gönderildi.

İddiaya göre hadise öncesinde mahalleden tanıdığı 2 kişi, tamir edilmesi amacıyla El A.'ya motosiklet getirdi. Saat 17.00 sıralarında teslim aldığı aracın arka fren teli ile balatasını yenileyen El A.'nın, motosikleti saat 20.30 civarında teslim ettiği belirtildi. Aracın çalıntı olduğunun anlaşılması sonrasında motosikleti El A.'dan satın aldığını öne süren Ö.Y.'nin, sorumluluktan kaçmak amacıyla tamirciye iftira attığı iddia edildi.

author: Brian Hioe
title: What is the Future of KMT-TPP Cooperation?
content:
THE KMT AND TPP’S future cooperation–or lack thereof–has increasingly become questioned in the course of elections.

The TPP would seem to be at a crossroads. The party was originally built as a vehicle for party founder Ko Wen-je’s bid for the presidency. But Ko is likely to return to jail soon on corruption charges over accepting bribes to expand the floor area of the Core Pacific City Mall.

With Huang Kuo-chang as the party’s acting chair, the party has lost many of its previous visible political figures. As many were Ko associates, it is possible that Huang drove them out of the party in his quest to maintain power of the party, with Huang having historically not been part of the TPP before suddenly taking leadership. This occurs even as Huang publicly vows fidelity to Ko and his ideals.

Likewise, though the TPP could have controlled the balance of power in the legislature by playing the DPP and KMT off from each other and, in that way, becoming the “kingmaker” within the Legislative Yuan, this has not occurred. Instead, the TPP has simply sided with the KMT on most policy initiatives–even highly controversial ones, such as drastically slashing the government budget, freezing the Constitutional Court, or expanding legislative powers.

This apparent lack of awareness that the party’s best interests were served by counter-balancing between the KMT and DPP, in line with the party’s claim to be beyond traditional partisan divisions in Taiwanese politics, is probably due to the fact that the majority of its politicians come from pan-Blue backgrounds. It may have been path dependency that caused the TPP to become overly reliant on the KMT.

ONE NOTES that party chair Huang Kuo-chang originally planned to run for New Taipei mayor, given that he was formerly a legislator of Xizhi. But Huang backed out in favor of Lee Shu-chuan of the KMT when polling results showed a stronger performance by Lee. That Lee is struggling against Su Chiao-hui of the DPP may make it sting that the KMT passed over Huang.

There are some places where the KMT has declined to run a candidate, but instead decided to back a TPP one. Hsinchu city mayor Ann Kao, for example, is still often regarded as part of the TPP despite technically being an independent, having departed the party after facing corruption charges that she was later acquitted of. Kao is running with the backing of the KMT and TPP, though she has often used the KMT’s blue when campaigning.

Chiayi City is another constituency where a TPP candidate is running with the endorsement of the KMT and TPP. However, the TPP candidate there, Chiang Chi-kai, recently courted controversy after being caught on camera urinating in public on a bush while on the campaign trail.

Still, splits opened up between the KMT and TPP in Zhubei, the administrative capital of Hsinchu County. There, the KMT has nominated Wu Hsu-chih, while the TPP has nominated Chiu Chen-yuan, but neither candidate agreed to back out in favor of the other.

As such, this led KMT chair Cheng Li-wun to declare an end to political cooperation between the KMT and TPP in Hsinchu County as a whole. This has not prevented Chiang Wan-an and pan-Blue commentator Jaw Shaw-kong from making public appearances with Chiu, in what has been questioned as potentially violating party discipline. That both party heavyweights have been willing to break from party discipline may reflect that Cheng’s grip over the KMT is quite weak at present.

Oppositely, in Hualien, the TPP county branch chair, Chang Tien-min, broke from party discipline to endorse independent Chang Chun rather than KMT nominee Yu Shu-chen. Chang has criticized Yu as beholden to KMT legislative caucus chair Fu Kun-chi’s political dynasty, which has historically dominated Hualien.

IN EVALUATING the current state of TPP-KMT relations, then, one sees cooperation in some districts while open competition in others. It is generally thought that current KMT chair Cheng Li-wun does not favor cooperating with the TPP, seeing it as splitting votes from the KMT and being an unnecessary collaborator, while others in the KMT, such as Chiang Wan-an, cling to the TPP as part of an attempt to rally votes.

author: Operation Münsterland
title: Herbstzauber im Pappelwäldchen – Unterwegs mit Dackel Börne
content:
Der Herbst zeigt sich von seiner schönsten Seite!


Begleitet uns auf einem gemütlichen Spaziergang durch das Pappelwäldchen in Ennigerloh. Zwischen bunten Blättern, herbstlichen Farben und der besonderen Ruhe des Waldes genießen wir die Natur und lassen einfach mal die Seele baumeln.


Natürlich darf einer dabei nicht fehlen: Unser Dackel Börne! 🐶 Mit seiner neugierigen Nase und seiner ganz eigenen Art macht er jeden Spaziergang zu einem kleinen Abenteuer.


Diese Dia-Show fängt einige schöne Augenblicke eines herbstlichen Ausflugs ein – ganz ohne Hektik, dafür mit viel Natur, frischer Luft und kleinen Momenten zum Genießen.


Denn bei Operation Münsterland geht es nicht darum, immer etwas Großes zu erleben. Manchmal sind es gerade die kleinen Ausflüge vor der Haustür, die besonders schön sind.


Viel Spaß beim Anschauen!

author: Gabriel Teles
title: O lado oculto da Black Friday
content:
Todos os anos, quando chega a Black Friday, voltam a circular denúncias sobre as estratégias utilizadas pelas empresas para

enganar

 os consumidores. A mais conhecida delas consiste em aumentar artificialmente os preços nas semanas anteriores, para depois anunciar descontos que, na realidade, pouco ou nada representam. É a famosa promoção pela “metade do dobro”.


Essas práticas merecem ser denunciadas. Entretanto,

existe um aspecto mais profundo da Black Friday que raramente aparece nas discussões públicas: a exploração e a precarização do trabalho daqueles que tornam possível a circulação de milhões de mercadorias em um intervalo tão curto.


Por trás das propagandas, dos descontos e das promessas de entrega rápida, existe uma extensa infraestrutura logística sustentada pelo trabalho de milhares de pessoas.

São trabalhadores que descarregam caminhões, recebem mercadorias, organizam estoques, separam pedidos, embalam produtos e preparam encomendas para expedição.

 Sem essas atividades, nenhuma das grandes plataformas de comércio eletrônico conseguiria cumprir aquilo que promete aos consumidores.


A dimensão dessa infraestrutura pode ser percebida pelos próprios números do setor. Segundo

projeções

 da Associação Brasileira de Inteligência Artificial e E-commerce (Abiacom), a semana da Black Friday de 2026 deverá movimentar aproximadamente R$ 16,6 bilhões no comércio eletrônico brasileiro, crescimento de 24,4% em relação ao mesmo período de 2025. A quantidade de pedidos deverá passar de 16,51 milhões para 21,66 milhões, um aumento de 31,2% em apenas um ano.


Essas milhões de mercadorias precisam ser movimentadas em um período curto. Cada pedido realizado pelo consumidor corresponde a uma sequência de operações, desde a localização do produto no estoque até sua expedição e entrega. Uma das principais respostas empresariais consiste na contratação massiva de trabalhadores temporários.


Somente neste mês de novembro de 2026 a Amazon anunciou a abertura de 12 mil vagas temporárias para atender ao aumento da demanda durante a Black Friday.

 A empresa

informou

 também que sua infraestrutura logística brasileira havia alcançado 350 unidades, após a abertura de mais de 120 instalações desde a Black Friday anterior.


A DHL Supply Chain, uma das maiores empresas de logística do mundo, anunciou a previsão de contratar aproximadamente 2,6 mil trabalhadores temporários adicionais durante a temporada de Black Friday e Natal.

 Esse contingente representa um aumento de 38% nas contratações temporárias em relação a um mês convencional. A empresa

projeta

 movimentar mais de 37 milhões de unidades no comércio eletrônico durante o período, volume 19% superior ao de um mês convencional.


A Americanas, por sua vez,

anunciou

 mais de 3,7 mil vagas temporárias, das quais aproximadamente 760 seriam destinadas às operações logísticas.


Os anúncios empresariais apresentam essas contratações como oportunidades de emprego e demonstrações do dinamismo econômico do setor.

Entretanto, grande parte desse contingente de temporários trabalha sob rotinas exaustivas, com funções repetitivas e metas rígidas, altamente vigiados por sistemas tecnológicos, além de não terem segurança do que vai acontecer quando o período de vendas passa. 


A legislação brasileira reconhece o trabalho temporário como modalidade destinada a atender necessidades transitórias de substituição de pessoal ou demandas complementares de serviços. Quando a demanda diminui, as empresas podem reduzir o contingente sem necessariamente incorporar aqueles que foram mobilizados para sustentar a expansão das vendas.


Centro de Distribuição da Amazon em Recife, inaugurado em 2024


O que acontece dentro dos galpões?


Em abril de 2025, publiquei no

Le Monde Diplomatique

 o artigo

Galpões logísticos e os novos rostos da exploração

, no qual discutia como a expansão do comércio eletrônico estava acompanhada pela constituição de novos espaços de exploração do trabalho.


Naquele momento, chamei atenção para uma contradição: as grandes plataformas anunciavam uma economia cada vez mais automatizada, enquanto seus centros de distribuição continuavam dependendo de uma imensa quantidade de trabalho humano, submetido a formas sofisticadas de controle da produtividade.


Desde então, minha pesquisa em sociologia do trabalho permitiu avançar na investigação desse processo.

author: Unknown
title: Do you remember 17 octobre ? - Réflexions et propositions pour le mouvement
content:
Courte brochure publiée le 12 novembre dernier. Réflexions et propositions pour le mouvement.


Disponible sur :

https://sanscontrolerevolution.wordpress.com/2026/11/12/do-you-remember-17-octobre/


Les blocus lycéens continuent, malgré la propagande du gouvernement sur «

 

l'essoufflement du mouvement

 

» pour pousser à la résignation. La semaine de rentrée, des dizaines de lycées ont été bloqués, et ce malgré le changement de politique répressive visant au déblocage coûte que coûte et à l'intimidation des lycéens et les manipulations des rectorats, qui déclarent qu'un établissement n'est pas bloqué dès qu'il y a 15 élèves dedans. Les pratiques qui ont fait la radicalité des luttes lycéennes depuis septembre n'ont pas disparu. Comme avant les vacances de la Toussaint, qui auraient pu tout éteindre, des portails ont brûlé, des mortiers ont été utilisés à l'intérieur même des établissements, des proviseurs ont été attaqués, des lycées ont été incendiés comme à Toulouse ou à Lyon. Cependant, si l'on regarde ailleurs qu'aux portes des lycées, peu de choses se passent depuis le 17 octobre, ou plutôt ce qui se passe pourrait malheureusement augurer d'une lente mort de la lutte actuelle qui serait décidée par les syndicats, contentée par les quelques ajustements octroyés par l'État, tout le monde se mettant d'accord pour éteindre la conflictualité et «

 

traduire

 

» la révolte dans la bataille des urnes en 2027 (c'est-à-dire rentrer chez soi et retrouver la normalité mortifère d'avant).


Le 17 octobre a été l'occasion d'une formidable explosion de la révolte et a permis un certain élargissement de la lutte à la question de la vie quotidienne sous la domination capitaliste, que l'on pourrait résumer ainsi : toujours plus d'exploitation, toujours plus d'autorité, toujours moins de thunes pour vivre. Ce jour a signifié l'entrée en lutte de nombreuses personnes, donnant une nouvelle ampleur aux luttes initiées par les lycéens, et a témoigné d'un débordement considérable de l'encadrement externe (le maintien de l'ordre) et interne (syndicats, partis, pacificateurs démocrates). Depuis, lors des jours de mobilisations, il est compliqué de retrouver l'énergie dévastatrice du 17 qui s'était déversée sans contrôle dans les rues. Le 24 et le 31 ont été l'occasion pour l'État de montrer les muscles et pour la gauche de reprendre globalement le contrôle sur le mouvement en assignant tout le monde au calme et à la discipline. Le 5 novembre et le 7 novembre n'ont pas été différent. À part quelques affrontements et barricades ne sortant pas vraiment de la normale, les manifs partout en France ont été bien tenues ou rendues presque complètement inoffensives. Il semble que le 17 octobre a été un point de bascule dans la gestion du maintien de l'ordre. Après avoir tenté d'enterrer le mouvement à petit feu par les fermetures administratives de lycées et de facs et les manifs perlées, l'État a opté depuis cette date pour la force brute en réprimant tout azimut. En plus de la répression judiciaire extrêmement ferme, les flics sont envoyés en nombre devant les lycées pour débloquer à tout prix et intimider, les occupations étudiantes sont délogées très rapidement et les manifs servent de démonstration de force avec leurs lots d'interpellations massives et de tabassages. Le but est clair, il est toujours le même : faire peur à tout le monde, créer le sentiment d'impuissance et faire rentrer tout le monde chez soi. Mais il est clair que ces tactiques de masquages qui confinent à la méthode Coué («

 

plus que 20 lycées bloqués sur l'ensemble du territoire

 

» quand chacun d'entre nous en connait déjà une vingtaine) n'ont qu'un temps et doivent avoir une efficacité immédiate sur le retour à la normale, sinon ça se voit. La vitalité du mouvement lycéen peut facilement les déjouer… mais encore faut-il pour cela qu'il perdure et s'amplifie.


Hors des lycées, l'essentiel de la mobilisation se passe aujourd'hui dans les manifs syndicales, depuis que le mouvement a été réduit à ce que l'on connaît classiquement des mouvements sociaux portés par la gauche. Ces manifestations à intervalles définis sont sérieusement encadrées et régulées efficacement par la police. Les appels sur les réseaux sociaux à aller dans d'autres endroits que les points de rassemblements déclarés légalement sont des échecs. Les occupations étudiantes sont globalement sous la forme des «

 

universités populaires

 

» qui reproduisent juste la fac version …

author: Unknown
title: Stains : non à la “classe défense” et à ses dérives au collège Joliot Curie
content:
Communiqué des personnels du collège Joliot Curie de Stains, mobilisé⋅es contre la “classe défense et sécurité globales”, le 24 novembre 2026


Jusqu'à preuve du contraire, utiliser une arme factice ou faire du collège une officine de recrutement de l'armée ne font pas partie des missions de l'école. C'est pourtant ce qu'ont vécu nos élèves de quatrième lors d'un atelier organisé dans le cadre du dispositif “classe de défense et de sécurité globales”.


Le 5 novembre 2026, au Fort de l'Est à Saint-Denis, nos élèves ont participé à des ateliers dits “pédagogiques” au cours desquels ils ont été mis en situation de guerre, affublés de fusils d'assaut factices et jetant des cailloux “comme si c'étaient des bombes”, leur a-t-on dit, entre deux remarques ordurières prononcées par des encadrants militaires telle que : “vous me faites chier avec vos wesh”.


Pendant ces ateliers, certain-es élèves n'étaient même pas encadré-es par des enseignant-es de notre collège. À la fin de la session, le colonel de la caserne a cru bon de leur déclarer qu'il les considérait comme de “probables futures recrues”.


Mais beaucoup plus grave, un de nos élèves a été victime d'une agression raciste négrophobe. Une encadrante lui a dit en le voyant : “Toi, tu as une bonne tête à servir”.


Les faits sont d'une extrême gravité. Ils nous indignent et nous révoltent. En aucun cas, nous ne pouvons ni n'avons le droit de mettre nos élèves en danger.


À l'heure où les discours suprémacistes prospèrent, à l'heure où un racisme décomplexé – pourtant puni par le code pénal – se donne des airs d'opinion, à l'heure où l'armée est davantage financée que l'école, à l'heure où les seules réponses apportées à une jeunesse qui doute, à une jeunesse qui s'inquiète pour son avenir, sont un pouvoir brutal et des dogmes autoritaires, nous refusons la militarisation de la jeunesse. Nous rappellerons que cette même institution (avec parmi elle, les escadrons de gendarmerie mobile, le

GIGN

 – groupe d'intervention de la gendarmerie nationale, les militaires de l'opération «

 

Sentinelle

 

») est en train de réprimer les lycéens et lycéennes qui revendiquent des conditions de travail décentes, en les mutilant et les blessant avec des armes de guerre (

LBD

, grenades de désencerclement, gaz lacrymogènes).


Des élus et des médecins ont d'ailleurs très récemment mis en garde l'opinion, et notamment l'Assemblée nationale, sur les troubles gynécologiques de long terme provoqués par les gaz lacrymogènes utilisés massivement contre des enfants depuis le début de la mobilisation lycéenne.


Quelle est donc cette logique absurde, d'une hypocrisie insoutenable, qui punit un élève quand il utilise un pétard, qui le mutile quand il réclame qu'on respecte ses droits, mais qui l'entraîne au combat militaire lors d'ateliers qui ressemblent à la guerre

 

?


En tant que personnels de l'éducation, nous affirmons que nos élèves ne doivent pas être formé-es à l'obéissance et au sacrifice. Ils n'ont pas à subir le racisme, le sexisme, les insultes d'une institution qui les maltraite en dehors de l'école.


C'est pour toutes ces raisons que nous, personnels du collège Joliot Curie de Stains mobilisés contre la classe défense, demandons la fermeture immédiate du dispositif, ainsi qu'une enquête sur les violences verbales et l'insulte raciste dont nos élèves ont été victimes.


Source :

https://www.sudeducation93.org/stains-non-a-la-classe-defense-et-a-ses-derives-au-college-joliot-curie/

author: Justin Umali
title: Lakbayan nati’y hindi papipigil: detention and the Southern Tagalog Lakbayan
content:
Detention is neither romantic nor heroic. Writing about it even less so.

To be detained is to be denied your rights, whether for a few hours or for years. For activists, detention is the state’s reward for standing up to fight. For me and the rest of Southern Tagalog Lakbayanis, detention was a method of last resort.

November 15 was the fourth day of the Lakbayan. What was supposed to be a protest march from Los Baños, Laguna to Liwasang Bonifacio became a daily struggle against police checkpoints and blockades. On the second day, our jeep’s brake lines were cut, and we were held for four hours in Biñan, Laguna. On the third day, we were blocked from crossing from San Pedro to Muntinlupa.

So we found ways to skirt around and continue our Lakbayan. On the fourth day, the police had cordoned off all routes going outside of Brgy. Sucat, Muntinlupa. Regardless, we were determined to find a way to continue.

Thus, the arrests. It took the police roughly two hours to brutalize and transport us to Camp Bagong Diwa. At least eight officers manhandled me while I tried to rescue Southern Tagalog Exposure journalist Marky Casaquite. I felt the back of my head kiss the concrete pole before the two of us went down on the ground.

The rest of us received similar treatments. Some of us were sucker punched. Others were kicked around. The worst had his knee dislocated. The entire time we asserted that there were no charges against us.

There is nothing romantic about police brutality. The state, with its monopoly on violence, can choose to impose it on the people at will. We were activists, unionists, media workers, paralegals, peasants, and indigenous youth from all over Southern Tagalog. Our weapons were our words and our principles. What could we have done against truncheons and riot shields?

But despite the brutality, I saw firsthand how determination beats physical strength. The police had barely begun their arrests when we started sending our alerts, communication, and other means. In the police trucks, we consoled each other that things would be fine while medics tended to our injuries. Those of us who were familiar with the legal system explained to the others what our rights were and what was to be expected.

When our trucks finally began to move, we started chanting: “Ang tao, ang bayan, ngayon ay lumalaban!” “Timog Katagalugan, tuloy-tuloy ang laban!” and “Reject, oppose, junk Pax Silica!” The neighborhood responded by cheering, raising their fists, and thanking us for fighting the good fight.

Even before the arrests, they were already showing their support by giving what they can. Some residents climbed a gate to give us packs of water bottles. One resident gave out hats that we could wear.

Another woman went back and forth to a nearby grocery store to buy snacks and water. She was a sari-sari store owner who asked me where we came from. When she found out that we started the Lakbayan in Los Baños, she said that she couldn’t imagine why anybody would march from Laguna to Muntinlupa. But she understood what we were marching for, and for me, that was enough.

A few days after the ASEAN Summit, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. went on record to say that he was “perplexed” why people were protesting against Pax Silica. He couldn’t imagine the ordinary Filipino being able to dissect the issue and see the initiative for what it really was: a sell-out of Philippine sovereignty for US interests.

In Sucat, coastal communities are threatened by the construction of the Laguna Lakeshore Road Network, a stretch of highway meant to expedite the transportation of raw materials and finished products from Laguna’s industrial enclaves to Manila, and ultimately, to the economic security zone in Capas, Tarlac. The reasons why the people of Sucat oppose Pax Silica are blatantly obvious.

Because we were organized and determined, we already knew going to Camp Bagong Diwa that we were only being detained to ensure that the US-Marcos II regime wouldn’t be embarrassed by popular dissent. Any charges were trumped-up and superficial. The police must have calculated that this would scare us into silence. Police officers aren’t known for being good at math.

The detention “facility” in Camp Bagong Diwa was a run-down multi-purpose hall. The tiles were broken and there were shards of ceramic on the ground. There was no ventilation to speak of. Only three out of eight air conditioners worked. Water in the bathrooms was intermittent, especially in …

author: Jian Sanz
title: ‘Trump Out 9’ freed after prolonged detention following protests
content:
8 of Trump Out 9 outside MPD upon their release. Photo from Anakbayan

“Last detained minor is free at last!” Salinlahi Alliance for Children’s Concerns” said in a statement, November 23, following the release of one of the minors last to be freed among the activists violently and arbitrarily arrested at Liwasang Bonifacio, dubbed the “Trump Out 9.”

Salinlahi said a release order for the nine detainees—including J, who is a minor—had already been issued as early as Friday, November 20. The group said, however, that his release “was delayed due to harassment and stonewalling from the Manila Youth Reception Center.”

After nearly five days in detention, eight of the nine youth activists and workers collectively known as the “Trump Out 9” were initially released on bail from the Manila Police District (MPD) on November 20.

The first three to be released were Philippine Normal University (PNU) youth activist Hizeno Aquino, Kilusang Mayo Uno (KMU) member Domingo Marbid Jr., and Alliance of Concerned Teachers (ACT) volunteer Ronald Artiaga, who were freed without charges. Five others were released on bail: Anakbayan National member William Dela Cruz, Ernanie Rafael of the commuters’ network PARA, PISTON member Cerillo Latoreno, KMU member Carla Nicoyco, and Tambisan sa Sining Novaliches Chairperson Peter John Charles Versoza.

In a statement, Anakbayan welcomed the release of Dela Cruz and seven others. “Anakbayan salutes the release of the Trump Out 9, which includes youth leader William Dela Cruz. This is the result of the people’s collective action to free victims of fascism under the Marcos regime,” the group said.

The youth organization also stressed that while the Trump Out 9 were released, the fight for justice continues. “Even though the Trump Out 9 are now free, this does not absolve the PNP of the crimes it committed. Videos clearly show people being dragged, beaten, and illegally arrested while protesting against Pax Silica and Marcos’s subservience to Trump.”

The minor, J, had been detained at the Manila Youth Reception Center (MYRC) for more than a week.

Alliance of Nationalist and Genuine Labor Organizations (ANGLO) staff Lance Vicher recalled the minor’s dedication to forwarding workers’ rights in an online post. “I still remember: you approached us on May 1 asking for a discussion on the condition of workers. You wanted to organize workers, and when I asked if you were sure, you said, ‘Determination always comes before readiness.’”

Salinlahi Alliance for Children’s Concerns denounced J’s continued detention, demanding that he be released immediately. Moreover, the alliance stressed that quarantine must never be used as an excuse to deprive a child of liberty, legal assistance, and contact with their family, citing Article 37 of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC), which states that detention be used only as a last resort and for the shortest appropriate period, with prompt access to legal assistance.

Kalipunan ng Demokratikong Kabataan (KDK) also decried MYRC’s delaying tactic, “Even though the documents for J’s release are already complete, MYRC claimed it is not possible because there is no officer-in-charge (OIC) to sign today—the same excuse they have been giving every day for the past few days.”

Footage circulating online shows that the nine activists were brutally and unlawfully apprehended during the November 15 Working People’s March at Liwasang Bonifacio, where labor and youth groups had gathered as part of ongoing protests against the impending signing of the U.S.-led Pax Silica initiative during the 49th ASEAN Summit.

In a Facebook post, Zairine Latoreno, daughter of Cerilo, one of the Trump Out 9, decried the forceful arrest of his father, who was inside an L300 vehicle. “Manila police forcibly arrested my father right inside the L300 and towed it. They carried him as if he weren’t human, treating him as if he had killed someone—as if he were one of those who stole from the Filipino people.” After her father was taken out of the vehicle and carried to the police mobile, the police towed the L300.

Zairine also stressed that police forces prevented them from immediately accessing Latoreno and providing medicine for his hypertension. author: Kerry Smith
title: NT Environment Centre demands full federal assessment of gas pipeline
content:
The Environment Centre Northern Territory (ECNT) is calling on Murray Watt, the federal Environment and Water Minister, to undertake a full environmental impact statement of the APA Group’s fracked gas export pipeline.

The Queensland portion of the pipeline, 899 kilometres, was referred to Watt on November 26.

Rather than submit the full plan, the APA Group is referring small sections of its pipeline at a time in a bid to avoid environmental scrutiny.

The Environment Centre NT’s Acting CEO Bree Ahrens described this as “approval by stealth”.

The 1561-kilometre North to East Australia Pipeline (NEAP) to Gladstone’s export port in Queensland is one piece of a bigger network being built to move fracked gas from the Northern Territory to the east coast.

APA has even split the Bulloo Interlink Pipeline Project into two federal referrals — one for Queensland and one for NSW.

ECNT estimates the pipeline would enable major expansion of fracking in the NT, having the capacity to transport gas fracked from 1000 yet-to-be-approved gas wells.

Environment Centre NT CEO Bree Ahrens said the reason APA is splitting this approval process up is an attempt to “downplay the impact of this fracked gas export pipeline, and try and push through approvals without appropriate environmental scrutiny”.

Ahrens said the NT fracking project has ever been assessed federally.

“This will be a major test of how willing the federal government is to stand up to frackers and ensure proper environmental scrutiny of the Beetaloo export pipeline.”

She said the pipeline “ploughs through habitat for dozens of threatened species on the NT side alone”, including greater bilbies, night parrots, plains wanderers. The it also runs through fragile Channel Country in south-west Queensland and the floodplains of the Kati Thanda-Lake Eyre Basin which is one of the world’s last free-flowing desert river systems.

“The fracked gas project in the NT is destructive at every stage of development. It risks groundwater in the NT, threatened species in Queensland and drives dangerous climate change when it’s burned. This is why Minister Watt must assess the whole Beetaloo-to-export chain as one project, not as convenient fragments.”

While it is being being split in two for assessment, at a state and Territory level, “the truth is that this is a single, massive fracked gas export pipeline” which the gas industry needs for its thousands of fracking wells across the NT.

[To find out more visit the Environment Centre NT.]

title: Rezo y Baile para un Buen Viaje
content:
Rezo y Baile para un Buen Viaje

En los Puyes (caracoles) zapatistas y en las comunidades -incluso en las partidistas-, los Tuneles y catequistas convocaron a un rezo para pedir por la delegación que va a encontrarse con las familias buscadoras en la Ciudad de México. Se rezó por su bienestar y el de las familias que tienen ese dolor y esa pena de no saber de un ser querido; para que les dé fuerza en su corazón para no desmayar hasta encontrarle.

Después siguió el baile, ahora ya tirando a la onda sonidera. Y ya de madrugada, salieron los vehículos de los 12 caracoles rumbo al CIDECI de San Cristóbal de las Casas. Algunos con hasta 8 horas de viaje, rebotando en las redilas y con una lluvia ligera limpiándoles el camino y el sueño, llegaron en horas del mediodía de este 25 de noviembre del 2026.

Mañana, 26 de noviembre, miles de manos estarán bordando para tratar de completar los regalos para las madres buscadoras. Todo por su culpa del capitán que primero dijo que 100, luego que 200, luego subió a 400, y ahora dice que más de 700 nacional de familiares que buscan. Así que va en su cuenta del capitán si no se completan.

Y miles de oídos se estarán preparando para escuchar y abrazar.

Desde las montañas del Sureste Mexicano.

Subcomandante Insurgente Moisés. Coordinador General. Noviembre del 2026.

author: Darío Aranda
title: Denuncia penal contra autoridades del INTA: contaminación,  censura y venenos en la sangre
content:
Por Anabel Pomar


Tras la

exoneración de la investigadora del INTA

 Virginia Aparicio, las repercusiones en torno al

censurado Proyecto Sprint

 suman un nuevo capítulo, esta vez en sede judicial. En carácter de ciudadano habitante del sudeste bonaerense, el abogado Mario Bolla (representante también de Aparicio), ingresó una denuncia ante tribunales federales. Solicitó se investigue a las autoridades jerárquicas del INTA por incumplimiento de los deberes de funcionario público y posible puesta en peligro de la salud de la población.


En la presentación ante el Ministerio Público Fiscal de Mar del Plata, el denunciante —que es acompañado en el escrito por 19 voluntarios del Proyecto Sprint en calidad de testigos— pide se investigue la posible comisión del delito contemplado en el artículo 249 del Código Penal Argentino.


Los funcionarios denunciados por el período 2023 (cuando se suspendió la participación del INTA en la investigación) son: Mariano Garmendia (presidente), Nacira Muñoz (vicepresidenta), Carlos Parera (director nacional) y Horacio Berger (director regional, que sigue en su cargo en la actualidad). Y los actuales: Presidente: Nicolás Bronzovich (presidente), Carlos Vera (vicepresidente) y Ariel Pereda (directo nacional).


La denuncia también pide que se evalué la participación del resto de los

integrantes del Consejo Directivo

, que ocupan cargos como vocales (con derecho a voto en las decisiones institucionales) tanto del sector público (son funcionarios nacionales) como del sector privado. Allí se encuentran representantes del INTA, de la Secretaría de Agricultura, Facultades de Agronomía, Facultades de Ciencias Veterinarias (Universidades Nacionales), la Asociación Argentina de Consorcios Regionales de Experimentación Agrícola (Aacrea), Confederación Intercooperativa Confederaciones Agropecuaria (Coninagro), Confederaciones Rurales Argentinas (CRA), Federación Agraria Argentina (FAA) y de la Sociedad Rural Argentina (SRA), entre otros.


Foto: Naranja Ciencia y Técnica


Ciudadanos contaminados y “huérfanos” de asistencia


El escrito de la denuncia penal señala que, desde junio de 2023, fecha en que las autoridades del INTA

decidieron suspender intempestivamente las actividades

 del Proyecto Sprint, hasta finalmente retirarse completamente en diciembre de ese año, y hasta la actualidad, los voluntarios participantes quedaron “huérfanos” de toda asistencia, contención, guía y asesoramiento oficial por parte del organismo que los convocó a participar.


El

Proyecto Sprint

, representado por el INTA en Argentina (socio número 16 identificado como CSS11-Buenos Aires dentro del proyecto), convocó la participación de personas en carácter de voluntarios. Son habitantes de zonas rurales o ciudades bonaerenses, comprendiendo las localidades de Balcarce, Necochea, Tres Arroyos, Lobería, San Cayetano y Mar del Plata. Fueron un total de 73 personas de Argentina que se prestaron como voluntarios donantes para que se les analizara en sus cuerpos la presencia de agrotóxicos.


Como informó Tierra Viva

, todas las personas testeadas tenían glifosato en su cuerpo con rango de 6 a 13 plaguicidas en orina, de 2 a 10 plaguicidas en sangre y hasta 18 plaguicidas en materia fecal. En el momento de conocerse internamente los resultados, las autoridades del INTA aceleraron la salida del organismo de ese proyecto, y jamás dieron a conocer públicamente esos resultados. Tampoco los que señalaban presencia alarmante en alimento, aire, agua y suelo, que documentan la presencia de una mezcla de agrotóxicos de 20, 30 o hasta más de 80 plaguicidas según la matriz estudiada.


La presentación judicial señala que era obligación de un organismo estatal, una vez que tuvieron en su poder los resultados alarmantes del estudio, dar intervención a las áreas de Salud de la Nación, de las provincias (en el caso, autoridades sanitarias de Buenos Aires) y de cada comuna en la cual se llevaron a cabo los muestreos. Por el contrario, institucionalmente se decidió "guardar silencio" sobre el tema, ocultar a la opinión pública y, en particular, no informar a la mayoría de los "voluntarios" los resultados obtenidos respecto a su salud.


“Ante el hallazgo de contaminantes químicos, con efectos lesivos sanitarios y ambientales diversos, tanto en el agua de consumo, el aire, como en organismos humanos y animales, los funcionarios responsables de realizar acciones tendientes a revertir un problema de salud pública, decidieron censurar …

content:
Humeur combative pour ce 26 novembre de l'éphéméride des luttes, aux quatre coins du globe. Il faut dire qu'on est bien déterminé-e-s à ne pas se laisser faire.


1920 :

 En Ukraine, les bolcheviks rompent leur seconde alliance avec Makhno, et l'armée rouge attaque Goulai-Polé, siège de la Maknovtchina, mais Makhno réussira à s'enfuir.


1927 :

 A Buenos Aires, l'anarchiste Italien Severino Di Giovanni fait sauter l'usine de cigarettes Combinados. Celle-ci avait lancé une nouvelle cigarette « pour ouvriers » qu'elle avait nommée la « Sacco et Vanzetti » (trois jours plus tôt, les deux anarchistes de Boston avaient été exécutés sur la chais électrique) afin de plaire tout de suite et d'économiser des frais d'électricité.


1970 :

 La Nouvelle Résistance Populaire (liée à la Gauche Prolétarienne) enlève le député Michel De Grailly, instigateur de nombreuses lois répressives et idéologue de la Cour de Sûreté de l'État.


1972 :

 A Dublin, probablement l'IRA fait sauter une bombe à l'extérieur du cinéma Film Centre vers 1h30 du matin.


1977 :

 A Paris, manifestation contre l'expulsion des squats du 14e arrondissement : 1000


personnes dont 300 autonomes : un squat expulsé est démuré, le siège de la SEMIREP et un car de police sont incendiés.


1978 :

 A Belfast, Albert Miles, responsable de la prison de Crumlin Road, est abattu devant chez lui par l'IRA.


1981 :

 A Garac (Gers), le Mouvement d'action révolutionnaire antinucléaire (MARAN) fait sauter un relais hertzien des PTT.


1983 :

 A Toulouse, le CLODO (Comité Liquidant et Détournant les Ordinateurs), composé de 'travailleurs de l'informatique', incendie les locaux de Speery Univac Ordinateur.


1984 :

 A Bierset, près de Liège, les Cellules Communistes Combattantes (CCC) font sauter deux pylônes et leurs installations au sol d'un centre de télécommunications de la base aérienne, qui accueille les chasseurs-bombardiers de l'OTAN.


2010 :

 A Rio de Janeiro, plus de 21.000 policiers surarmés investissent plusieurs favelas de la ville dans le but de les "pacifier", accompagnés de véhicules blindés et de soldats. Au moins 49 personnes sont tuées par balles au cours des plusieurs jours que dure cette "opération".


2013 :

 A Tegucigalpa, capitale hondurienne, des affrontements violents éclatent dans le cadre d'une lutte étudiante contre des résultats électoraux falsifiés.


2014 :

 Au Chili, dans la province de Talagante près de Santiago, le 'Groupe Anarchiste Coordonné (GAC) - Bande Organisée Mauricio Morales / Cellule Incendiaire Sebastián Oversluij' bloque des voies ferrées avec de gros rochers et des pneus incendiés en solidarité avec les anarchistes Tamara Sol Farías et Sebastián Oversluij.


2015 :

 A Tlanepantla dans la province de Puebla au Mexique, une manifestation a lieu contre le maire et sa politique. Rapidement, la manifestation tourne à l'affrontement contre la police venue réprimer la grogne, des molotovs font leur apparition et plusieurs véhicules du maire sont incendiés.


 A Maracaibo au Venezuela, c'est un bus qui est brûlé par un groupe de manifestant-e-s masqué-e-s lors d'une protestation.

author: Jeremy Brecher, Alexandria Shaner
title: United States: ‘Now the real work begins’
content:
Voters have just delivered an overwhelming rejection of United States President Donald Trump, opening a real opportunity to limit his drive to lock the country further into oil, gas and coal.

Labour historian and organiser, Jeremy Brecher, argues that this is only a starting point. Even if the worst of Trump’s fossil fuel agenda is blocked, the US is still on course to become a “fossil fuel island”, paying more for energy and falling behind economically while much of the world shifts to cheap solar, wind and batteries.

In his new report, The Greentech Revolution, Brecher makes the case that avoiding that fate means embracing a just transition to a fossil free economy.

Brecher stresses that cheaper technology won’t get us there on its own. What decides the outcome is who owns and controls the energy system, what it’s for, and whether ordinary people get a say. That fight is already underway in city halls, statehouses, and neighbourhoods organising against data centres.

With the midterms behind us, the real work begins now. I asked Brecher what that work looks like, from policy fights to organising well beyond the ballot box.

The midterms are over, and you say limiting Trump won’t be enough. What’s the gap between blocking the worst and actually building the alternative? Who has to close it, and where, outside of Congress?

We are already experiencing climate catastrophe and if we stay on our current trajectory it will only get worse and worse. We are already experiencing historic inequality, and if we stay on our current trajectory it will only get worse and worse. The same is true for our health, education, housing and all the other necessities of life.

Even if we block new Trump depredations, we will face an American era similar to Russia’s “Yeltsin Era” following the fall of the Soviet Union, when the legal, educational, healthcare, manufacturing and other basic systems went into unending decline — marked, for example, by a six-year drop in male life expectancy.

To change that will take the kind of transformative reconstruction that was envisioned by the Green New Deal. But because conditions have changed and deteriorated so much, we need to update that to what I call a “Green New Deal 2.0”.

From the beginning, the Green New Deal was a convergence of progressives inside the political system and social movements based in civil society.

The defeat of Trumpism in the 2026 midterm elections was similarly a convergence of outside-the-system forces like the No Kings coalition and inside-the-system Democrats who cared about Gaza, war, climate, the Constitution and the wellbeing of ordinary people. Plus, the decision by ordinary people that they had to step forward, whether it was by protecting their immigrant neighbours against ICE [Immigration and Customs Enforcement] or in voting en masse against Republicans. Those same forces need to take the lead in developing the alternative — the “Green New Deal 2.0”.

The report argues the technology is already cheaper and winning. So why isn’t the US just switching? Who is holding it back, and what does the “fossil fuel island” cost ordinary people?

While the rest of the world is racing to switch to fossil-free greentech energy production and consumption, the US is going in the opposite direction. This is due to two main factors.

The first is the power of the fossil fuel industry.

Even under Joe Biden’s “Build Back Better” program, supposedly “green” policies like carbon capture and hydrogen were coined into profits for fossil fuel developers while the US underwent its largest ever expansion of natural gas.

The second is a nationalist drive to use energy policy for geopolitical power.

The Biden administration put high tariffs on cheap Chinese solar and EV imports that could have revolutionised American energy use. The Trump administration put both of these dynamics on steroids. It has tried to destroy Greentech energy initiatives not only in the US but worldwide. And it has provided vast subsidies for fossil fuel expansion.

But this is a fool’s strategy. You can see the actual results for ordinary Americans in the price of gasoline, heating oil, diesel fuel and electricity. And you can see the long-term effects of fossil fuel domination in the devastating heat waves, floods, wildfires and other products of climate change.
